airport-c1y-budget.title: 格安航空会社について

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: Budget airlines are definitely cheap, but doesn't the service quality feel worse than it used to be?

lines.speaker: 재훈
lines.en: I actually think of it as a rational trade-off. You only pay for what you need.

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: Still, they keep shrinking seat pitch and baggage fees keep climbing. Doesn't the consumer end up losing out?

lines.speaker: 재훈
lines.en: I'd call it expanded choice rather than a loss. For a light traveler with no baggage, it's actually a benefit.

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: In theory, sure, but in practice there are so many hidden fees that sometimes when you compare it later there's not much difference from a full-service carrier.

lines.speaker: 재훈
lines.en: I'll grant you that. Transparency is an area where regulation probably needs to be tightened.

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: There's also the concern that safety management and maintenance cycles get neglected because of cost-cutting pressure.

lines.speaker: 재훈
lines.en: On that point, as long as they pass aviation authority certification, the same legal standards apply, so I think that fear is unfounded.

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: In the end it's a matter of weighing it against your own travel purpose. Since I'm traveling light this time, I think I'll give one a try.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I'd like to hear the company's position on last week's forced passenger removal incident.

lines.speaker: 임원
lines.en: First, I offer my deepest apologies to that passenger and everyone who was present. We acknowledge our response fell short.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: 'Fell short' seems like an understatement. There's criticism that the rules were interpreted arbitrarily.

lines.speaker: 임원
lines.en: The rule itself existed, but in the frontline staff's discretionary judgment, sufficient consideration for the passenger wasn't reflected.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So what are the preventive measures going forward? I hope this isn't just an apology in words.

lines.speaker: 임원
lines.en: We plan to retrain all staff on passenger handling, and to substantially raise the compensation cap for voluntary bumping in overbooking situations.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: It's questionable whether raising compensation is a fundamental fix. Is there no plan to reconsider the overbooking practice itself?

lines.speaker: 임원
lines.en: Overbooking is tied to the profit structure across the whole industry, so immediate abolition is difficult, but we'll improve algorithm accuracy to lower how often it occurs.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: It seems it will take considerable time to restore the trust lost in this incident.

lines.speaker: 임원
lines.en: We take that very seriously as well. I believe we have no choice but to prove it through our actions.

airport-c1y-loyalty.title: マイルプログラムの改悪

lines.speaker: 민호
lines.en: Did you see the mileage program overhaul? The miles needed per seat almost doubled.

lines.speaker: 은영
lines.en: I saw it. Ten-plus years of accumulation effectively cut in half overnight — no wonder people feel betrayed.

lines.speaker: 민호
lines.en: From the airline's perspective they'll say it's adjusting to demand given limited seat supply, but I wonder if they even consider consumer trust.

lines.speaker: 은영
lines.en: On top of that, the notice period was short. They should've at least given existing members a grace period.

lines.speaker: 민호
lines.en: What's more bitter is that this is a trend other airlines will follow too. It's not like the industry colluded, but they all overhaul around the same time.

lines.speaker: 은영
lines.en: So I think we should stop thinking of miles as an asset and treat them more like a coupon whose value can be cut at any time.

lines.speaker: 민호
lines.en: Agreed. I'm going to change my strategy this time too — instead of pushing for a higher cabin class, I'll just redeem miles as soon as they accumulate.

lines.speaker: 은영
lines.en: That sounds like a wise choice. The conditions for maintaining elite status also keep getting stricter, so it feels less like a reward for loyalty and more like a burden now.

lines.speaker: 직원 A
lines.en: Did you hear the union is starting a slowdown this afternoon? Baggage handling speed is going to noticeably drop.

lines.speaker: 직원 B
lines.en: I heard. The wage increase proposal doesn't even keep up with inflation, so the frontline staff's frustration is no small thing.

lines.speaker: 직원 A
lines.en: Management keeps giving the excuse that air travel demand hasn't fully recovered yet, but that line doesn't seem to work anymore.

lines.speaker: 직원 B
lines.en: Demand has already surpassed pre-pandemic levels. They just keep leaving staffing understaffed, so we're the ones getting worn down.

lines.speaker: 직원 A
lines.en: I'm worried that if passenger inconvenience grows from this, public opinion won't be on our side either.

lines.speaker: 직원 B
lines.en: That's why the union chose gradual pressure instead of a full strike. They can't completely ignore public opinion either.

lines.speaker: 직원 A
lines.en: If negotiations aren't settled by next week, the situation will worsen — do you think management will finally take it seriously this time?

lines.speaker: 직원 B
lines.en: Well, last time too they only reached a deal after going right up to the brink. I doubt it'll be much different this time.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I've heard there's considerable backlash from nearby residents over this runway expansion plan. What specifically is the problem?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The biggest issue is noise. Even now, on days with early morning flights we lose sleep, and with the expansion, takeoffs and landings will nearly double.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: The airport authority has said it prepared soundproofing support and relocation compensation — do you think that's not enough?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The compensation amount is one issue, but our home, where our family has lived for generations, isn't something you can simply convert into money.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: The airport authority emphasizes the effect on local economic revitalization and job creation. What do you think about that aspect?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: More jobs is welcome, but I doubt whether those benefits actually reach our neighborhood, which directly bears the noise damage.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I've heard the residents' committee plans to demand a redo of the environmental impact assessment. How feasible do you think that is?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It won't be easy, but if we don't raise our voices this issue will clearly get quietly buried, so we plan to keep pushing to the end.

lines.speaker: 지우
lines.en: Another thirty-minute delay, apparently. Every time this happens, I end up thinking about the environmental impact of flying.

lines.speaker: 현석
lines.en: Right, there's actually research showing short-haul flights emit far more carbon than trains.

lines.speaker: 지우
lines.en: And yet because of price and time we end up choosing planes anyway, so it doesn't seem like something individual choice alone can solve.

lines.speaker: 현석
lines.en: Signing up for a carbon offset program is one option, but questions about its actual effectiveness keep being raised too.

lines.speaker: 지우
lines.en: In the end, I think it'll take airlines accelerating the adoption of sustainable aviation fuel and governments creating policy mechanisms like carbon taxes to fundamentally change things.

lines.speaker: 현석
lines.en: If such policies are adopted, ticket prices will rise, and I worry that travel might revert to being a privilege for a select few again.

lines.speaker: 지우
lines.en: I recognize that dilemma too. Still, wouldn't that be better than the current structure where nobody pays the environmental cost at all?

lines.speaker: 현석
lines.en: That makes sense. At the very least, let's try to prioritize direct flights starting with our next trip.

lines.speaker: 출입국 직원
lines.en: Have you filled out the overseas Korean re-entry declaration? I see you've been residing abroad for over five years.

lines.speaker: 귀국자
lines.en: Yes, I've filled it out. I heard the policy recently changed — is there anything that applies to me?

lines.speaker: 출입국 직원
lines.en: For people returning after long-term residence abroad, the conditions for the health insurance re-enrollment grace period have become stricter than before.

lines.speaker: 귀국자
lines.en: I see. Can I get the related documents here, or do I need to visit a separate agency?

lines.speaker: 출입국 직원
lines.en: I can give you the informational notice here, but the actual submission needs to be done directly at your district office.

lines.speaker: 귀국자
lines.en: May I also ask if anything has changed regarding taxes? I'm a bit worried about reporting overseas income.

lines.speaker: 출입국 직원
lines.en: Tax matters aren't within our jurisdiction, so it would be more accurate to inquire at the National Tax Service consultation window.

lines.speaker: 귀국자
lines.en: Understood. Coming back after so long, the procedures have changed a lot and feel unfamiliar. Thanks for the guidance.

lines.speaker: 출입국 직원
lines.en: Welcome back. If you have further questions, the airport information desk can also help, so keep that in mind.

lines.speaker: 정우
lines.en: Look at this long line. I doubt whether even making people take off their shoes actually does anything effective.

lines.speaker: 혜리
lines.en: That procedure started after the shoe bomb attempt. I think it also has a symbolic meaning.

lines.speaker: 정우
lines.en: Symbolic and actually addressing a real threat are different things. I wonder if this is what's called security theater.

lines.speaker: 혜리
lines.en: That's not entirely wrong, but doesn't it still serve the positive function of giving passengers psychological reassurance?

lines.speaker: 정우
lines.en: I think pouring resources into low-probability scenarios for the sake of psychological reassurance, at the expense of more realistic risks, is inefficient.

lines.speaker: 혜리
lines.en: Then what approach do you think would be more efficient? Random checks, or behavioral analysis?

lines.speaker: 정우
lines.en: Personally I think strengthening data-driven risk assessment is better than checking everyone the same way.

lines.speaker: 혜리
lines.en: But that risks sliding into racial or nationality profiling. How would you address that side effect?

lines.speaker: 정우
lines.en: That's a fair point. There's no perfect solution, but at the very least I think we should reconsider maintaining practices without verifying their effectiveness.

airport-c1y-liminal.title: 空港の独特な空間について

lines.speaker: 여행자 A
lines.en: Excuse me, but isn't this place, the airport, kind of strange? It feels like it belongs nowhere.

lines.speaker: 여행자 B
lines.en: I've always felt that way too. The moment you pass through departure inspection, you're neither still in this country nor yet gone.

lines.speaker: 여행자 A
lines.en: Maybe that's why people seem to act differently here. They start conversations with strangers more easily too.

lines.speaker: 여행자 B
lines.en: Maybe it's because it's a space where the rules of daily life are temporarily suspended. You know you'll probably never meet again.

lines.speaker: 여행자 A
lines.en: I heard anthropologists call this kind of space a 'liminal space' — meaning an in-between zone caught between rites of passage.

lines.speaker: 여행자 B
lines.en: Now that you mention it, that's really true. While I'm here, I feel like neither my past self nor the self I'll be at the destination.

lines.speaker: 여행자 A
lines.en: That uncertainty is a little unsettling, but at the same time it seems to give a strange sense of freedom.

lines.speaker: 여행자 B
lines.en: Right. Maybe that's exactly why people find it easier to open up to strangers at airports.

airport-c2y-atc.title: 航空管制官の労働交渉

lines.speaker: 노조 대표
lines.en: We've already warned about the controller staffing shortage on multiple occasions. Without a staffing increase in this negotiation, an agreement is impossible.

lines.speaker: 당국 대표
lines.en: Given the budget allocation process, immediate hiring is realistically difficult. However, a phased expansion plan could be considered.

lines.speaker: 노조 대표
lines.en: We've already experienced how 'phased' ends up meaning delays of several years. Frontline controllers are already burned out from overtime.

lines.speaker: 당국 대표
lines.en: I understand that concern, but the reality is that newly hired staff need at least two years of training before they can reach independent controller status.

lines.speaker: 노조 대표
lines.en: That's exactly why we need to start right now. A longer training period should be a reason to hurry, not a reason to delay the decision.

lines.speaker: 당국 대표
lines.en: That's a fair point. However, we'll likely need to link the adjustment of controller working-hour caps with the staffing scale to persuade the budget authorities.

lines.speaker: 노조 대표
lines.en: We agree to adjusting working-hour caps, but that must not be exploited as a pretext for delaying staffing. Please put a deadline in writing.

lines.speaker: 당국 대표
lines.en: Specifying a concrete deadline requires higher-level approval, so I can't give an immediate answer here, but I'll try to reflect it as much as possible.

lines.speaker: 노조 대표
lines.en: The word 'try' alone won't persuade our members. Please come to the next negotiation with a concrete draft deadline prepared.

airport-c2y-hub.title: Debating whether the airport should be a mega-hub

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: The government has put forward a blueprint to grow this airport into a Northeast Asian hub, but I think the strategy itself is anachronistic.

lines.speaker: 학자
lines.en: I find that hard to agree with. If we fail to capture transfer demand, we'll effectively hand over all the added value of our aviation industry to neighboring hub airports.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: Before discussing added value, shouldn't we first weigh the environmental cost and community conflict that large-scale expansion will bring?

lines.speaker: 학자
lines.en: Of course those costs shouldn't be overlooked, but for a fair discussion we must also factor in the long-term loss of jobs and tourism revenue if hub status is lost.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: I'd point out that the assumption of long-term loss itself rests on the uncertain premise of aviation demand forecasting. Demand patterns have fundamentally shifted since the pandemic.

lines.speaker: 학자
lines.en: It's true the pattern has changed, but there are also indicators showing cargo transport and business demand have not just recovered but are growing.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: In the end, I think this debate is simply a rehash of the old tension between growth-at-all-costs thinking and sustainability.

lines.speaker: 학자
lines.en: Even granting that tension, I believe policy decisions ultimately need to be based on concrete figures and scenario analysis, not reduced to an ideological clash.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: I agree on that point. But we also need to verify who produces those figures and whose interests are reflected in them.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: It seems we've now entered an era where you can board with just facial recognition, no passport needed. Today we'll examine the light and shadow of this biometric boarding system.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: In terms of speed, it's certainly innovative. There are statistics showing gate transit time dropped to a third of what it used to be.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: However, concerns over privacy protection are no small matter either. Isn't the key question how far this data could be used?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Right. Airlines say it's used only for boarding purposes, but the reality is there's a lack of transparent disclosure about third-party sharing or long-term retention.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Some critics also raise the point that such technology, under the guise of convenience, could become a stepping stone to legitimizing a surveillance society.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: I don't think that criticism is mere exaggeration. We can't rule out the possibility that biometric authentication, starting in the controlled space of the airport, could spread to other public domains.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So how should consumers be guaranteed the right to opt out of this technology?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: At the very least, I believe there needs to be an explicitly guaranteed alternative procedure that allows boarding within the same waiting time even if you opt out of biometric authentication.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: In the end, how to strike a balance between technological convenience and individual self-determination will be the challenge going forward.

airport-c2y-slots.title: Debating the fairness of slot allocation

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: Maintaining slot allocation at congested airports through the current customary system is, from a market efficiency standpoint, a clear distortion.

lines.speaker: 항공사 관계자
lines.en: Rather than calling it a distortion, shouldn't we see it as a minimal safeguard for balancing between new entrants and incumbent carriers?

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: How would you explain the side effect that, under the name of a safeguard, the vested interests of major carriers who already secured slots become entrenched?

lines.speaker: 항공사 관계자
lines.en: If we switch to an auction system, there's a risk that only well-capitalized airlines survive, and low-profit routes like regional connections could disappear entirely.

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: Even granting that risk, couldn't we secure both market efficiency and public interest simultaneously by pairing it with separate subsidies or mandatory allocation for public-service routes?

lines.speaker: 항공사 관계자
lines.en: That sounds plausible in theory, but at the actual policy design stage, endless lobbying and conflict will arise over where exactly to draw that line.

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: I also think it's hard to justify simply leaving the current inefficient system in place just because political conflict is anticipated.

lines.speaker: 항공사 관계자
lines.en: In the end, rather than sweeping reform, I think a gradual approach — piloting an auction system on a portion of slots first to accumulate data — might be more realistic.

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: I agree with a gradual approach, but unless clear evaluation metrics and an end date are fixed for the pilot program, there's a risk it will fizzle out again.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: Statistics show staff turnover has surged since airport security work was outsourced to private contractors. How do you diagnose this?

lines.speaker: 노동 연구자
lines.en: This is the textbook structure where low-bid competition among contractors ultimately leads to wage pressure, which then manifests as worsening working conditions and rising turnover.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: So do you see it as a flawed design from the outset to entrust a task directly tied to national security, like security screening, to the private sector at all?

lines.speaker: 노동 연구자
lines.en: Rather than outright rejecting private outsourcing itself, I think the system needs to be reformed so that evaluation criteria reflect skill and tenure rather than just the lowest bid.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: How to objectively measure skill would itself seem to become a point of contention.

lines.speaker: 노동 연구자
lines.en: There's no perfect metric, but at the very least I think we could start by reflecting quantitative data such as past incident history or retraining completion rates.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: Some argue that security work should be fully reintegrated into the public sector. What's your view on that?

lines.speaker: 노동 연구자
lines.en: It's a difficult plan to realize in the short term, both financially and administratively, but I think it's well worth setting as a long-term goal.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: In the end, this issue too comes down to where society places its priority between cost reduction and the value of public safety.

airport-c2y-noise.title: Op-ed style commentary on night flight curfews

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: The debate over relaxing night flight curfews has flared up again. Today we'll examine this issue from multiple angles.

lines.speaker: 패널
lines.en: From the logistics industry's standpoint, night cargo transport that leverages time zone differences is central to international competitiveness. Keeping the curfew could destabilize the airport's position as a cargo hub.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: On the other hand, wouldn't this arrive for nearby residents as a much more direct and immediate harm — an infringement of their right to sleep?

lines.speaker: 패널
lines.en: I have no intention of disputing that point. However, I think a compromise worth considering is piloting a limited relaxation on the condition that noise-reducing aircraft are introduced.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: Do you consider the technical solution of noise-reducing aircraft to be sufficiently proven to justify policy relaxation?

lines.speaker: 패널
lines.en: It's not a complete solution, but empirical data has already accumulated showing perceived noise is substantially reduced compared to older aircraft models.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: Even so, for residents, the gap between reduced noise and no noise at all wouldn't be easy to accept.

lines.speaker: 패널
lines.en: That's why I believe this issue can't be resolved purely through technical or economic logic, and ultimately a social consensus process involving compensation and trust-building must proceed in parallel.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: So in the end, rather than a binary between relaxation and restriction, the key is how we design the middle ground between them.

lines.speaker: 정치인
lines.en: If we sell airport equity to private capital, I believe it will resolve the chronic budget deficit and also improve operational efficiency.

lines.speaker: 시민단체 대표
lines.en: Hasn't 'efficiency' already been reported to translate into fee hikes and reduced services in multiple overseas cases?

lines.speaker: 정치인
lines.en: Of course that side effect can be a concern, but I believe it's a problem that can be prevented by specifying fee caps and minimum service standards in the sale contract.

lines.speaker: 시민단체 대표
lines.en: No matter how elaborate the contract clauses are, it's undeniable that once you hand a critical national infrastructure to profit-seeking private entities, you lose a considerable degree of control.

lines.speaker: 정치인
lines.en: The expression 'loss of control' seems somewhat exaggerated. It's an equity sale, not a full transfer of management rights.

lines.speaker: 시민단체 대표
lines.en: We've already witnessed, in multiple industries, cases where actual decision-making power shifts to private majority shareholders based on the equity structure.

lines.speaker: 정치인
lines.en: Leaving the budget deficit unaddressed is also ultimately a problem that must be plugged with taxpayer money — what alternative do you propose?

lines.speaker: 시민단체 대표
lines.en: Rather than privatization, I believe there's ample room to improve the revenue structure by diversifying non-core ancillary businesses within a public operating framework.

lines.speaker: 정치인
lines.en: Whether that approach can generate a scale sufficient to offset the deficit in the short term is still a question in my mind.

lines.speaker: 작가
lines.en: When I listen carefully to the language of airport announcements, there are times I feel that the politeness embedded in it actually produces a kind of alienation.

lines.speaker: 청자
lines.en: That's an interesting perspective. I actually felt those formulaic expressions gave a sense of stability.

lines.speaker: 작가
lines.en: While giving that stability, isn't there also a sense that each passenger's individual story gets erased, and everyone is reduced to an anonymous presence within the same procedure?

lines.speaker: 청자
lines.en: Looking at it that way, there does seem to be a kind of bureaucratic rhythm even in a single sentence like 'We will now begin boarding.'

lines.speaker: 작가
lines.en: I often quote that rhythm in my novels. I want to show the point where an individual's narrative collides with institutional language.

lines.speaker: 청자
lines.en: On the other hand though, I wonder if that impersonal language is actually essential in crisis situations. There are moments when emotion shouldn't factor in.

lines.speaker: 작가
lines.en: That's a fair point. That's why, rather than criticizing this language, I want to make that very duality the subject matter of my writing.

lines.speaker: 청자
lines.en: Do you have plans to write a story set at an airport for your next novel?

lines.speaker: 작가
lines.en: Yes, actually I'm working on the idea right now. I want to interweave the different timelines of characters who happen to cross paths in front of a boarding gate.

airport-c2y-drones.title: Debate over drone incursions grounding flights

lines.speaker: 보도자
lines.en: Last night the runway was closed for over three hours because of a drone spotted in the nearby airspace. We'll examine why this keeps recurring.

lines.speaker: 보안 전문가
lines.en: The current response system is designed mainly around detection, and actual neutralization measures are held back due to insufficient legal grounds.

lines.speaker: 보도자
lines.en: By neutralization, do you mean physical measures like shooting it down? Wouldn't that actually be more dangerous?

lines.speaker: 보안 전문가
lines.en: It's usually signal jamming or signal hijacking rather than physical shootdown. But that too is fairly strictly regulated because of the potential impact on civilian communication networks.

lines.speaker: 보도자
lines.en: So are you saying that fundamentally we're left with only after-the-fact responses like identifying and punishing the drone owner?

lines.speaker: 보안 전문가
lines.en: The problem is that after-the-fact response alone can't prevent recurrence. From a preventive standpoint, I think we need mandatory drone registration and real-time location sharing within the airport's radius.

lines.speaker: 보도자
lines.en: Wouldn't such a system have little binding power over a genuinely malicious operator anyway? They could just fly it secretly without registering in the first place.

lines.speaker: 보안 전문가
lines.en: That's correct. That's exactly why I'm saying we need a dual strategy of building a dense detection sensor network alongside the registration system.

lines.speaker: 보도자
lines.en: So in the end, unless technology and institutions keep pace together, these kinds of delay incidents are bound to continue.

lines.speaker: 민주
lines.en: Did you see the carbon offset option at check-in? Every airline seems to have it now.

lines.speaker: 태석
lines.en: I saw it but didn't pay. Honestly I don't trust where that money actually goes.

lines.speaker: 민주
lines.en: They say it goes to tree planting or renewable energy projects — why don't you trust it?

lines.speaker: 태석
lines.en: There have been several reported cases of trees that were already going to be planted anyway getting rebranded as their offset results. The so-called 'additionality' problem.

lines.speaker: 민주
lines.en: I've heard of that too. But isn't doing something better than nothing at all?

lines.speaker: 태석
lines.en: It could actually backfire. Once you pay and the guilt disappears, the pressure to actually reduce air travel demand weakens.

lines.speaker: 민주
lines.en: So what's the alternative then? It's not like we can just stop flying entirely.

lines.speaker: 태석
lines.en: I think it's better to choose offset programs certified by third-party verification bodies, or donate directly to a vetted environmental group instead of through the airline.

lines.speaker: 민주
lines.en: So in the end the consumer has to verify everything themselves. That's exhausting.

airport-c1z-biophilic.title: An airport designer on biophilic trends

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Recent terminals even have indoor trees and waterfalls — why has this design trend emerged?

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: It's because of research showing that travelers' stress levels at airports are quite high. It's been demonstrated that natural elements lower those numbers.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So it's not just for looks, it's aimed at a psychological effect.

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: Exactly. From skylights to indoor plants, we call this 'biophilic design,' and it has the effect of making waiting time feel shorter than it actually is.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: But maintenance costs must be considerable. Doesn't that cost ultimately get reflected in usage fees?

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: The initial investment is large, but many analyses show it's offset in the long run because as passenger dwell time increases, retail revenue rises along with it.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So it's a design where aesthetics and commercial interest are intertwined.

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: I can't deny that. But if the result is that passengers actually board their flight less anxious and less exhausted, I think it's meaningful design.

lines.speaker: 교수A
lines.en: The 'flight shame' movement started in Europe and has spread to Korea — do you think it's actually reducing air travel demand?

lines.speaker: 교수B
lines.en: There are statistics showing a noticeable drop in short-haul route usage in some countries. But we need to separate whether that's due to guilt or because rail alternatives improved.

lines.speaker: 교수A
lines.en: I'm skeptical of the approach itself of appealing to individual moral choice. Most aviation emissions come from cargo or business demand, not personal leisure travel.

lines.speaker: 교수B
lines.en: That's statistically debatable. There's also IATA data showing that international passenger demand is the main driver of the emissions increase.

lines.speaker: 교수A
lines.en: Even if that's true, I think discourse that places guilt on the individual has the side effect of obscuring structural issues — like fuel tax exemptions or subsidies.

lines.speaker: 교수B
lines.en: I agree. Still, I don't think it's a completely meaningless movement, since shifting public awareness eventually translates into policy pressure.

lines.speaker: 교수A
lines.en: So the conclusion is that individual choice and institutional reform need to go hand in hand.

lines.speaker: 교수B
lines.en: Right, I don't think either one alone can solve the emissions problem.

airport-c1z-pilotunion.title: Pilots' union and management negotiation snippet

lines.speaker: 노조대표
lines.en: The core demand we're making in this negotiation is expanding the minimum rest time to prevent fatigue buildup.

lines.speaker: 인사임원
lines.en: Extending rest time reduces the number of flights operated, and that's a demand that's impossible without additional hiring.

lines.speaker: 노조대표
lines.en: Then just hire more people. Right now captains' average monthly flight hours are close to the legal upper limit.

lines.speaker: 인사임원
lines.en: An increase in labor costs will inevitably lead to higher ticket prices. We have to consider the burden on consumers too.

lines.speaker: 노조대표
lines.en: I'd like to ask which is the more serious problem — a fatigued pilot sitting in the cockpit, or ticket prices rising by a few thousand won.

lines.speaker: 인사임원
lines.en: We're not dismissing safety. It's just that we also need to consider the sustainability of the business.

lines.speaker: 노조대표
lines.en: We've presented simulation data as evidence. We'd like to receive a concrete proposal within this week.

lines.speaker: 인사임원
lines.en: We'll review it and bring a revised proposal to the next negotiation session.

airport-c1z-baggagescandal.title: A journalist exposing a baggage-handling scandal

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: We've obtained internal documents showing your baggage damage rate is three times the industry average. How do you explain this?

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: I think we first need to verify the source and sampling period of that document. It differs considerably from our official statistics.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I can't disclose the source, but it's data covering damage reports filed over the past six months. There was also a tip suggesting statistics were underreported.

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: We accept and process every reported case according to regulations. The claim of underreporting hasn't been verified.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Then are you willing to undergo public verification through an internal audit?

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: Whether to disclose audit results is a matter that needs to be discussed with the legal team. I can't give a definite answer here right now.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: By when will that discussion be concluded? Consumers want an answer right now.

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: We'll put together an official position within this week and get back to you.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I will make sure that response goes on the record.

lines.speaker: 연구원A
lines.en: Our government just signed a visa-waiver agreement with that country. Isn't it positive from a tourism standpoint?

lines.speaker: 연구원B
lines.en: In terms of numbers, sure. But there's criticism that it's an asymmetric agreement benefiting only our citizens relative to the other country's own, which violates the principle of reciprocity.

lines.speaker: 연구원A
lines.en: Insisting on full reciprocity often makes it hard to even reach an agreement in the first place. Wouldn't a phased approach be more realistic?

lines.speaker: 연구원B
lines.en: The problem is that 'phased' often turns into an indefinite postponement in practice. Domestic public opinion is also critical over the fairness issue.

lines.speaker: 연구원A
lines.en: Still, there's also a view that diplomatically, preemptive openness can be a card that increases bargaining power.

lines.speaker: 연구원B
lines.en: We need to verify whether that card has actually drawn out reciprocal measures from the other country. Looking at past cases, many ended up fizzling out.

lines.speaker: 연구원A
lines.en: So in the end we need a clause that creates quantitative evaluation metrics and mandates a review after a set period.

lines.speaker: 연구원B
lines.en: Right, without such a safeguard, there's a high risk these agreements amount to nothing more than political symbolism.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: This time I bought a ticket from Incheon connecting through Tokyo to Seoul, but I'm getting off at Tokyo and not taking the Seoul leg. It was cheaper that way.

lines.speaker: 은서
lines.en: That's 'hidden city ticketing,' right? I've heard of it — isn't that a violation of the airline's terms?

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: It does violate the terms, but I think it's morally fine since it's a choice made within the price the consumer legitimately paid.

lines.speaker: 은서
lines.en: But that seat can end up meaning another passenger on the waitlist can't get on. It's not entirely harmless.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: That's a problem caused by the airline habitually overbooking — I don't think it's fair to blame it on my individual choice.

lines.speaker: 은서
lines.en: Not being able to check baggage is also a downside. And if you get caught, your mileage account could get suspended.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Taking on that risk is ultimately my own responsibility, so I factor that in when I do it.

lines.speaker: 은서
lines.en: I understand the logic, but personally the risk if I got caught feels too big, so I don't think I'd do it.

airport-c1z-chaplain.title: An airport chaplain reflecting on grief and farewells

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: A chaplain stationed at the airport seems like an unusual job. What kind of people do you mostly meet?

lines.speaker: 목사
lines.en: People who suddenly have anxiety attacks before a long flight, people rushing to leave the country after hearing of a family member's death — it's really varied.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: It feels like a space where grief becomes concentrated. Is there a particular moment that stays with you?

lines.speaker: 목사
lines.en: There was a person who collapsed in front of the gate after hearing news of their father's death. All I could do was sit beside them and hold their hand, but later they sent me a letter.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Why do you think a place like the airport particularly amplifies emotions like that?

lines.speaker: 목사
lines.en: Because it's the one place where farewells and reunions happen simultaneously. The fact that time is short and there's uncertainty about when you'll meet again also matters a lot.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I'm curious whether you also help people of different religions.

lines.speaker: 목사
lines.en: Of course. What I do isn't to preach a particular doctrine, but simply to be present beside someone in that moment.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: We've reached an era where boarding can be completed through facial recognition at the airport — what are the privacy issues with this?

lines.speaker: 윤리학자
lines.en: The biggest problem is that it's hard for passengers to know exactly how long that biometric data is stored and who it's shared with.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Airlines explain it's for security and convenience — is that justification alone sufficient?

lines.speaker: 윤리학자
lines.en: The justification itself is valid. The problem is that the consent process tends to become a mere formality in the name of convenience and safety.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Is the option to opt out of facial recognition actually guaranteed in practice?

lines.speaker: 윤리학자
lines.en: Theoretically it exists, but if you opt out the line becomes much longer and the process more cumbersome, so it effectively becomes a pressure in many cases.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: What institutional supplements do you think are needed?

lines.speaker: 윤리학자
lines.en: I think we need to codify the deletion timeline for collected data, and have an independent body that regularly audits whether it's shared with third parties.

airport-c2z-hubidentity.title: A historian on how an airport shaped a city

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: You've said the airport played a decisive role in this city gaining its current international standing — what specifically was the turning point?

lines.speaker: 역사학자
lines.en: When regular international routes began service in the late 1960s, the city started being reorganized from a mere regional hub into a gateway for international logistics and human exchange.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Did the citizens at the time embrace that change entirely positively?

lines.speaker: 역사학자
lines.en: Not entirely. The airport expansion required entire neighboring villages to relocate, and there was considerable backlash over noise pollution. Behind every advance, there was always a sacrifice.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Even so, you see the city's identity itself as ultimately having been reconstructed around that airport.

lines.speaker: 역사학자
lines.en: Yes, tourism, trade, and even the citizens' own self-perception came to align with the narrative of being 'a city connected to the world.' The airport became more than mere infrastructure — it became the city's symbol.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Watching similar debates recur around new airport construction these days, it feels like history repeating itself.

lines.speaker: 역사학자
lines.en: That's a precise observation. Though this time there's a difference in that environmental impact assessments and resident participation procedures have become far more sophisticated than back then.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: In the end, finding balance between development and preservation, convenience and sacrifice, seems to be a city's eternal task.

airport-c2z-nightcurfew.title: Residents and an official debating runway noise

lines.speaker: 주민대표
lines.en: Our village is right under the runway, and there are countless nights we lose sleep to takeoff and landing noise. Soundproof window support alone isn't enough.

lines.speaker: 공항관계자
lines.en: We've already reduced late-night flight operations by 15 percent and introduced noise abatement procedures. Complete control is realistically difficult due to cargo and passenger demand.

lines.speaker: 주민대표
lines.en: Do you think 15 percent is noticeable? What we're demanding is a complete flight ban from midnight to 5am.

lines.speaker: 공항관계자
lines.en: That time slot is when over half of cargo routes are concentrated. A total ban would strike the entire logistics industry.

lines.speaker: 주민대표
lines.en: Isn't there room to shift cargo routes to other time slots? Are you saying logistics efficiency takes priority over people's right to health?

lines.speaker: 공항관계자
lines.en: That's not what I mean. I'm just saying a full adjustment involves slot reallocation and renegotiating contracts with logistics companies, which takes time.

lines.speaker: 주민대표
lines.en: We've been hearing the same answer for ten years now. This time we want a concrete implementation schedule in writing.

lines.speaker: 공항관계자
lines.en: We'll submit a phased reduction plan in writing at next month's regional consultative committee meeting.

lines.speaker: 주민대표
lines.en: I hope it's honored this time. We have no more room left to give in either.

lines.speaker: 분석가A
lines.en: There's talk that some airlines barely use their allocated slots, only meet the formal minimum operation requirement, and then quietly transfer the remaining time slots.

lines.speaker: 분석가B
lines.en: The so-called 'ghost flights.' There really are flight numbers that get flown almost empty of passengers and cargo, purely to hold onto the slot.

lines.speaker: 분석가A
lines.en: That's exploiting a loophole in the regulations. Since they just need to meet the slot usage threshold, isn't this a serious fairness issue?

lines.speaker: 분석가B
lines.en: Very serious. Especially considering carbon emissions, the practice of flying empty planes can't be justified environmentally either.

lines.speaker: 분석가A
lines.en: I've heard regulatory authorities are moving toward either raising the usage threshold or tightening the exception approval process.

lines.speaker: 분석가B
lines.en: But there's also a counterargument that if the threshold is made too strict, it could actually raise entry barriers for new airlines or small routes.

lines.speaker: 분석가A
lines.en: So in the end, a dual standard is needed that blocks major carriers' loophole exploitation while still protecting new entrants.

lines.speaker: 분석가B
lines.en: Easy to say, but where exactly to draw that line is the core challenge in designing the regulation.

lines.speaker: 분석가A
lines.en: It seems like an issue we'll need to keep watching for the time being.

airport-c2z-antitrafficking.title: Border officer training on trafficking indicators

lines.speaker: 신입직원
lines.en: Senior, distinguishing suspected trafficking indicators seems far harder than I expected. On the surface it can look just like a family trip.

lines.speaker: 선배직원
lines.en: Right, that's why you can't judge based on a single indicator alone. You have to weigh multiple circumstances together — like a companion trying to answer on someone's behalf, or a child reacting as if seeing their passport for the first time.

lines.speaker: 신입직원
lines.en: But asking those questions could end up offending a family that actually has no issue at all. How do you strike that balance?

lines.speaker: 선배직원
lines.en: The manner of asking matters. The key is asking the same question naturally to multiple people, as if it's a routine part of the process, rather than interrogating.

lines.speaker: 신입직원
lines.en: If suspicion turns into conviction, what's the next procedure?

lines.speaker: 선배직원
lines.en: The principle isn't immediate arrest — you guide them to a separate space, arrange dedicated counseling staff and an interpreter, and start with victim protection procedures first.

lines.speaker: 신입직원
lines.en: So until confirmed as a victim, the approach treats them as someone to protect, not a potential criminal.

lines.speaker: 선배직원
lines.en: That's the single most important principle in this job. Because the cost of getting the judgment wrong is far too great.

airport-c2z-lostgeneration.title: A retired flight attendant reflecting on the golden age

lines.speaker: 후배
lines.en: You've worked at the airline since its early days — what do you feel is the biggest difference between then and now?

lines.speaker: 은퇴승무원
lines.en: Back then, the flight itself was a special occasion. Passengers boarded in formal attire, and it was a point of pride for crew to provide formal, dignified service.

lines.speaker: 후배
lines.en: Now that it's become so mass-market, a lot of that specialness must have disappeared.

lines.speaker: 은퇴승무원
lines.en: Mass-market access itself isn't a bad thing. The problem is that the essence of the service has shifted entirely from 'hospitality' to 'efficiency.' Passenger numbers grew while staffing actually decreased.

lines.speaker: 후배
lines.en: So today's crew are effectively working under far harder conditions than back then.

lines.speaker: 은퇴승무원
lines.en: Both physically and in terms of emotional labor, yes. But I don't want to romanticize that era unconditionally either — discriminatory regulations against female flight attendants were severe back then too.

lines.speaker: 후배
lines.en: Looking at it that way, it's not something that can simply be divided into 'better' or 'worse.'

lines.speaker: 은퇴승무원
lines.en: Exactly. Something was gained and something was lost. But my one wish is that the attitude of treating passengers as full human beings holds true no matter how the era changes.

lines.speaker: 후배
lines.en: Thank you for those words. I'll keep that mindset in mind as I work too.

lines.speaker: 연구자A
lines.en: Seeing this airport get jam-packed to a standstill every holiday, it seems like a ticket home means more than mere transportation for migrants.

lines.speaker: 연구자B
lines.en: Right. I call it a 'ritual of identity reaffirmation' — and the longer someone has been away from their home country, the heavier that symbolic weight tends to become.

lines.speaker: 연구자A
lines.en: But there's also a considerable class of migrant workers who can only afford to go every other year, or give it up entirely, because of airfare costs. Does the same logic apply to them?

lines.speaker: 연구자B
lines.en: It applies even more strongly. The sense of loss or guilt felt in a year they can't go becomes a driving force that makes the next visit feel more desperate.

lines.speaker: 연구자A
lines.en: Then could we say the expansion of budget airlines has substantively contributed to securing this group's mobility rights?

lines.speaker: 연구자B
lines.en: Partially. But budget airlines generally don't offer direct routes, so there's a limitation in that a different form of cost — time cost — arises instead.

lines.speaker: 연구자A
lines.en: So even as economic accessibility improves, a barrier still remains for people who don't have the luxury of time.

lines.speaker: 연구자B
lines.en: Right, I think fully guaranteeing the right to mobility requires discussing not just cost but labor conditions as well.

lines.speaker: 연구자A
lines.en: We should dig into that part more in our next research then.

lines.speaker: 환경단체
lines.en: This runway's vicinity overlaps with a migratory bird route, and the approach of destroying the habitat itself in the name of preventing bird strikes needs to be reconsidered.

lines.speaker: 공항안전팀
lines.en: We're not trying to eliminate the habitat either. But if we don't reduce bird density within the runway radius, there's a real risk it leads to an actual accident.

lines.speaker: 환경단체
lines.en: There are non-lethal methods like sonic deterrents or falconry — why is habitat landfilling being considered as an extreme first measure?

lines.speaker: 공항안전팀
lines.en: We're already running non-lethal methods in parallel. But our data confirms their effectiveness drops significantly during breeding season.

lines.speaker: 환경단체
lines.en: Even so, if you destroy the habitat, aren't you just shifting the risk — birds displaced to another area will collide with a different flight path instead?

lines.speaker: 공항안전팀
lines.en: That's a fair point. That's why we're also reviewing a plan to create alternative wetlands that disperse habitat density, rather than complete landfilling.

lines.speaker: 환경단체
lines.en: Whether that alternative wetland creation will actually be a valid alternative for the birds needs to be verified through an independent ecological survey, I believe.

lines.speaker: 공항안전팀
lines.en: Agreed. Once the third-party institution's survey results come out next month, let's discuss again based on that.

lines.speaker: 환경단체
lines.en: We request that landfilling-related procedures be provisionally suspended until those results come out.

airport-c2z-fuelhedging.title: Finance analysts on jet fuel hedging strategy

lines.speaker: 분석가A
lines.en: Looking at last quarter's results, the fuel hedging strategy actually functioned as a loss factor. Is this a strategic failure, or just market volatility?

lines.speaker: 분석가B
lines.en: I think both are intertwined. As oil prices fell more sharply than expected, the hedge contracts ended up locked into prices higher than the market rate.

lines.speaker: 분석가A
lines.en: Then wasn't setting the hedge ratio that high in the first place itself a misjudgment?

lines.speaker: 분석가B
lines.en: From a risk management standpoint, it was a rational choice. It's insurance-like protection against a scenario of sharp oil price spikes, so criticizing it purely based on the outcome could be hindsight bias.

lines.speaker: 분석가A
lines.en: I grant that, but wasn't there room to adjust the hedge ratio more flexibly according to market conditions?

lines.speaker: 분석가B
lines.en: Theoretically possible, but frequent adjustments can instead increase transaction costs and psychological noise, undermining the consistency of the long-term strategy.

lines.speaker: 분석가A
lines.en: In the end, this loss needs to be explained to investors not as short-term performance deterioration but as a long-term risk management cost.

lines.speaker: 분석가B
lines.en: Right. But we also need to keep in mind that if that explanation repeats every quarter, it loses persuasive power.

lines.speaker: 경제학자A
lines.en: There's a lot of consumer complaint about airfares showing different prices every time you search — is this simply reflecting supply and demand, or is it closer to price discrimination?

lines.speaker: 경제학자B
lines.en: Strictly speaking, it's both. Dynamic pricing based on seat occupancy is the baseline, but recently there are suspicions it also factors in search history or device information.

lines.speaker: 경제학자A
lines.en: If it's presenting different prices to different individuals, isn't that clearly discrimination? For the same seat, some people end up paying more.

lines.speaker: 경제학자B
lines.en: Legally, the term used is 'segmented pricing' rather than 'discrimination.' The problem is that the criteria for that segmentation aren't transparently disclosed.

lines.speaker: 경제학자A
lines.en: Then consumers searching in incognito mode or clearing cookies to lower prices becomes a kind of counter-strategy as well.

lines.speaker: 경제학자B
lines.en: Right. But the very fact that such tricks work is itself evidence of the system's opacity. The information asymmetry is working against consumers.

lines.speaker: 경제학자A
lines.en: Is there no room for regulators to intervene — mandating disclosure of the pricing algorithm, for instance?

lines.speaker: 경제학자B
lines.en: Discussions have begun in some countries, but progress is slow because of considerable pushback from airlines that it conflicts with trade secret protection.

lines.speaker: 경제학자A
lines.en: In the end, rather than full disclosure, a compromise banning at least the practice of factoring personally identifiable information into pricing seems more realistic.

lines.speaker: 경제학자B
lines.en: Yes, I think that's the most realistic middle ground achievable between consumer protection and a company's pricing autonomy.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Where are the luggage carts?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: They're over there next to the pillar.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Are they free?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, they're free.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Where do I weigh my bag?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please put it on that scale.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, got it.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's 15 kilos. That's fine.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'd like to print my boarding pass again.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please show me your passport.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Here it is.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, I'll print you a new one.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Where's the currency exchange?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's on this floor.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: ありがとうございます。

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You're welcome, have a good trip.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I need a wheelchair.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, please wait here.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: How long will it take?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: About 5 minutes.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'm traveling with my dog.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Do you have a carrier?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Yes, here it is.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Good. The size is fine.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: This bag has fragile items.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll put a fragile sticker on it.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: ありがとうございます。

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We'll handle it carefully.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Where's the lounge?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's on the third floor.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Do I need a ticket?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, please show your boarding pass.

lines.speaker: 승무원
lines.en: For the meal, we have chicken or fish.

lines.speaker: 승객
lines.en: I'll have the chicken, please.

lines.speaker: 승무원
lines.en: What would you like to drink?

lines.speaker: 승객
lines.en: Water, please.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I lost my boarding pass.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Do you have your passport?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Yes, here it is.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll make you a new one.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Where's the pickup point?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's exit number 1.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Is it far from here?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: No, it's close.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Where's the tax refund counter?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's counter 20 over there.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Is the line long?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's short right now.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Do you have a phone charger?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: There's one next to the chairs over there.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: ありがとうございます。

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You're welcome, feel free to use it.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Where's the elevator?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Go to the left.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, got it.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You'll see it right away.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'd like a luggage tag.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please write your name on the bag.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I wrote it here.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, the tag is attached.

airport-a2x-scale-heavy.title: Bag is over the weight limit

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Your bag is over 23 kilos.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: How much over is it?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's 3 kilos over.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'll take some things out of the bag.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you can take them out here.

airport-a2x-lounge-buy.title: Buying a day pass for the lounge

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'd like to buy a day pass for the lounge.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Will you pay by card?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Yes, I'll pay by card.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The price is 30,000 won.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, I'll pay.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Your child is flying alone, right?

lines.speaker: 학부모
lines.en: Yes, that's right.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please fill out this form.

lines.speaker: 학부모
lines.en: Who will take my child there?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Our staff will take her to the gate.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'd like to bring my cat into the cabin.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Did you apply when you booked?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Yes, I applied.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then I'll check the carrier.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Here it is.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: What's today's exchange rate?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's 1,300 won.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'll exchange 100 dollars.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: There's a small fee.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: That's fine, please exchange it.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Did the gate just change?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it changed to gate 35.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Is it far from here?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you'll need to walk a bit.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I should hurry then.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: My flight got canceled.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I see. I'll change you to the next flight.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: When does it leave?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It leaves at 3 p.m.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, I'll take that one.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: This bag needs special packaging.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Does that cost extra?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it costs about 5,000 won.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then please pack it.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, I'll do it now.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'm here to pick up a friend.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Do you have a sign with the name?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: No, I haven't made one yet.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The kiosk over there sells paper.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Thanks, I'll go check.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Can I borrow a portable charger?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, if you register a card, we'll lend one.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: When do I need to return it?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please return it before boarding.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Got it, thank you.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'd like to request a vegetarian meal.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: When are you flying?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Tomorrow at 10 a.m.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If you request now, it'll be ready.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Yes, please request it.

airport-a2x-lostpass-reissue.title: Reissuing a lost boarding pass at the gate

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I lost my boarding pass and can't find my gate.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please tell me your name and flight number.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Kim Minsu, flight KE201.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Found it. I'll print you a new one.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Thank you so much.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: My mother needs a wheelchair.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What time is her flight?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: 2 p.m.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please come back here an hour before.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, I'll do that.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Where do I return this cart?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You can leave it at the cart area over there.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Can I get my coin back?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it comes out automatically when you return it.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Got it, thank you.

airport-a2x-taxfree-form.title: Filling out a tax refund form

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: How do I fill out the refund form?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please write your passport number and card number.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Is this how I write it?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's right. Please sign it too.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: All done.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Your bag is 5 kilos over, so there's an extra fee.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: How much is it?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's about 60,000 won.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: That's too expensive. Can I move some items around?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If you have another bag, you can split them up.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, let me sort it out for a moment.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Take your time, there's time.

airport-b1x-lounge-guest.title: Bringing a guest into the lounge

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'd like to bring a companion into the lounge.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Let me check if there's a guest privilege.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: My card is a premium card.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: In that case, you can bring one guest for free.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: That's a relief. Thank you.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please show me your card and boarding pass.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: どうぞ。

airport-b1x-minor-pickup.title: Confirming who will pick up a minor

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Who is picking up your child at the arrival airport?

lines.speaker: 학부모
lines.en: The child's uncle will be picking her up.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We'll need a copy of his ID.

lines.speaker: 학부모
lines.en: I sent it by email in advance—could you check?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, one moment. It's confirmed.

lines.speaker: 학부모
lines.en: That's a relief. My daughter is quite worried.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Our staff will be with her the whole way.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Do you have the vaccination certificate?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Oh, I think I left it at home.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then we can't board your pet.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I have a photo on my phone—would that work?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Let me check for a moment. Please send the photo.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I just sent it.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's confirmed. We'll let it pass this time.

airport-b1x-exchange-large.title: Exchanging a large amount of cash

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'd like to exchange 2,000 dollars for won.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Since it's a large amount, we'll need ID.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Will a passport work?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, a passport is enough.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: How much is the fee?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's about 2 percent.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, please exchange it.

airport-b1x-rebook-hotel.title: Rebooking and asking about a hotel voucher

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: My flight got canceled and moved to the next morning.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, I see it. Sorry for the inconvenience.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then what about tonight's hotel?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We can give you a hotel voucher.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Is it close to the airport?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it's a 10-minute shuttle ride away.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Great, I'll take that, please.

airport-b1x-lost-belt.title: Item left at the security tray

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I think I left my belt at the security tray.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: About when did you go through?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: About 10 minutes ago.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: One moment, I'll check by radio.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: They found it. You can go back to the checkpoint.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: What a relief, thank you.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: The driver who's supposed to pick me up isn't here.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Do you have your booking confirmation?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Yes, it's on my phone.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll call the company to check.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Yes, please.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: They say the driver will arrive in 10 minutes.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, I'll wait here.

airport-b1x-gate-far.title: Gate changed to a far terminal

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I heard on the announcement that the gate changed—is that right?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it's been moved to a different terminal.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: How long does it take to get there?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: By shuttle, it takes about 15 minutes.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I should go right now.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you catch the shuttle over there.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Thanks, I'd better hurry.

airport-b1x-fragile-refuse.title: Fragile item the airline won't check

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We can't accept this pottery as checked baggage.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Why not?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's too fragile and doesn't meet our policy.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then can I carry it on board?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If the size fits, yes.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Let me check the size.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Try putting it in the sizer over there.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I have a peanut allergy—will that be reflected in the meal?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Didn't you request it when booking?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I forgot. Is it possible even now?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: There's 2 hours until departure, so it should be possible.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Really? What a relief.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll put in the request right now.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Thank you so much.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'd like to go into the lounge.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry, but it's full right now.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: How long do I need to wait?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It usually takes about 20 minutes.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then I'll wait and come back.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll give you a number ticket.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, thank you.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I don't see any carts—are they all taken?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it's been busy this morning so we're short right now.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I have a lot of luggage, so it's hard without one.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: When will more come in?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: A staff member just went out to collect them, so they'll be here soon.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then I'll wait here for a bit.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll bring one to you as soon as I see one.

airport-b1x-lounge-time.title: How long can you stay in the lounge

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: How long can I stay in the lounge?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You're free to stay until boarding begins.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: My flight is in 3 hours, so I'll probably be here a while.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: That's fine, there's no time limit.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then can I also use the shower room?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you can use it if you just make a reservation.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: That's great, I'll reserve one now.

lines.speaker: 승무원
lines.en: I'm sorry, but the vegetarian meal has run out.

lines.speaker: 승객
lines.en: What? I requested it in advance.

lines.speaker: 승무원
lines.en: Let me check the reservation record, one moment.

lines.speaker: 승객
lines.en: Yes, please check.

lines.speaker: 승무원
lines.en: I'm sorry, it wasn't reflected in the system.

lines.speaker: 승객
lines.en: Then is there anything I can eat now?

lines.speaker: 승무원
lines.en: I can give you fruit and salad.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Until what time is the exchange counter open?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Until 8 p.m. There's only 20 minutes left now.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then can we do this quickly?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, how much would you like to exchange?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: 300 dollars.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, I'll process it right away.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Thank you, I'm glad I made it in time.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: One of the cart wheels seems to have come off. It keeps pulling to one side.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Oh, I'm sorry. I'll get you a new cart.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I need to move my luggage again—could you help?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, I'll move it for you.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Thank you. I was worried since I don't have much time.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: There's still plenty of time before check-in closes, so don't worry.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: That's a bit of a relief, then.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Can I get a refund on this receipt too? It's been a while since I bought it.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: When did you purchase it?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Three weeks ago. The timing is a bit borderline.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Our policy is within 3 months of purchase.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Oh, then it should still be fine.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, just give me your passport and the original receipt.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Here you go. Please check them.

airport-b2x-pet-weather.title: Pet cargo restricted due to weather

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Because of today's weather, pet cargo transport may be restricted.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: What does that mean—that my pet can't fly?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The temperature is too high, so it's under review for safety reasons.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: When will they decide? I need to board soon.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We'll let you know by 30 minutes before boarding.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: If it's not allowed, what should I do?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: In that case, we'll change you to the next flight for free.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry, but this bill isn't being recognized by our machine.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Really? That's strange—I got it from a bank.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Could you exchange it for a different bill?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: This is all I have right now. What should I do?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: For now, I'll exclude this bill and exchange only the rest.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then what do I do with this bill?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It would be best to check it again at a bank counter.

airport-b2x-rebook-connection.title: Rebooking that breaks a hotel reservation

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: You said you'd change me to the next flight, but that means arriving very late at night.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, I'm sorry, but that's the only seat available today.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'm worried the hotel check-in time will have passed by then.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We can contact the hotel to request a late check-in on your behalf.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Can you really do that for me?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, could you show me your reservation confirmation?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Here you go, I'd appreciate it.

airport-b2x-lostbelt-claim.title: Filing a claim for an item lost at security

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I think I lost my watch at security, but I can't find it anywhere.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Do you remember when and which checkpoint it was?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: About an hour ago, I think it was checkpoint 3.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then you'll need to fill out a lost item report.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: If it's found, how will I be contacted?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If you leave your contact info, we'll call as soon as it's found.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, I'll write my number down here.

airport-b2x-minor-late-pickup.title: Guardian late to pick up an unaccompanied minor

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The person who was supposed to pick up your child hasn't arrived yet.

lines.speaker: 보호자
lines.en: What? We've been waiting here the whole time.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry, let me check again. What's the name?

lines.speaker: 보호자
lines.en: Park Jihoon. The child's uncle.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Ah, confirmed. Just show your ID and I'll hand her over right away.

lines.speaker: 보호자
lines.en: Here it is. I was really worried.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry for the trouble.

airport-b2x-gate-shuttle-miss.title: Missed the shuttle to a changed gate

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I missed the shuttle and I think I'll be late for the gate.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Which gate are you headed to?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Gate 42. I heard it just changed.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The next shuttle comes in 5 minutes.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then I don't think I'll make it in time for boarding.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll contact the gate ahead of time to let them know.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Thank you so much, I'll hurry.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I even put a fragile sticker on it, but when I opened it after arrival, it was broken.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm truly sorry. When and where did you notice this?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I just opened it at the baggage claim.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If you fill out a damage report, we'll help you with the compensation process.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Do I need a receipt—for the item inside?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, if possible bring it, but a photo helps too if you don't have it.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, I'll fill out the report now.

airport-b2x-taxfree-electronics.title: Tax refund on electronics needs inspection

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Electronics need a physical inspection before the refund.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Oh, so I need to take it out of my luggage now?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you need to have it checked before checking in your luggage.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I already checked in—what should I do?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then please go to the customs verification counter over there first.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Can they verify it there too?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, once you get the stamp there, we'll process it.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: The number on this scale is very different from what I measured at home.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Our scale is checked every morning. There shouldn't be much error.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Still, a 2-kilogram difference seems strange.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If you'd like, I can weigh it again on another scale.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Yes, I'd appreciate that.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Let's move it over here and check again.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: If it's the same, I'll just pay the excess fee.

airport-b2x-arrival-nowifi.title: Can't reach pickup driver without wifi

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I can't get wifi, so I can't reach the driver.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The free wifi zone is over near the information desk.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: That's a bit far—could I possibly borrow a phone here?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you can use it for a moment. What's the number?

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'll tell you the number, thank you.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's connected, go ahead and talk.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: This was a huge help.

airport-b2x-charger-not-returned.title: Forgot to return the borrowed charger

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You haven't returned the portable charger you borrowed yet.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Oh, sorry. I forgot it was in my bag.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Boarding has already started, and if it's not returned there's a charge.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I'll take it out right now, one moment.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Here it is, I'm really sorry.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's fine, I've confirmed it so there won't be a charge.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: What a relief, I'll board quickly.

airport-b2x-lounge-noshow.title: Lounge access denied due to system error

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I was told my card gives lounge access, but it's showing as not valid.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Let me scan the number on the back of the card again.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Here. It worked without any issue before.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It seems to be an error on our system's side, one moment.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: How long will it take? I don't have much time before my flight.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I've requested a check with headquarters, so it should be resolved within 5 minutes.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Okay, I'll wait here.

airport-b2x-wheelchair-mismatch.title: 航空管制官の労働交渉

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I requested a wheelchair for my father when booking, but there's no record here.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry, I can't find it in the system.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: That's strange, I even got a confirmation email.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If you show me the email, that would help.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Here, please check.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Confirmed. I'll get a wheelchair ready for you right now.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Thank you, I was worried he'd have a hard time standing for long.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The carrier is 2 centimeters bigger than our standard.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: What? This is the size I confirmed when I booked.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry, but our in-cabin policy is a bit stricter.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: Then what should I do? I don't have another carrier.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Let me check if the shop sells a carrier that fits.

lines.speaker: 여행객
lines.en: I don't have much time—could you check quickly?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, I'll contact them right now.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: This bean has an unusually distinct aroma. Where do you source it from?

lines.speaker: 로스터
lines.en: It's direct-contract grown with a cooperative in Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia. We more or less bypass the middlemen.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then the price is bound to be high.

lines.speaker: 로스터
lines.en: Right, because we pay farmers a fair price, our cost is about thirty percent higher than the chains. Even so, customers have been understanding about it.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Have you gotten fair-trade certification too?

lines.speaker: 로스터
lines.en: The certification process is so demanding that we're still operating on our own internal standards. I think verifying the relationship directly beats relying on a certification stamp anyway.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hearing that actually puts my mind at ease with every cup.

lines.speaker: 로스터
lines.en: If it feels that way to you, there's nothing more we could ask for.

lines.speaker: 재현
lines.en: This alley already has over ten cafes now. It used to just have a hardware store and a laundromat.

lines.speaker: 은서
lines.en: Exactly. As rents go up, the people who ran shops here for years get pushed out one by one.

lines.speaker: 재현
lines.en: But we can't just categorically call it a bad thing that cafes are moving in either. The foot traffic increase has revitalized the commercial district itself.

lines.speaker: 은서
lines.en: But if that revitalization comes at the cost of driving out the original residents, can we really call that pure development?

lines.speaker: 재현
lines.en: Your point has merit, but then what's the alternative? If we allow neither redevelopment nor commercialization, is the neighborhood just supposed to stay run-down?

lines.speaker: 은서
lines.en: I think the premise that there's no path between decay and gentrification is itself the problem. We should first think about institutional safeguards like rent caps.

lines.speaker: 재현
