lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Glad it's found — take care.

cafe-b1x-menuboard.title: Asking about a price on the menu board

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: The menu board price and the one posted there seem different — could you check?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Oh, sorry. Prices went up last week and we haven't updated the poster yet.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then which price will I be charged?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: I'll charge you the old price today since it was our mistake.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you for being considerate.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: I'll get the poster updated by the end of today.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: We already mentioned the noise from the next table last week, and today it's a similar situation.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: I'm really sorry. We put up a notice after last time, but it doesn't seem to be working.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: We understand, but if it keeps happening, it's hard to have a quiet conversation.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: I understand. Shall I move you to a slightly more soundproofed seat in the back today?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, that would be great. And what should we do if this happens again?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Please call me or the manager right away — we'll respond immediately.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood, please do that for today.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Sorry, but I think I need to cancel tomorrow's coffee catering — the event got postponed suddenly.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Ah, I see. We've already ordered the beans, though, so there may be a small cancellation fee.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I see. Could we just reschedule instead? Same day next week.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, in that case we can move it without any fee at all.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's much better. Then next Tuesday, please.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Confirmed. I'll send you a confirmation text.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you, and sorry for the trouble.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's been over fifteen minutes since I ordered and it still hasn't come out. Is something wrong?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: I'm really sorry. One of the espresso machines suddenly stopped, so we're remaking it on the other one.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh, that's what happened. How much longer should I wait, then?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: About five more minutes. Please have a cookie while you wait.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thanks, I understand. It'd help to be told in advance next time, though.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: You're right, I'm sorry. We'll let customers know right away if there's a delay from now on.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I heard gym members from nearby get a discount, but it wasn't applied.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Sorry, let me check. Could you show me your membership card or app screen?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Sure, here — the screen shows I'm a member this month.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Confirmed. I'll cancel the payment and redo it with the discount applied.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. I guess I should ask in advance next time.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: No, we should have asked at the register ourselves — we missed it. I'm sorry.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: We need to discuss some sensitive work matters — could you seat us somewhere without people nearby?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Sure, I understand. The seat in the back is a bit more separated, so that should be better.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Good. It won't be loud enough for other tables to overhear us, will it?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: That seat is also far from the speakers, so it's relatively quiet.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thanks. Could we also ask you to keep service to a minimum so we're not interrupted during the meeting?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Of course — just raise your hand when you need something and I'll come only then.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you so much, that'll really help.

cafe-b2x-eventspaceask.title: Negotiating to rent the whole cafe

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: We're planning a small book talk — could we rent out the whole cafe in the evening?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, it's possible, but from six to eight is our closing time, so it needs some coordination.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is there a separate rental fee, or is there a minimum sales requirement?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: We usually set a minimum drink order based on headcount. About how many people are coming?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: We're expecting around twenty people.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: In that case, we can offer the space from six on the condition of ordering at least twenty drinks.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Great, I'll book it on those terms. Do we need any kind of contract?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I paid through the app, but my card statement shows I was charged twice.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: I'm sorry, let me check. What time was the order?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: About ten minutes ago — it seemed like the order wasn't going through, so I tapped it again.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Ah, that's probably due to network lag. Only one order came through the system, but the payment may have gone through twice.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: So can one of them be refunded? How long will it take?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, we'll process the cancellation right away. Depending on your card issuer, it may take two to three days.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood — could I get a confirmation text at least?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'm a freelancer and often work here for a long time — is there some kind of time limit?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: There's no fixed limit, but we might ask for your understanding when seats are scarce.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Could you let me know in advance if seats run short? I'll pack up and leave right away.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Sure, we'll do that. In return, it'd help us if you ordered about one drink an hour.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Of course, that's no problem. Is there some kind of membership pass, by the way?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, there's a monthly pass that includes up to two drinks a day.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That sounds good — I'll look into it.

cafe-b2x-lostwallet.title: Reporting and confirming a lost wallet

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Was a wallet turned in this afternoon, by any chance? It's a brown bifold.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: One moment, let me check. Could you tell me what's inside it? We need to verify it's yours.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: There should be a student ID, two cards, and a movie ticket.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, that matches. Here it is. Could I also see your ID?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Sure, here. I'm so relieved — I was worried I wouldn't find it.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Glad it worked out. Could you just sign this confirmation form?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Sure, here you go. Thank you so much.

cafe-b2x-managerfeedback.title: Giving detailed feedback to the manager

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is the manager here? I'd like to bring something up about the service.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Yes, I'm the manager. What was it about?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: The staff were kind, but it took over twenty minutes for my drink to come out.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: I see, I'm really sorry. One staff member couldn't come in suddenly today, so we were short-staffed.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I see, that explains it. Still, it would have helped to be informed in advance.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: You're right — we'll put up a delay notice going forward. Today's drink will be on us.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you, I appreciate you listening.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'm on the monthly subscription and I'd like to cancel it after this month.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Okay, understood. May I ask why? It would help us improve.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I just haven't been using it much — I've been too busy with work to come by.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: I see. There's also an option to pause it temporarily — would that work for you?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh, is there such an option? That sounds better than fully canceling.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, you can pause it for up to two months, and you won't be charged during that time.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's great — let's go with a two-month pause, please.

cafe-b2x-allergyupdate.title: Updating an allergy note on file

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I used to come here often, and I recently found out I have a dairy allergy. Could you flag that on my order history?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Sure, I'll add an allergy note to your membership info. Could I get your phone number?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: 010-5566-7788. And could my orders automatically switch to soy or oat milk?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Our system can't auto-switch, unfortunately — you'll need to mention it each time you order.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, then just keep the allergy flag on file and I'll mention it each time.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Done, it's registered. Should I switch today's order to soy milk too?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, please.

cafe-b2x-latenightclose.title: Asking to finish up before closing

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Excuse me, sir/ma'am, but we close in ten minutes.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh, I didn't realize. I'm almost done — could I stay just a little longer?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Sure, about fifteen minutes should be fine. We might start cleaning up, though.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's fine, I'll wrap up quietly without getting in the way.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Thank you. You can just leave your cup at the return counter.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Will do. Thanks for letting me stay a bit late.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: No problem at all, have a good night.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'm a regular here — are you preparing anything new for the fall season menu?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Yes, actually we're planning to launch a jujube tea latte next month — what do you think?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh, that sounds good. Is there any way I could try a sample?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: We actually made a few test cups today — would you like to try one?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, please! Can I give you my thoughts?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Of course — honest feedback really helps us.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: The sweetness is just right, but I think the flavor could be a bit stronger.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: We have an alumni gathering next Saturday — could we reserve seating for twelve people?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, that's possible, but our largest table seats eight, so we'd have to split it into two tables.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Could you push the two tables together, then? We'd like everyone to be able to talk together.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, that works, but that spot might overlap with other reservations, so you'd need to arrive at least two hours ahead.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood. Also, would it be okay if we brought our own cake to cut and share?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Yes, outside cake is allowed — we'll provide plates and forks for it.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you so much — please confirm the reservation, then.

cafe-b2x-spilledlaptop.title: Handling a spill near a laptop

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Excuse me, a staff member spilled a bit of water near my laptop while passing by, but luckily it didn't splash on it.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Oh no, I'm really sorry. May I take a look? Just in case, it might be best to turn it off.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yeah, it looks fine on the outside. Still, I'm a bit uneasy about it.

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: I understand. If any issue comes up later, I'll give you our manager's contact so you can let us know.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's kind of you to offer. For now, could I get a dry towel?

lines.speaker: 점원
lines.en: Sure, I'll bring one right away. The table looks wet too — shall I move you to a dry one?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, that would be great. Thanks for taking care of it.

directions-c1y-subway-hearing.title: Public hearing on a new subway route

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Today's hearing is to explain the proposed route for the new Line 9 extension.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It completely bypasses our neighborhood — was the demand survey even done properly?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Given the ground conditions, securing a straight section was difficult, so we had no choice but to opt for a detour route.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: So what you're saying is that our residents just have to put up with the inconvenience.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Instead, we plan to run a free shuttle bus to the new station.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: If the shuttle's intervals are spread out, it'll actually end up being more roundabout than now.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: We'll fix the interval at under ten minutes specifically during rush hour.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Can you put that promise in writing? Verbal promises have fizzled out time and again.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Yes, we'll compile today's discussion and distribute it as an official document before the next round of hearings.

directions-c1y-gentrification.title: Debating displacement with a longtime resident

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: There's a lot of talk that this alley, once it got famous through gentrification, ended up pushing out the original residents.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Don't even get me started. I've lived in this alley for thirty years, and now I can't even get my bearings.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Specifically, what feels most unfamiliar to you?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It's bitter having to give directions using cafe names instead of the alley names.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So have the old place names or signs disappeared entirely?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The district office left the signs up, but people only follow map apps, so they're useless.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: There's a call to preserve local identity — do you think that'll actually be effective?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: With the commercial district already transformed, a few signs aren't going to bring back the identity.

directions-c1y-15min-city.title: Explaining the 15-minute city to skeptical citizens

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: The 15-minute city is a concept where you restructure things so all daily necessities are reachable within fifteen minutes on foot or by bike.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It sounds nice, but isn't it ultimately about blocking car access?

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: It's not a total ban — essential travel is allowed, but only through-traffic is rerouted.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Then what happens to people like us who commute from the outskirts?

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: We've designed more transfer hubs so residents from the outskirts can also enter the fifteen-minute zone via public transit.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The design sounds plausible, but will you also forcibly change the layout of shops?

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: Not by force — we're inducing daily-essential businesses to move in through tax incentives.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: In that case, it might be worth watching over time.

directions-c1y-wayfinding-blind.title: Wayfinding design for the visually impaired

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I heard the wayfinding design for the visually impaired in this station's remodeling is drawing attention.

lines.speaker: 설계자
lines.en: Yes, tactile paving alone wasn't enough, so we combined tactile maps with voice guidance.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: What did you find lacking about the existing tactile paving?

lines.speaker: 설계자
lines.en: At points where the path branches, like transfer sections, it was easy to misjudge direction.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: How exactly does the voice guidance work?

lines.speaker: 설계자
lines.en: It links with a smartphone app and announces directions at every branching point as the user approaches.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Still, wouldn't elderly users who can't use the app end be left out?

lines.speaker: 설계자
lines.en: That's why we also installed audible beacons in parallel, so people can follow the sound without the app.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So you've essentially built in double and triple safeguards.

lines.speaker: 역사가
lines.en: This very intersection you're standing at was the first fork just outside the city gate during the Joseon dynasty.

lines.speaker: 관광객
lines.en: So does that big road over there used to be where the fortress wall stood?

lines.speaker: 역사가
lines.en: To be precise, it was the patrol path just inside the wall, and the wall itself ran along the ridge of that hill.

lines.speaker: 관광객
lines.en: Looking at the terrain, the path we just walked seems like it might have been a waterway originally.

lines.speaker: 역사가
lines.en: You've observed correctly. It's been covered over and turned into a road now, but it used to be a stream.

lines.speaker: 관광객
lines.en: Then following the old waterway would naturally lead into the heart of downtown, wouldn't it.

lines.speaker: 역사가
lines.en: That's right. In fact, old maps show that the commercial district all formed along that waterway.

directions-c1y-self-driving-streets.title: Do self-driving cars need different streets?

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: There's an opinion that as autonomous vehicles increase, the current road system will fall short.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Signs and lane markings were designed on the premise of human drivers, so recognition errors often occur.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: In what specific situations do errors occur most often?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: When lane markings are covered by snow or fallen leaves, sensors sometimes fail to properly detect the road boundary.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So does that mean dedicated lanes need to be built separately?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Rather than dedicated lanes, there's discussion that burying guidance lines under the road surface is more realistic.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: In that case, how would conflicts with existing pedestrian paths be coordinated?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: At every intersection, they're strengthening a pedestrian-priority signal system so autonomous cars are designed to yield automatically.

directions-c1y-street-closure-town-hall.title: A heated town hall on closing a street to cars

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: If you turn this street into a car-free zone, our shop won't even be able to bring in goods.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: We're reviewing a plan to allow delivery vehicles in during the early morning hours.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: If it's only allowed at dawn, what are we supposed to do about urgent daytime deliveries?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: For emergency cases only, we plan to issue separate permits to allow exceptions.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: If the permit process is complicated, it's bound to become meaningless in the end.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: We'll adjust the system so permits are issued instantly through online applications.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: I welcome more pedestrians, but you also need to consider our livelihood.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: We'll intensively monitor that exact point during the pilot operation period.

directions-c1y-layout-behavior.title: How city layout shapes social behavior

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: There's research showing that in neighborhoods with narrow, winding alleys, the odds of neighbors bumping into each other rise.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: What's the difference compared to new towns built around straight boulevards?

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: Straight boulevards are efficient for movement, but they aren't a structure that generates chance encounters.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Then are there cases where winding alleys are deliberately designed?

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: Yes, recent apartment complexes deliberately bend the pathways slightly so they pass through community spaces.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Don't the residents find that inconvenient instead?

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: There are complaints like that at first, but over time that spot tends to settle in as a meeting place.

lines.speaker: 친구1
lines.en: I heard starting next month you have to pay a congestion charge to enter downtown?

lines.speaker: 친구2
lines.en: Yeah, they say a fee will be charged if you drive in during rush hour.

lines.speaker: 친구1
lines.en: Then won't more people take detours, and end up clogging the other roads instead?

lines.speaker: 친구2
lines.en: Because of that possibility, they plan to gradually extend the charge to the detour roads too.

lines.speaker: 친구1
lines.en: So basically wherever you go, you'll have to pay.

lines.speaker: 친구2
lines.en: Instead, they say all the collected fees go toward expanding public transit.

lines.speaker: 친구1
lines.en: Whether that promise can be trusted is something we'll have to wait and see.

directions-c2y-heritage-vs-redevelop.title: Debating heritage preservation versus street redevelopment

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: There's a sharp standoff between a movement to designate this alley as modern cultural heritage and voices pushing for redevelopment.

lines.speaker: 학자
lines.en: This maze-like alley itself should be seen as a living map bearing witness to modern commercial history.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Talk of testimony and living maps is fine, but if there's a fire in an alley where not even a single fire truck can enter, who takes responsibility?

lines.speaker: 학자
lines.en: The safety issue can be resolved with a compromise that partially secures a fire access road while preserving the alley's skeleton.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: 'Partially securing' just means tearing down someone's front yard, doesn't it.

lines.speaker: 학자
lines.en: If compensation and relocation measures are carried out in parallel, it can't be called a one-sided sacrifice.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Listening to both of you, it seems the crux is how much of the alley's physical form should be preserved.

lines.speaker: 학자
lines.en: My concern is that if the form isn't preserved, the memory is erased along with it.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: But memory can only be carried on if the people survive safely, wouldn't you say.

directions-c2y-algorithmic-navigation.title: Debating algorithmic route optimization and social cost

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: There's criticism that navigation algorithms are funneling cars into side streets, effectively turning residential alleys into de facto arterial bypasses.

lines.speaker: 개발자
lines.en: Our algorithm is simply designed to minimize travel time — it's not deliberately targeting or funneling into any particular street.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: It's hard to say the absence of intent absolves you of responsibility for the outcome, isn't it.

lines.speaker: 개발자
lines.en: We're already reviewing an update that assigns weighting to dense residential sections to suppress the diversion inflow.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: Isn't it ironic that such adjustments end up being governed more by the algorithm designer's discretion than by the municipality's own road policy?

lines.speaker: 개발자
lines.en: For our part, we're trying to share data with municipalities to jointly reflect their policy judgments.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: There's no adequate way to verify how much the shared data actually gets reflected in real policy decisions.

lines.speaker: 개발자
lines.en: We plan to improve this by regularly publishing transparency reports.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: So it ultimately comes down to a question of trust. We'll have to see whether the reports can restore that trust.

directions-c2y-desire-lines.title: A design critic on desire lines and official planning

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: That dirt path cutting across the lawn is what's often called a 'desire line' — it's evidence that betrays the designer's original intent.

lines.speaker: 설계자
lines.en: Rather than betrayal, I'd say it's a belated revelation of the actual foot traffic that the design phase failed to capture.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: So in the end, the pedestrians have drawn a more honest map with their bodies than the blueprint did, haven't they.

lines.speaker: 설계자
lines.en: Recently we've also started observing for a set period after opening and incorporating those desire lines as official walkways.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: That would mean a perfect design can't exist from the outset, and design must presuppose post-hoc revision.

lines.speaker: 설계자
lines.en: Exactly. We now treat the first blueprint not as a final plan but as a hypothesis.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: The word 'hypothesis' is interesting. That would make the users the true co-designers, then.

lines.speaker: 설계자
lines.en: I fully agree with that framing. Though practical constraints like budget and safety standards still remain.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: So it comes down to having to find a new compromise between ideal and reality every time.

directions-c2y-toponym-erasure.title: A journalist on the erasure of old place names

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: There's growing concern that, since the administrative district mergers, old place names are disappearing from maps one by one.

lines.speaker: 지명학자
lines.en: A place name isn't just a marker — it's a linguistic heritage that compresses the land's history and topographical information.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Specifically, what kind of information do you mean is embedded in a place name?

lines.speaker: 지명학자
lines.en: For instance, a name like 'Galhyeon-dong' carries topographical information that there used to be a reed-covered hill pass there.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: But new administrative names are mostly composed of just numbers or compass directions, aren't they.

lines.speaker: 지명학자
lines.en: That's right. Prioritizing efficiency alone ends up erasing the entire narrative the land once held.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Is there a realistic alternative to stem this trend?

lines.speaker: 지명학자
lines.en: I believe even just installing signs that co-list the old place names alongside the administrative ones could restore a significant part of it.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So in the end, one small sign becomes the last bastion holding up a region's memory.

directions-c2y-superblock-debate.title: A debate over superblocks and local commerce

lines.speaker: 패널1
lines.en: There's fierce backlash from merchants claiming that restricting internal road traffic under the superblock policy has depressed local commerce.

lines.speaker: 패널2
lines.en: Looking only at short-term statistics might make it seem that way, but foot traffic itself has actually increased.

lines.speaker: 패널1
lines.en: But an increase in pedestrians isn't proof that it translated into sales, is it.

lines.speaker: 패널2
lines.en: Looking at the initial six-month data, sales at small cafes and bookstores rose distinctly.

lines.speaker: 패널1
lines.en: On the other hand, large stores have been complaining one after another that logistics costs have surged as delivery vehicles are blocked.

lines.speaker: 패널2
lines.en: I acknowledge that point. I think a supplementary measure expanding dedicated delivery time slots is needed.

lines.speaker: 패널1
lines.en: So it means the policy's light and shadow are starkly divided depending on the scale of the business.

lines.speaker: 패널2
lines.en: That's right. But rather than scrapping the policy itself because of that divide, we should supplement it with more finely tuned exception clauses.

lines.speaker: 패널1
lines.en: How quickly that fine-tuning is carried out will likely determine whether the policy succeeds or fails.

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: Since this passenger terminal opened, complaints are pouring in that the multilingual signage is actually increasing confusion.

lines.speaker: 기자2
lines.en: I went and saw it myself — with four languages crammed onto a single sign, it actually didn't stand out at all.

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: That's a textbook case of information overload actually harming readability.

lines.speaker: 기자2
lines.en: On top of that, the priority order between languages was jumbled, so foreign tourists took time even finding their own language.

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: There's also a proposal to simplify things by relying mainly on pictograms — what about that?

lines.speaker: 기자2
lines.en: The limitation is that pictograms alone struggle to convey detailed direction — like exactly which gate number.

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: So it comes down to how you hierarchically arrange language and pictograms.

lines.speaker: 기자2
lines.en: The terminal authority stated they'll test pilot signage with readjusted viewing angles and color contrast by next quarter.

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: At least they've correctly identified the problem, so the outcome is worth looking forward to.

directions-c2y-street-vendor-informal-ma.title: Informal vendor networks versus the official street map

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: It's fascinating that the alley maps street vendors informally share among themselves are more sophisticated than the official map.

lines.speaker: 상인
lines.en: We know down to which alley the enforcement team enters from, even which ones are dead ends.

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: Is it accurate to say that information gets passed down orally across generations?

lines.speaker: 상인
lines.en: Yes, I inherited it from my mother, and now I'm passing it on to junior vendors.

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: The official map doesn't reflect any of that behind-the-scenes routing at all.

lines.speaker: 상인
lines.en: Of course. Our map is a map for survival, not one for tourists.

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: Then shouldn't urban policymakers need to bring this informal knowledge into the institutional fold?

lines.speaker: 상인
lines.en: From our position, we're also worried that could end up making enforcement more sophisticated instead.

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: So finding a balance between sharing knowledge and protecting livelihoods remains the homework left to do.

directions-c2y-flood-evacuation-route.title: Reassessing evacuation routes after a flood

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: This heavy rain revealed that a significant portion of the existing evacuation routes were, in practice, useless.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: The shortest route on the map actually passed through low-lying areas, which ended up increasing the flood risk instead.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: So what factor should be the top priority in redesigning the routes?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Based on elevation data, evacuation routes must be designated strictly in the uphill direction.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: I doubt residents will abandon the shortcuts they're familiar with and follow an unfamiliar route.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: That's why the key is to have regular evacuation drills even in ordinary times, so the new route becomes second nature.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Increasing the number of drills isn't easy given the budget — is there an alternative?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Instead of live drills, providing a virtual evacuation simulation through an augmented reality app is also worth considering.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: First we'll overhaul the signage for the high-ground routes, then move on to the next stage.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: There's considerable backlash against the decision to move the statue from the center of the square to the outskirts.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: That statue isn't just a piece of art — it's served as this square's landmark reference point.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: How do you view the city's explanation that it's being moved due to a historical reassessment of the figure?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: I think the reassessment is necessary. But erasing the location entirely is a different matter.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: What specific inconvenience arises if the location is erased?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: We always set meeting spots as 'in front of the statue,' but now that reference point itself disappears.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: The city said it will put up a large clock tower in that spot instead.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It'll take quite a while for a clock tower to settle into people's minds the way the statue did.

directions-c1z-border-identity.title: A geographer on how district lines shape identity

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I hear you've researched how administrative district boundaries affect residents' sense of belonging.

lines.speaker: 지리학자
lines.en: Yes, even areas that look like the same neighborhood often split in identity because of a single boundary line.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Could you give a specific example?

lines.speaker: 지리학자
lines.en: Based on this road, one side is 'Gangnam' and the other isn't, and that alone changes everything from property values to school zones.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Do residents actually feel that boundary in practice?

lines.speaker: 지리학자
lines.en: Yes, in surveys a high proportion answered that residents across the road were 'people from a different neighborhood,' not 'neighbors.'

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Then would readjusting the boundary change that perception too?

lines.speaker: 지리학자
lines.en: Changing the line alone won't shift it right away — the place names and signage imprinted over a long time carry far more weight.

directions-c1z-highrise-view.title: Neighbors debating a high-rise blocking mountain views

lines.speaker: 주민1
lines.en: Did you know that once that apartment goes up, the mountain we see from our veranda will be completely blocked?

lines.speaker: 주민2
lines.en: I know. But that's a building on private land, so there's no way for us to stop it.

lines.speaker: 주민1
lines.en: There are cases where people went as far as lawsuits over infringement of view rights.

lines.speaker: 주민2
lines.en: Most of those lawsuits involved sunlight rights, and view alone is rarely recognized on its own.

lines.speaker: 주민1
lines.en: So you're saying all we can do is just watch it happen.

lines.speaker: 주민2
lines.en: We could at least request a height restriction at the district office's briefing session.

lines.speaker: 주민1
lines.en: Even if the height is lowered, won't the mountain still be blocked unless the orientation changes?

lines.speaker: 주민2
lines.en: We should file a complaint asking them to rotate the building layout too. If that fails, we'll figure out another way then.

directions-c1z-delivery-algorithm.title: A sociologist on delivery-app algorithms and street commerce

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: What's the basis for the claim that delivery-app algorithms determine the rise and fall of back-alley commerce?

lines.speaker: 사회학자
lines.en: Since exposure ranking depends on delivery distance and review count, storefronts on main streets are structurally favored.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So do shops tucked in the alleys have no chance at all?

lines.speaker: 사회학자
lines.en: The initial barrier to entry is high, but I've also seen rankings flip once reviews accumulate.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So it seems the position within the app has become more important than the alley's physical location.

lines.speaker: 사회학자
lines.en: Exactly. Because customers judge based on the app's map before the actual alley map.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Then policies aiming to revive commercial districts would need to consider the app's exposure system too.

directions-c1z-gps-memory.title: Is GPS eroding our spatial memory?

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I hear there's research showing that spatial memory declines the more we rely on navigation apps.

lines.speaker: 인지과학자
lines.en: Yes, when people follow arrows instead of mentally mapping the route themselves, hippocampal activity noticeably decreases.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Does that mean the very ability to find one's way is degenerating?

lines.speaker: 인지과학자
lines.en: It doesn't vanish entirely, but the ability to improvise directions in an unfamiliar place definitely weakens.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: How does that compare to people like taxi drivers who've memorized routes through long experience?

lines.speaker: 인지과학자
lines.en: There's research showing that veteran drivers actually have a more developed posterior hippocampus.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So is completely cutting off navigation the answer?

lines.speaker: 인지과학자
lines.en: No — occasionally turning off the map and practicing routing your own path is enough.

directions-c1z-road-diet.title: A city planner defending a road diet against driver backlash

lines.speaker: 운전자
lines.en: If you shrink a four-lane road down to two lanes, won't the already congested road just get worse?

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: It may feel that way in the short term, but measured data shows travel speed itself doesn't change much.

lines.speaker: 운전자
lines.en: Then isn't the leftover lane just being wasted?

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: It's not wasted — it's reallocated into a bike lane and a left-turn lane, which actually lowers the accident rate.

lines.speaker: 운전자
lines.en: Even granting the accident rate, the congestion I feel during rush hour has definitely increased.

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: The first couple of months after implementation are an adjustment period where congestion stands out, but the typical pattern is that it eases afterward.

lines.speaker: 운전자
lines.en: The problem is that enduring those couple of months isn't easy for us.

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: That's why, during the adjustment period, we plan to temporarily adjust the signal system on nearby detour roads to spread the burden.

directions-c1z-shortcut-dispute.title: Discussing shortcut culture and property disputes

lines.speaker: 주민1
lines.en: I heard the shortcut across that backyard got blocked off by the owner recently.

lines.speaker: 주민2
lines.en: Right, it's technically private land, but everyone had just walked through it for decades, so it caught people off guard.

lines.speaker: 주민1
lines.en: If it's been used that long, doesn't a customary right of way get established?

lines.speaker: 주민2
lines.en: You can make a customary-law claim, but apparently once the owner explicitly blocks it, the standing disappears from that moment.

lines.speaker: 주민1
lines.en: So now everyone has to take a ten-minute longer detour via the main road.

lines.speaker: 주민2
lines.en: There's also talk of filing a complaint asking the district office to designate it as an official right-of-way.

lines.speaker: 주민1
lines.en: That would require the owner's consent to be accepted — do you think they'll agree readily?

lines.speaker: 주민2
lines.en: There's also a suggestion to discuss a toll or landscaping support as compensation, so there might be room for negotiation.

directions-c1z-invisible-disability.title: An accessibility advocate on invisible disabilities and wayfinding

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Are you saying that beyond wheelchair ramps, wayfinding for people with cognitive disabilities is also needed?

lines.speaker: 활동가
lines.en: Yes, disabilities that aren't visible from the outside are often not even considered in signage design at all.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: What kind of problem specifically arises?

lines.speaker: 활동가
lines.en: When complex color coding or multiple overlapping arrows are used, it takes a long time to judge direction.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So how do you think signage should be changed?

lines.speaker: 활동가
lines.en: The amount of information needs to be reduced, and each point should be simplified to require only one decision.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Wouldn't that kind of design actually be inconvenient for people without disabilities?

lines.speaker: 활동가
lines.en: It's actually the opposite — simple wayfinding reduces the time anyone spends getting lost.

directions-c1z-forgotten-alley.title: An urban explorer's essay on a forgotten alleyway

lines.speaker: 탐방객
lines.en: This alley doesn't even show up on maps — how did you know to come here?

lines.speaker: 탐방가
lines.en: I stumbled on it while digging through old land registry maps. It's a road that got erased during redevelopment.

lines.speaker: 탐방객
lines.en: It's actually still intact like this — why did it disappear from the map, then?

lines.speaker: 탐방가
lines.en: Administratively it was processed as a decommissioned road, but the demolition budget fell short, so it physically remains as is.

lines.speaker: 탐방객
lines.en: So we're currently walking on a road that legally doesn't exist.

lines.speaker: 탐방가
lines.en: Right. Quite a few of these gaps in the fabric remain scattered around the city.

lines.speaker: 탐방객
lines.en: Isn't it dangerous, given it's an unmanaged section?

lines.speaker: 탐방가
lines.en: The structure is fairly sturdy so there's no major danger, but at night there's no lighting, so you have to be careful.

directions-c2z-tidal-causeway.title: Whether to keep publishing a tidal causeway's safe-crossing times

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Given how often accidents happen, why keep that tidal-flat path open when it's only walkable depending on the tide?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Most stranding incidents happen when people ignore the safe-crossing times we've officially posted.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Wouldn't the fundamental solution be to just close it entirely and build a bridge?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Building a bridge would eliminate the very landscape unique to this area, where the path appears and vanishes with the tide.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Isn't weighing scenery against safety a burden for the administration?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: It is a burden, but in resident surveys more responses favored stronger control measures over building a new bridge.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: If control is being strengthened, what specific measures are planned?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: We plan to install a real-time tide display board at the entrance and physically lock a gate during restricted hours.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Even with the gate locked, how will you stop people who go around it?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: We're increasing surveillance cameras at bypass points and pushing an ordinance to impose fines when caught.

directions-c2z-desire-path-park.title: A parks official on paving over trampled desire paths

lines.speaker: 설계가
lines.en: There's a proposal to just pave over those bare-earth paths worn across the lawn and officially recognize them as walking trails.

lines.speaker: 공원 관리자
lines.en: If we pave them, wouldn't visitors take that as a signal they can ignore the landscape design altogether?

lines.speaker: 설계가
lines.en: It's actually the opposite — it would amount to admitting the real problem was a design that ignored how people actually walk.

lines.speaker: 공원 관리자
lines.en: So are you saying the original mistake was failing to predict these actual walking patterns when designing the landscaping?

lines.speaker: 설계가
lines.en: Perfect prediction is impossible, but the paths that form after opening should be recorded as data and reflected in future designs.

lines.speaker: 공원 관리자
lines.en: Then you're saying we should survey those paths now and incorporate them as official routes.

lines.speaker: 설계가
lines.en: Yes, though ecologically sensitive sections should be an exception, with a separate detour route encouraged instead.

lines.speaker: 공원 관리자
lines.en: I'm not sure encouraging a detour is as easy as it sounds — people ultimately take the shortest path in the end.

lines.speaker: 설계가
lines.en: That's why using planting to naturally redirect attention, rather than physical barriers, is what actually works.

directions-c2z-informal-market-map.title: Debating whether to formalize an informal street market

lines.speaker: 상인
lines.en: Our street stalls don't appear on official maps, but regulars all find us by word of mouth.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: But the problem is that because of that word-of-mouth system, first-time visitors don't even know you exist at all.

lines.speaker: 상인
lines.en: If we get put on the map, we worry it might actually make us a target for enforcement.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: If you're listed on the map on the condition of formal registration, it actually makes you a protected entity rather than an enforcement target.

lines.speaker: 상인
lines.en: If the registration process is complicated, small-scale vendors like us won't even be able to consider it.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: That's why this time we simplified the process so registration is possible through an on-site inspection alone, without paperwork.

lines.speaker: 상인
lines.en: Once registered, will our location show up accurately on map apps too?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Yes, we're coordinating to provide the local government's data to map companies so even stall locations get reflected.

lines.speaker: 상인
lines.en: In that case, there's really nothing for us to lose.

directions-c2z-flood-route-remap.title: Remapping delivery routes after repeated flash floods

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I hear logistics companies are completely redrawing delivery routes because of frequent localized flooding.

lines.speaker: 물류담당자
lines.en: Yes, low-lying roads with a history of flooding are automatically excluded from routing the moment there's a rain forecast.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Rerouting like that must significantly lengthen delivery times — are there no customer complaints?

lines.speaker: 물류담당자
lines.en: There were some at first, but customers now understand it's better than delivery being delayed entirely due to flooding.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: How do you update the route data in real time?

lines.speaker: 물류담당자
lines.en: We receive drainage sensor data from the district office, and when the water level at a specific point exceeds the threshold, a detour signal is sent immediately.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: How do you handle sections without sensors?

lines.speaker: 물류담당자
lines.en: For those sections, we preemptively block routing based solely on rainfall forecasts, using past flooding history.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So the map essentially keeps being redrawn in real time.

lines.speaker: 물류담당자
lines.en: Exactly. You could think of it not as a fixed map, but as a living route network that responds to the weather.

directions-c2z-scent-landmark.title: Using smell as an unofficial landmark for the visually impaired

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: We've confirmed that smells like a bakery's or a salted-seafood market's actually function as real landmarks for visually impaired users.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: It's uncommon to see wayfinding research using smell rather than touch or hearing.

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: Right, when we interviewed people, far more responses than expected cited using smell to identify location.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Then can this olfactory information actually be incorporated into signage design?

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: Rather than the signage itself, we could adjust shop placement or ventilation locations to make a smell stand out distinctly at a specific point.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: But if the shop changes, wouldn't that olfactory landmark disappear along with it?

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: That's right, that's the limitation of this approach. So we're recommending it be applied first only to sections with a stable commercial district.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: In the long term, are you also considering placing artificial scents at specific sections?

lines.speaker: 연구자
lines.en: We are reviewing it, but there's pushback that artificial scent feels unnatural, so we're approaching it cautiously.

directions-c2z-drone-corridor.title: Residents pushing back on a proposed drone delivery corridor

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Regarding the plan for a drone delivery corridor to pass over our apartment complex, is there any noise mitigation plan?

lines.speaker: 업체 담당자
lines.en: We expect ground-level noise to be minimal by keeping the altitude above 120 meters.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Setting altitude aside, doesn't the corridor raise privacy concerns? These drones have cameras on them.

lines.speaker: 업체 담당자
lines.en: The delivery drones are equipped only with navigation cameras, and the footage is designed to be deleted in real time.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: How can we verify that claim? It ultimately just comes down to trusting the company's word.

lines.speaker: 업체 담당자
lines.en: We'll coordinate with the district office so a third-party agency regularly audits the video processing method.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Why was the corridor set right above the residential complex in the first place? There's open land nearby too.

lines.speaker: 업체 담당자
lines.en: The open-land route would double the distance, so the current corridor was optimal for battery efficiency.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: If it's purely about efficiency, doesn't that mean only we bear the noise and the risk?

lines.speaker: 업체 담당자
lines.en: I understand your point. We'll reconsider restricting nighttime operations, at least over the section above the complex.

directions-c2z-cemetery-shortcut.title: Debating a proposed shortcut path through an old cemetery

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: A dispute has arisen because the shortest route connecting the school and the residential area happens to cut through an old cemetery.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Children crossing through a cemetery on their way to school every day can't be good emotionally.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: We also reviewed creating a new path around the cemetery's edge in the form of a walking trail, but that adds about fifteen minutes to the actual commute.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Asking children to bear the emotional burden just for those fifteen minutes seems like the priorities are backward.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: So as a compromise, we're proposing to build a landscaped wall along the cemetery's boundary to block the view.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Even with a wall, they'd still ultimately be passing through the cemetery grounds all the same.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: There's also a way to coordinate with the cemetery management committee to register the school-route section as a separately designated parcel.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: If it's separated that way, would it legally no longer count as passing through the cemetery?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Yes, on the register it would be converted into a right-of-way, and the landscaping would be redone to resemble an ordinary walking trail.

directions-c2z-ai-signage-translation.title: Journalists debating AI-translated street signage errors

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: I hear complaints have increased that tourists are getting more lost, not less, as automatically translated signs have spread.

lines.speaker: 기자2
lines.en: Yes, apparently signs were found where 'meokja-golmok' was translated literally, so the meaning didn't come across at all.

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: Proper nouns should be transliterated and only common nouns translated — sounds like the machine can't make that distinction?

lines.speaker: 기자2
lines.en: Right, and even the same word needs different renderings depending on context, but since it's processed uniformly, mistranslations keep repeating.

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: So how is the district office responding to this issue?

lines.speaker: 기자2
lines.en: They say they'll assign review staff to filter errors before installation, but apparently the budget isn't generous.

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: So there's a chance mistranslations end up being left unaddressed due to budget issues after all.

lines.speaker: 기자2
lines.en: Yes, so they're apparently even considering a system that rewards points to citizens who report mistranslations.

lines.speaker: 기자1
lines.en: So it ends up being a situation where people have to fill in the gaps the machine leaves behind after all.

directions-c2z-tunnel-vibration.title: Residents contesting a new tunnel's projected vibration radius

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: You said the tunnel blasting vibration wouldn't affect our house, but what's the basis for that?

lines.speaker: 시공사 담당자
lines.en: According to the geological survey, the area was classified as having a high vibration-attenuation rate due to solid bedrock.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: But I heard the neighboring area got a similar explanation and cracks still appeared.

lines.speaker: 시공사 담당자
lines.en: That case involved different geological conditions, so it's hard to apply it directly to our section.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: From our side, we have no choice but to request a reassessment by an independent agency before construction.

lines.speaker: 시공사 담당자
lines.en: If you request it, we'll conduct the preliminary survey again through a third-party verification agency.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: If the results come out different from our concerns, would you be willing to change the blasting method itself?

lines.speaker: 시공사 담당자
lines.en: If the vibration exceeds the threshold, we plan to switch from blasting to mechanical excavation instead.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Mechanical excavation would extend the construction period, so we'd need to discuss compensation for that delay too.

directions-c2z-heat-shade-route.title: Debating a shade-priority pedestrian route for extreme heat

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: As the number of extreme-heat days rises, a proposal came up to add a shade-following detour route to guidance instead of the shortest path.

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: The intent is good, but the problem is that shade routes don't always connect to a safe sidewalk.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Then what if we prioritize designating only sections that satisfy both safety and shade at the same time?

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: That would sharply reduce the number of sections that qualify, which could undercut its effectiveness.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: Then how about planting street trees in parallel to gradually fill in the deficient sections?

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: That's a realistic approach, but it takes at least five years for trees to grow enough to actually cast shade.

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: In the meantime, we'll fill the gap by temporarily installing canopy-style awnings.

lines.speaker: 도시계획가
lines.en: Awnings would come with considerable maintenance costs — has the budget actually been secured?

lines.speaker: 공무원
lines.en: We plan to install them as a pilot first in heat-vulnerable sections, then allocate additional budget depending on the response.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Excuse me, where's the bank?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It's next to the convenience store over there.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: ありがとうございます。

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: You're welcome, take care.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is there an ATM near here?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Yes, it's inside this building.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: What floor?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The first floor.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: The pharmacy is closed.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: There's another pharmacy over there.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is it far?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: No, it's close.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is the bus stop across the street?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Yes, cross at that crosswalk.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Got it, thanks.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Take care crossing.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Which platform is the airport train?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Platform 3.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is it this way?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Yes, that's right.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where's the elevator?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: It's next to the stairs.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Can I take the stairs too?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Yes, either is fine.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: What time is the last train?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: It's midnight.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: There's still time.

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Yes, but hurry.

directions-a1x-card-tap.title: Where to tap the transit card

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where do I tap my card?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Here, on the green part.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Like this?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Yes, that's right.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Where's the parking lot entrance?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: It's behind the building.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Can I drive there?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Yes, go straight there.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where in the plaza should we meet?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Let's meet in front of the fountain.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Okay, sounds good.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: See you then.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What's the restroom code?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's on the receipt.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh, here it is.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's it.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Which exit number?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Exit 5.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is it far from here?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: No, it's right there.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where's the post office?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It's on the left at the intersection.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is it close to walk?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Yes, five minutes is enough.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where do I catch a taxi?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: It's outside the main gate.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is the line long?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: It's short right now.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where's the park entrance?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It's after you cross the bridge.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: ありがとう。

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Take your time getting there.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I tapped my transit card but the gate didn't open.

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Did the card have enough balance?

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I topped it up earlier, that's strange.

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Try tapping again here.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Oh, it opened now.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Until what time is the bank open?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It was until 4, and it's 3:50 now.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then I should hurry.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: If you run, you won't be late.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Okay, I'll go now!

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is there a pharmacy open at night?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Yes, there's a 24-hour pharmacy in front of the station.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How long does it take to get there?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It'll take about ten minutes on foot.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Okay, I'll go check it out.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Do I catch the City Hall bus from this stop?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: No, that's on the stop across the street.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then how do I cross over?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: You can cross using that overpass.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Okay, thank you.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Can I check my luggage in advance on the airport train?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Yes, it's possible at the city air terminal.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where is that?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Go out exit 2 and you'll see it right away.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Great, I'll head there.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: The elevator is broken.

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Yes, it's been under repair since this morning.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: So I have to carry my luggage on the stairs?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: You can use the wheelchair lift instead.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Oh, that's a relief.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: This parking lot is full.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Yes, there's another lot behind here.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Are there spots there?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: I just checked, and a few spots are left.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Then I'll head over there.

directions-a2x-plaza-crowded.title: Finding a friend in a crowded plaza

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: There are too many people in the plaza, I can't find them.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: What color clothes are they wearing?

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: They're wearing a red jacket.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: I think they're near the clock tower over there.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Oh, I found them, thanks!

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I entered the code but it won't open.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The code changed yesterday.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What's the new code?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's written at the bottom of the receipt here.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh, found it.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: The market's main entrance is under construction.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Then you have to go in through the side door.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where's the side door?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It's at the end of that alley.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Got it, thank you.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Which way is the emergency room?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: It's in the annex, not the main building.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How do I get to the annex?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Go outside and head to the right.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Okay, I'll hurry over.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is there a luggage locker near here?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Yes, right after you pass the ticket gate.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How much does it cost?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: It depends on the size, but it's usually 3,000 won.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Great, I'll use it.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: What gate is my seat at?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Could you show me your ticket?

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Here it is.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: You should go to gate 7.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Thanks, I'll head there.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where do visitors enter?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: You need to come through the back gate, not the front.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is the back gate far from here?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: It takes about two minutes by car.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Okay, I'll head over.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: What floor is the gym on?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: It's on basement floor 1.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Can I take the elevator?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Yes, just press the B1 button.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: ありがとうございます。

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: I didn't realize this was a one-way street.

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: Right, it seems you missed the sign.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: So how do I get out now?

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: Go straight ahead and turn right at the next alley.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Can I get to the main road from there?

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: Yes, it connects directly.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is this path only for bicycles?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Yes, the walking section is marked separately.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where should I walk, then?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The green line on the ground is the walking path.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Oh, I didn't notice the marking.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It can be confusing the first time you come here.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Does the night bus run near here too?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Yes, but the route is a bit different from the daytime bus.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: So is the stop location different too?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: This stop is shared for both.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: That's a relief, I almost got confused.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The interval is long, so check the schedule.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is there a good spot to see the night view from here?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: There's an observation deck on the roof of that building.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Can regular visitors go up there too?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Yes, but it's only open until 8 PM.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: If I go now, I should make it in time.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The elevator is a bit slow, so hurry.

directions-b1x-palace-shortcut.title: Shortcut vs scenic route to the palace

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Between the fast way and the scenic way to the palace, which is better?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The fast way is ten minutes along the main road.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How much longer is the scenic way?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It goes through the hanok alleys, so about twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Since I have time, I'll take the scenic route.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: There will be lots of good photo spots.

directions-b1x-delivery-phone.title: Directing a delivery driver by phone

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Sir/Ma'am, I can't find the entrance.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Did you pass the convenience store?

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Yes, I'm in front of it now.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Turn into the alley on the left there.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Oh, I see it now, thank you.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Please ring the buzzer on the third floor.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Which alley number is the tteokbokki place famous around here?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: I don't know the exact number, but it's near the central aisle.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Which direction is the central aisle?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Go straight in from the entrance and you'll find it.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I think I could find it by smell too.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Right, the place with the line is it.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I heard there's a shuttle bus to the main building.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Yes, you can catch it at the shuttle stop outside the main gate.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How often does it run?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: One comes every fifteen minutes.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Walking might actually be faster.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: That could be true if you don't have luggage.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: This street is closed off because of the festival.

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: Yes, please use the detour route.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then how do I get to City Hall?

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: Go around through that alley over there.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How much longer will it take?

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: It'll take about ten extra minutes.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: The building numbers aren't in order.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Right, that's because new buildings got their numbers later.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: So what number is the engineering building?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Building 7, and it's the farthest from the main gate.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I'd better look at a map app.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Yes, the campus app is more accurate.

directions-b1x-ferry-terminal-gate.title: Wrong gate at the ferry terminal

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Which gate is the ferry to Jeju Island?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Looking at your ticket, it's gate 5, not gate 2.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where's gate 5?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Go all the way to the end of this corridor.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I'm running short on time, I should run.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: There's still time before boarding closes.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Can I walk to where the cable car departs?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Yes, but it's a bit steep so it might be tough.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Isn't there a shuttle bus?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: There is, but it only runs on weekends.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Since it's a weekday today, I'll have to walk.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: If you go slowly, twenty minutes is enough.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I'm looking for the meeting room on the third floor.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: You'll need to get a visitor pass first.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where do I get that?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Give me your ID at this desk and I'll issue one.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: どうぞ。

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: The first button on the left of the elevator is for the third floor.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How many bike rental stations are near here?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: There are about three along the riverside.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Which one is closest?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: There's one under the bridge, but bikes are often unavailable.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then I should go to another one.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The one by the park entrance usually has more available.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Where do I go for a connecting flight?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: The transfer information desk is this way.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Do I need to recheck my luggage there too?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: If it's a direct connecting flight, you don't have to.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: That's a relief, I didn't have much time.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Still, it's best to hurry.

directions-b1x-apartment-visitor-parking.title: Visitor parking at an apartment complex

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Where do visitor cars park?

lines.speaker: 경비원
lines.en: There's a visitor zone next to the main gate.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Would there be a spot there?

lines.speaker: 경비원
lines.en: There's usually space at this time.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Could you also tell me which building to go to?

lines.speaker: 경비원
lines.en: Building 101 is over there on the right.

directions-b2x-underground-mall-maze.title: Getting lost in an underground shopping mall

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I had no idea the underground mall was this complicated, I got completely lost.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: First-timers always do, but each section is color-coded so you can use that as a reference.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Oh, now that you mention it, the floor colors are different.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The red zone is clothing, and the blue zone is general goods.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: So which side is the shoe store I'm looking for?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Shoe stores are clustered at the far end of the blue zone.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Thanks to you I finally have a sense of direction, thank you.

directions-b2x-toll-gate-lane.title: Picking the wrong toll gate lane

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: I didn't realize this was a Hi-pass-only lane, what should I do?

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: Slow down for now and pass through as is, the toll will be billed to you by text later.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Won't I get a fine?

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: For accidental entries, only the toll is charged, so you don't need to worry.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: I'll have to watch the signs more carefully next time.

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: The regular lanes are always clustered on the right, keep that in mind.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: The map shows two forks here, but there are actually three.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Ah, that's probably a new side trail from last year, the map hasn't been updated yet.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: So which one is the original route to the summit?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The middle path is the summit route, and the left one branches off to a viewpoint.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I'm curious about the viewpoint too, how much longer would it add?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: It would add about thirty minutes round trip.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then I'll go to the summit first and stop by on the way down.

directions-b2x-delivery-address-mismatch.title: 航空管制官の労働交渉

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: I've arrived at the address, but the building name posted here doesn't match the app.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh, our building recently changed its name, it seems the registration wasn't updated.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Could you tell me the old name then, I want to double-check.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It was Hanbit Building, the sign is probably still up as is.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Ah, that's right, I found it.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's closer if you come through the back door instead of the front.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Okay, I'll go around to the back door.

directions-b2x-subway-construction-detou.title: Station renovation forces a longer walk

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Exit 3 is blocked because of construction, is there another way?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: Yes, you'll need to exit through gate 1 and go a longer way around instead.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: So how much longer than usual would that take?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: It would feel like about five to ten minutes longer.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Do you know how long the construction will continue?

lines.speaker: 역무원
lines.en: The sign says it's until the end of next month.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Until then I guess I'll just have to take the long way.

directions-b2x-shared-office-floor-plan.title: Confusing floor plan at a shared office

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: The meeting room names are all similar and confusing, where exactly is it?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: 'Haeoreum' room is in Building A, and 'Haeoreum 2' is in Building B, everyone gets confused at first.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: The one I booked is just 'Haeoreum', so that's Building A, right?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Yes, that's right, go straight down the left hallway from the lobby.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is there a separate sign, or just room numbers?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: There's a nameplate on the door, but the lighting is dim so it might be hard to see.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then I'll look carefully, thank you.

directions-b2x-riverside-run-route.title: Choosing a running route along the river

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Could you recommend a good route for a morning run?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The riverside route is flat and nice, but at this hour it overlaps with cyclists so it gets a bit crowded.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then is there another route that's less crowded?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: There's a route that loops through the inside of the park, but it has a slight uphill.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: If it has an uphill, is the distance shorter too?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: No, the distance is similar, but it feels a bit more challenging.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then I'll try the park route today.

directions-b2x-night-market-alley-number.title: Finding a stall by unofficial alley numbers

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: None of these alleys have names, so it's hard to explain the location.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Vendors just call them by numbers among themselves, that one over there is alley 3.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then why doesn't the map app show any of this?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: They're unofficial names, so they're not registered.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: So how should I explain it to a friend, then?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Taking a photo of the entrance and sending it is the most accurate way.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: That's a good idea, I'll do that.

directions-b2x-cruise-terminal-shuttle-l.title: Two shuttle lines at the cruise terminal

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: There are two kinds of shuttle buses, which one goes downtown?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: The blue bus goes downtown, and the yellow one goes to a nearby outlet mall.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How long does it take to get downtown?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: It's forty minutes without traffic, but could take over an hour with it.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How is it at this time of day?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: It's the afternoon so it might be congested, so leave with some buffer time.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Got it, I'll get moving.

lines.en: I came to apply for a passport, but they wouldn't accept me at the main entrance.

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: Visitors with civil affairs need to enter through the basement entrance of the building next door.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Which way do I go around to reach the basement entrance?

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: Go right along this wall for about a hundred meters and you'll see stairs.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Should I have my ID ready in advance too?

lines.speaker: 경찰
lines.en: Yes, they check it at the entrance, so have it out beforehand.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Understood, thank you.

directions-b2x-camp-site-numbering.title: Campsite numbering doesn't match the reservation

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: The reserved site number doesn't seem to match the number on the sign.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: The numbers changed a bit when the zones were rearranged last year.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: So the reservation system wasn't updated then?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Yes, sorry about that, let me guide you again based on the on-site numbering.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: We wanted a spot by the river, where's that?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: The riverside zone now starts with the letter A, you can head that way.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Okay, I'll head over there.

directions-b2x-elevator-restricted-floor.title: Elevator won't go to a restricted floor

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I pressed the button for floor 12 but it's not lighting up.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: That floor requires a card authentication to go up, do you have a visitor pass?

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I haven't gotten one yet, where do I get it?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: You can get one issued at the lobby desk on the first floor.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: So I have to go back down.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Yes, but issuing is quick so it won't take long.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Okay, I'll be back quickly.

directions-b2x-airport-rental-car-shuttl.title: Rental car shuttle pickup point moved

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Is this the right spot for the rental car shuttle? The signage seems to not match the location.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Ah, the pickup location moved to near exit 3 starting last week.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: How far do I need to walk from here, then?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: With luggage, it'll take about five minutes.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Shouldn't they put up new signs?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: You're right, we keep raising that too.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then I'll head to exit 3 right away.

directions-b2x-temple-visitor-route.title: Temple has a separate route for visitors during a ceremony

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I was heading toward the main hall, but the monks are stopping people from passing.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: There's a ceremony going on right now, so visitors have to go around the side path.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: If I take the side path, will I not be able to see the main hall at all?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: No, you can see it from a bit farther away, you just can't get close.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: About when does the ceremony end?

lines.speaker: 주민
