lines.en: It usually takes about an hour, so you could come back then.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then I'll look around elsewhere first and come back.

directions-b2x-warehouse-loading-dock.title: Truck driver directed to the wrong loading dock

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: You told me to come to loading dock 3, but this one is marked 5.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: Sorry, the sign plate is old and hasn't been updated.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: So where's the actual number 3?

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: The second building from here is the real number 3.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: I need to turn the truck around, but the space is tight.

lines.speaker: 안내원
lines.en: I'll go out and guide you while you back up.

lines.speaker: 기사
lines.en: Thanks, that's a big help.

directions-b2x-flea-market-vendor-map.title: Vendor map doesn't match the actual flea market layout

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: The map I got from the information booth doesn't seem to match the actual layout.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Right, the vendor positions are decided by lottery every month, so the map is often wrong.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Then how do I find the shop I'm looking for?

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: The section numbers don't change, so you can ask using those.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: I heard the shop I'm looking for is in section 3.

lines.speaker: 주민
lines.en: Section 3 is on the left past those tents.

lines.speaker: 행인
lines.en: Okay, I'll look again using the section number, thank you.

lines.speaker: 의사1
lines.en: Did you see the healthcare reform plan they announced? Apparently they're drastically raising reimbursement rates for essential specialties.

lines.speaker: 의사2
lines.en: I saw it too. I agree with the intent, but where the funding will come from seems to be the crux of it.

lines.speaker: 의사1
lines.en: Raising health insurance premiums alone will only go so far—without more government funding, I don't think it'll be sustainable.

lines.speaker: 의사2
lines.en: Right. And the avoidance of essential specialties isn't purely a reimbursement issue either. The malpractice-litigation burden and workload intensity can't be ignored.

lines.speaker: 의사1
lines.en: In the end a comprehensive approach is needed, but this plan's financial measures seem somewhat lacking, which makes me doubt its effectiveness.

lines.speaker: 의사2
lines.en: Still, I want to find significance in the fact that the discussion has started. It also seems like the medical community's voice was reflected to some degree this time.

lines.speaker: 의사1
lines.en: Once the public hearing schedule is set, I think our hospital should submit an opinion paper.

lines.speaker: 의사2
lines.en: I agree. If the voices from the field are left out, it'll inevitably become another case of desk-bound policymaking.

hospital-c1y-hedging.title: Explaining a difficult diagnosis with care

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Before I share the test results, I want to first say that this isn't a confirmed diagnosis yet—we're at the stage where an additional biopsy is needed.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Okay... but I'd still like to know, even roughly, what the possibilities are.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: The imaging revealed an area suspected of dysplasia. We can't completely rule out malignancy, but there's also overlap with benign findings.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: If it comes back as the bad outcome, what happens then?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: In that case, further tests to determine the stage would follow, and the treatment plan would be decided accordingly. But rather than jumping to conclusions now, it's right to wait for the results.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I can't help feeling anxious.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: That's completely understandable. The biopsy results will take about a week, and if you have any questions in the meantime, please feel free to contact us anytime.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Thank you. I suppose I should prepare myself for the worst case too.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Preparing is fine, but I'd like you to keep in mind that statistically, the chance of a benign result isn't low either.

hospital-c1y-burnout.title: A resident opens up about burnout

lines.speaker: 전공의
lines.en: Doctor, lately I keep thinking I don't know what I'm doing this work for anymore.

lines.speaker: 선배 의사
lines.en: Given how packed the on-call schedule's been, it's no wonder you'd feel that way.

lines.speaker: 전공의
lines.en: When I see patients, I don't feel moved the way I used to—I'm just mechanically writing prescriptions, and it surprised even me.

lines.speaker: 선배 의사
lines.en: That's a textbook sign of burnout. If you leave that emotional numbness unaddressed, it eventually affects the quality of care too.

lines.speaker: 전공의
lines.en: But since everyone else is enduring it like this, I feel self-conscious about being the only one struggling.

lines.speaker: 선배 의사
lines.en: Just because everyone endures it doesn't mean it's normal. Whether it's psychiatric counseling or taking leave, taking the necessary measures is actually the more responsible attitude.

lines.speaker: 전공의
lines.en: Honestly, the very idea of getting counseling feels like admitting a weakness.

lines.speaker: 선배 의사
lines.en: I felt the same way during my residency. But looking back, asking for help back then is exactly why I've been able to keep doing this work.

hospital-c1y-budgetcuts.title: 格安航空会社について

lines.speaker: 행정팀장
lines.en: Starting next quarter, each department's supply budget will be cut by ten percent.

lines.speaker: 과장
lines.en: Does that include supplies directly tied to patient safety?

lines.speaker: 행정팀장
lines.en: Essential medical supplies are excluded—the adjustment is planned mainly around office supplies and consumable equipment.

lines.speaker: 과장
lines.en: That's a relief, but is the hospital's overall finances really that bad?

lines.speaker: 행정팀장
lines.en: Bed occupancy hasn't fully recovered since the pandemic, and the rise in labor costs was larger than expected.

lines.speaker: 과장
lines.en: Staff on the ground are worried that if the budget shrinks, hiring will be postponed right away too.

lines.speaker: 행정팀장
lines.en: The hiring plan itself will remain in place, but the approval process may become somewhat more cautious.

lines.speaker: 과장
lines.en: I'd ask that you communicate that clearly to department heads. If it's left to rumor, morale will suffer.

lines.speaker: 행정팀장
lines.en: I'll distribute the detailed materials at next week's department heads meeting.

hospital-c1y-bioethics.title: Medical students debate a bioethics case

lines.speaker: 학생1
lines.en: This case study is about a patient refusing a blood transfusion for religious reasons. To what extent should medical staff respect that?

lines.speaker: 학생2
lines.en: I think patient autonomy should be respected in principle, as long as they're an adult with no impairment of judgment.

lines.speaker: 학생1
lines.en: But what if the decision is critical enough to directly determine life or death? What about the medical staff's ethical responsibility?

lines.speaker: 학생2
lines.en: They should try their best to persuade the patient, but ultimately I don't think medical staff have the authority to override the patient's wishes.

lines.speaker: 학생1
lines.en: Then what about a minor child's case—if the parents refuse the transfusion?

lines.speaker: 학생2
lines.en: That's a completely different issue. There are precedents where courts intervened and prioritized the child's right to life.

lines.speaker: 학생1
lines.en: So in the end, the line between autonomy and the protection of life gets drawn differently depending on the situation.

lines.speaker: 학생2
lines.en: Exactly. That's why these cases don't have a single correct answer—instead, they train us in a framework for judgment.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Complaints keep coming in that patients weren't properly informed about non-covered items—what's the hospital's position?

lines.speaker: 원무과장
lines.en: We follow the required prior-explanation procedure, but it's true there were cases where the explanation for some items fell short.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Specifically which items did the problems occur with?

lines.speaker: 원무과장
lines.en: They were mostly cases where real-time consent wasn't obtained when additional tests or special materials were used.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So do you have measures in place to prevent recurrence?

lines.speaker: 원무과장
lines.en: We plan to introduce an electronic consent system so that patients are notified in real time whenever an item is added.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: When do you expect that system to be introduced?

lines.speaker: 원무과장
lines.en: Once the internal review is complete, we plan to implement it within the next quarter.

hospital-c1y-mentalhealthgap.title: Generational views on mental health treatment

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: When I told my mother I was going to therapy, she just said, 'Can't you simply toughen your resolve?'

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: In the previous generation, receiving psychiatric care itself was often seen as something stigmatizing.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: At first, I hesitated too, because taking medication felt like admitting some kind of defeat.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Many people feel that way. But depression and anxiety disorders are conditions with biological factors, just like any other chronic illness.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Hearing that puts my mind a bit more at ease, though I'm still at a loss for how to explain it to my mother.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: If you'd like, you could bring your mother to the next appointment, and I could explain it to her directly.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: That would really help. Coming from a specialist, she might accept it a bit differently.

hospital-c1y-fundingpitch.title: Negotiating funding for a clinical trial

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: The phase 2 results for this clinical trial came back positive, so I'd like to request additional support to move into phase 3.

lines.speaker: 재단 관계자
lines.en: Glad to hear the positive results. But phase 3 will be much larger in scale—what's the estimated cost?

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: Since it'll expand into a multi-center trial, we estimate roughly three times the budget compared to before.

lines.speaker: 재단 관계자
lines.en: To persuade the board, we'll likely need more concrete grounds. Do you have plans to secure other sources of funding?

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: We've also separately applied for a government research grant, and the results will be announced next month.

lines.speaker: 재단 관계자
lines.en: In that case, it seems safer to finalize our support amount after the government funding results come out.

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: I understand. But since preparing for phase 3 itself takes time, could you at least start a preliminary review from now?

lines.speaker: 재단 관계자
lines.en: Yes, we'll go ahead and begin the preliminary review right away.

lines.speaker: 간호사1
lines.en: I have to cover twenty-two patients on the ward alone during tonight's shift—I'm not sure this is really safe.

lines.speaker: 간호사2
lines.en: I was in a similar situation last week too—it was already a struggle just to keep up with medication times.

lines.speaker: 간호사1
lines.en: If a medication error happens because of this, the responsibility will ultimately fall on us.

lines.speaker: 간호사2
lines.en: Right. The staffing standards themselves seem far too disconnected from reality.

lines.speaker: 간호사1
lines.en: I think we need to formally raise this issue, whether through the union or otherwise. It's no longer something individuals can bear.

lines.speaker: 간호사2
lines.en: I agree. How about we compile the staffing data and submit it at the next department meeting?

lines.speaker: 간호사1
lines.en: Good idea. If we show it with numbers, it'll be harder for management to ignore.

lines.speaker: 간호사2
lines.en: Let's make sure this doesn't fizzle out this time—let's see it through.

hospital-c2y-triagedebate.title: Debating triage priorities during a surge

lines.speaker: 응급의학과장
lines.en: There's a persistent disagreement between departments over how to adjust triage criteria during a surge in patients.

lines.speaker: 내과과장
lines.en: If we lower the priority of patients with worsening chronic conditions too much, we'll end up seeing more cases where the golden hour is missed.

lines.speaker: 응급의학과장
lines.en: I understand, but under conditions of limited resources, prioritizing patients with immediate life-threatening conditions is also the international standard.

lines.speaker: 내과과장
lines.en: That standard was designed with disaster scenarios in mind, so I question whether it's really valid to apply it identically to routine overcrowding as well.

lines.speaker: 응급의학과장
lines.en: Then whether we regard the current overcrowding as tantamount to a disaster is itself the crux of this debate, isn't it.

lines.speaker: 내과과장
lines.en: Exactly. And depending on that judgment, the entire hospital's philosophy of resource allocation is bound to change.

lines.speaker: 응급의학과장
lines.en: For now, I think the urgent priority is to convene a committee within this week and draft a provisional set of criteria.

lines.speaker: 내과과장
lines.en: I agree. But until the final criteria come out, I'd ask that clinical discretion in the field be respected.

lines.speaker: 응급의학과장
lines.en: Of course. This isn't meant to constrain frontline staff with regulations—it's meant to protect them, if anything.

hospital-c2y-epidemiology.title: A public health official presents an epidemiological report

lines.speaker: 보건 당국자
lines.en: I'll present the epidemiological investigation results for this cluster outbreak. The initial route of transmission has not yet been fully identified.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: There have been claims that the spread was faster than expected—wasn't there a problem with the initial response?

lines.speaker: 보건 당국자
lines.en: It's possible that the incubation period, which was observed to be shorter than expected, affected the speed of spread, and the initial contact tracing was carried out according to protocol.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Then do you have no plans to revise the protocol itself?

lines.speaker: 보건 당국자
lines.en: We're reviewing a revision to expand the scope of contact tracing based on this case, and it will go through an expert advisory meeting next month.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: How likely do you think it is that this will spread into community transmission?

lines.speaker: 보건 당국자
lines.en: As of now, the confirmed sources of infection are confined within a specific facility, but we don't judge it to be a stage where we can be complacent.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: If there's anything citizens should be particularly careful about, please tell us.

lines.speaker: 보건 당국자
lines.en: We ask that anyone who visited the facility report to the public health center regardless of symptoms, and that those classified as close contacts comply with the self-quarantine guidelines.

hospital-c2y-mediaethics.title: Editorial debate on covering a medical error

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: For this medical-error story, is it right to disclose the hospital's name? The investigation results aren't even finalized yet.

lines.speaker: 데스크
lines.en: Considering the public interest, citizens' right to know takes priority, but if we treat an unconfirmed matter as settled fact, there's also a risk of defamation.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: But if we anonymize it, the sense of alarm this incident is meant to raise could itself get diluted.

lines.speaker: 데스크
lines.en: That's true, but we also have to consider the side effect that our reporting could subject even innocent medical staff to trial by public opinion.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Then how about a compromise—disclose the hospital's name but keep the individual staff members' personal information private?

lines.speaker: 데스크
lines.en: That seems like a realistic balance. But until the investigation results come out, please consistently use the term 'allegation.'

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Understood, and we should also give the hospital's rebuttal equal weight.

lines.speaker: 데스크
lines.en: Of course. The moment we lose balance, the credibility of the report itself will be shaken.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Understood. I'll go ahead and request the hospital's official statement again first.

hospital-c2y-airesearch.title: Debating AI diagnostic tools in practice

lines.speaker: 의사1
lines.en: I heard the proposal to introduce the AI-assisted reading system finally passed at the board level.

lines.speaker: 의사2
lines.en: I'm still quite concerned. It's a structure where the algorithm's reasoning isn't fully transparent, yet the final responsibility rests entirely on the clinician.

lines.speaker: 의사1
lines.en: I agree on that point, but multiple papers have shown the reading accuracy itself approaches the level of experienced specialists.

lines.speaker: 의사2
lines.en: High accuracy doesn't resolve the question of liability for misdiagnosis. It's still unclear who's responsible for a finding missed due to a system error.

lines.speaker: 의사1
lines.en: In the end, isn't operating a dual-reading system, where AI is used only as an auxiliary tool, the realistic compromise?

lines.speaker: 의사2
lines.en: I agree with that direction too. But I think the real risk factor is that dependence will gradually increase over time.

lines.speaker: 의사1
lines.en: That's why I think a system for regularly reviewing error cases and feeding back the findings needs to run in parallel.

lines.speaker: 의사2
lines.en: I agree. Rather than rejecting the technology outright, establishing a framework to control it should come first.

lines.speaker: 의사1
lines.en: I should also propose separately tracking and sharing performance metrics for the first six months after implementation.

hospital-c2y-rareconsent.title: Debating consent for an experimental therapy

lines.speaker: 주치의
lines.en: Since we can no longer reasonably expect a response from standard treatment, I'd like to propose an experimental therapy.

lines.speaker: 보호자
lines.en: To what extent has that therapy's safety been verified? I've heard there aren't many clinical cases.

lines.speaker: 주치의
lines.en: A meaningful response rate has been reported in small-scale trials, but there isn't yet sufficient accumulated data on long-term side effects.

lines.speaker: 보호자
lines.en: If severe side effects occur, is there a way to reverse them?

lines.speaker: 주치의
lines.en: We can stop administration immediately and switch to symptomatic treatment, but I can't guarantee a full return to the original condition.

lines.speaker: 보호자
lines.en: May I ask what the patient herself thinks about this?

lines.speaker: 주치의
lines.en: The patient has already expressed a wish to take a chance on the remaining possibility. However, we'd like to obtain final consent only after you've had a thorough discussion with the family.

lines.speaker: 보호자
lines.en: Could you give us a few days to discuss it among ourselves?

lines.speaker: 주치의
lines.en: Of course. But since the treatment's efficacy is higher the earlier it starts before the disease progresses, I'd appreciate a decision within a week.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: There's criticism that funding for rare disease research is cut every year, while research sponsored by certain large corporations is receiving concentrated investment.

lines.speaker: 보건 당국자
lines.en: Budget allocation is the result of comprehensively considering patient numbers and social burden—it doesn't reflect any particular company's interests.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: But isn't the structure such that rare diseases are always pushed to lower priority precisely because of their small patient numbers?

lines.speaker: 보건 당국자
lines.en: To make up for that, we operate a separate fund dedicated to rare diseases, and this year's support was also modestly expanded.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: You said 'modestly expanded,' but accounting for inflation, isn't that effectively close to a freeze?

lines.speaker: 보건 당국자
lines.en: There's some validity to that point. We're consulting with the relevant departments to reflect a real increase in next year's budget proposal.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Can you tell us the specific scale or timing of the increase right now?

lines.speaker: 보건 당국자
lines.en: Since it hasn't been finalized, I'm cautious about giving specific figures, but we plan to finalize the direction before the National Assembly's budget review.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I hope you'll keep in mind that patient advocacy groups are continuing to watch this closely.

lines.speaker: 역학전문가
lines.en: As the national health screening program expands, I think the issue of overdiagnosis needs to be discussed alongside it.

lines.speaker: 임상의
lines.en: Isn't it an established fact that early detection improves survival rates? Overemphasizing overdiagnosis risks discouraging screening altogether.

lines.speaker: 역학전문가
lines.en: The problem is that improved survival isn't necessarily due to early detection alone. A considerable number of cases are reported where lesions that would never have progressed are detected and lead to unnecessary treatment.

lines.speaker: 임상의
lines.en: Even so, there's no reliable way for an individual physician to distinguish beforehand which lesions will progress and which won't.

lines.speaker: 역학전문가
lines.en: That's exactly why I'm arguing that a risk-stratified screening strategy makes more sense than a uniform, blanket screening approach.

lines.speaker: 임상의
lines.en: It sounds plausible in theory, but I question whether finely stratifying risk groups is realistically feasible in the field.

lines.speaker: 역학전문가
lines.en: There's no perfect model, but I believe there's considerably more room for improvement than the current uniform approach.

lines.speaker: 임상의
lines.en: In the end, this debate too is bound to remain at an impasse until enough evidence accumulates.

lines.speaker: 역학전문가
lines.en: That's why our research team is preparing to propose a long-term follow-up cohort study.

hospital-c2y-disclosurecrisis.title: Crisis meeting after disclosing a systemic error

lines.speaker: 병원장
lines.en: The internal investigation found that this medication-error incident stemmed not from a simple mistake, but from a structural flaw in the system.

lines.speaker: 품질관리팀장
lines.en: The core cause was identified as an interface issue in the electronic prescribing system, where similarly named drugs appear together.

lines.speaker: 병원장
lines.en: Then this isn't something that can simply be blamed entirely on the individual nurse's fault.

lines.speaker: 품질관리팀장
lines.en: That's right. However, there's a concern that publicly acknowledging this could also broaden the scope of the hospital's legal liability.

lines.speaker: 병원장
lines.en: Rather than trying to avoid responsibility and losing trust entirely, I believe it's right to acknowledge the structural flaw and announce prevention measures together.

lines.speaker: 품질관리팀장
lines.en: I agree. But I think we need to coordinate the wording with the legal team beforehand, to clearly separate the factual record from the acknowledgment of responsibility.

lines.speaker: 병원장
lines.en: I think it's only right that we personally explain this to the patient's family ourselves before the press announcement.

lines.speaker: 품질관리팀장
lines.en: I'll arrange a meeting with them today and also prepare a concrete draft of the recurrence-prevention plan.

lines.speaker: 병원장
lines.en: Let's use this incident as an opportunity to thoroughly re-examine the system as a whole.

hospital-c2y-consentwithdrawal.title: Debate after a research subject withdraws consent

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: In the middle of the phase 3 trial, one subject has suddenly expressed intent to withdraw consent.

lines.speaker: 임상연구간호사
lines.en: When I asked the reason, she said it wasn't the side effects themselves, but rather anxiety triggered by news coverage of a different clinical trial incident.

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: I understand, but if she withdraws at this point, it could affect the statistical power, which is concerning.

lines.speaker: 임상연구간호사
lines.en: Still, withdrawal of consent is an absolute right, so we can't pressure her to stay just because of our statistical concerns.

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: Of course. But it should still be fine to give her accurate information again regarding what she's worried about.

lines.speaker: 임상연구간호사
lines.en: I think that much is necessary. But the final decision has to be left entirely up to her.

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: Since this withdrawal could also affect other subjects, we'll need to carefully decide how to communicate it more broadly as well.

lines.speaker: 임상연구간호사
lines.en: I think it would be best to keep individual information strictly confidential and share only a summary of the overall safety indicators.

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: I agree. We should also report this case to the IRB to confirm there was no issue with the procedure.

hospital-c2y-culturaltaboo.title: Commentary on cultural taboos around terminal illness

lines.speaker: 완화의료 전문의
lines.en: In our society, there's still a deeply rooted tendency to hesitate about directly informing the patient of a terminal diagnosis.

lines.speaker: 사회복지사
lines.en: Families generally try to hide the truth for fear the patient will lose hope. I don't fail to understand that impulse either.

lines.speaker: 완화의료 전문의
lines.en: The problem is that this good intention actually deprives the patient of the opportunity to plan their own remaining time.

lines.speaker: 사회복지사
lines.en: That's true. There have been quite a few cases where patients, upon belatedly learning the truth, expressed a sense of betrayal.

lines.speaker: 완화의료 전문의
lines.en: That's why our approach is to first hold a family meeting, but ultimately persuade them to prioritize the patient's own wishes on whether to disclose.

lines.speaker: 사회복지사
lines.en: Still, we can't entirely ignore the cultural context either. Especially for elderly patients, some feel that preserving dignity means maintaining silence.

lines.speaker: 완화의료 전문의
lines.en: That's exactly the difficult part. Simply transplanting the Western model of autonomy wholesale isn't necessarily the right answer.

lines.speaker: 사회복지사
lines.en: In the end, we need to find a balance that takes into account both each family's culture and the individual patient's disposition.

lines.speaker: 완화의료 전문의
lines.en: That's why our hospital has also decided to strengthen a case-by-case counseling system instead of relying on a one-size-fits-all manual.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: With several rural hospitals closing, patients now have to travel more than two hours just to see a doctor.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: The government claims telemedicine can fill that gap—but is that realistic?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: In areas with poor internet infrastructure, even video consultations keep dropping, so it's hardly a fundamental solution.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Then why do you think doctors avoid working in rural areas in the first place?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: There's a pay gap, but the bigger factor is the isolation—having no colleagues to consult with in emergencies.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So you're saying it's not just about adding beds, but redesigning the medical workforce network.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Exactly. Rural healthcare can only be sustained if we build rotating staff systems and remote consultation networks together.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: That kind of reform would need significant funding—I worry it might keep getting deprioritized.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Since it's not a vote-winning policy, that concern is well founded. Still, we have to keep raising our voices.

lines.speaker: 통역사
lines.en: When immigrant patients describe symptoms, cultural context is often tangled in, so plain translation isn't always enough.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Can you give a specific example of when that becomes difficult?

lines.speaker: 통역사
lines.en: For instance, the phrase 'my chest feels stuffy' sometimes actually refers to depression—translating it literally can lead to a misdiagnosis.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: So you're not just a conduit for language—you're also acting as a cultural mediator.

lines.speaker: 통역사
lines.en: Yes, but I'm always careful not to cross that line. If my own interpretation intrudes too much, it can actually break trust.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: There's talk of the hospital expanding interpreter staff—do you personally feel the shortage?

lines.speaker: 통역사
lines.en: There's an absolute shortage of interpreters per language—some days I alone rotate between patients from several different language backgrounds.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: That kind of burden must affect the accuracy of the interpretation too.

lines.speaker: 통역사
lines.en: Right, that's why whenever an ambiguous expression comes up, I always go through a reconfirmation step with the patient.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: If the assisted-dying bill passes, it would give terminal patients like me a choice.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: It's true it would create a choice, but before the law takes effect, adequate safeguards against abuse need to be in place.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I believe I have the right to judge my own suffering. Why should the state decide that for me?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Your right to self-determination deserves respect, but we can't rule out the risk that depression or financial pressure could cloud that judgment.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: That's why the clause mandating psychiatric evaluation was included, I take it.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Yes, and there's also discussion of a dual-confirmation process requiring judgment from at least two independent doctors.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: The more complicated the procedure becomes, the harsher it might be on patients who actually have very little time left.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: That dilemma is still an unsolved challenge for us too. Balancing safety and dignity is genuinely difficult.

hospital-c1z-ethicistmediation.title: A hospital ethicist mediates a family dispute

lines.speaker: 윤리상담사
lines.en: Having heard both of you, it seems there's a significant disagreement over your father's course of treatment.

lines.speaker: 보호자1
lines.en: I think we should continue life-sustaining treatment. This isn't the stage to give up yet.

lines.speaker: 보호자2
lines.en: You haven't actually seen how much pain Father is in, unlike me. I can't bear to watch it any longer.

lines.speaker: 윤리상담사
lines.en: Did your father ever express his own wishes about a situation like this before?

lines.speaker: 보호자1
lines.en: I heard he filled out an advance directive a few years ago, but I've never actually looked at it closely.

lines.speaker: 윤리상담사
lines.en: Then confirming that document first seems like the most important starting point for narrowing the gap between your views.

lines.speaker: 보호자2
lines.en: And if the document doesn't state a clear wish, how should we decide then?

lines.speaker: 윤리상담사
lines.en: In that case, we'd need a family meeting to revisit together the values your father held dear in daily life.

lines.speaker: 보호자1
lines.en: It won't be easy, but I agree we need that kind of conversation instead of just letting emotions lead.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: The longer a new drug's patent protection lasts, the later generics arrive, which increases the burden on patients.

lines.speaker: 제약업계 관계자
lines.en: But if development costs can't be recovered, new drug development itself is bound to shrink in the first place.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: I understand that logic, but the practice of keeping prices high even after development costs are already recovered is hard to justify.

lines.speaker: 제약업계 관계자
lines.en: You shouldn't overlook the fact that follow-up research and side-effect monitoring costs continue as well.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Then wouldn't we need transparent cost disclosure to verify exactly what counts as a justified cost?

lines.speaker: 제약업계 관계자
lines.en: Cost disclosure is directly tied to trade secrets, so it's not easy for the industry to accept.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: In the end, this conflict comes down to a fundamental clash between patent protection and patient access to medicine.

lines.speaker: 제약업계 관계자
lines.en: That's right. Rather than a perfect solution, we'll need to keep searching for a compromise through social consensus.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: The biggest problem is that the three-shift rotation is too fast—our bodies barely adjust before the next shift starts.

lines.speaker: 수간호사
lines.en: I'm well aware of that difficulty. But if we lengthen the rotation cycle while short-staffed, gaps could appear during certain hours.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Then has hiring a dedicated night-shift-only staff been considered?

lines.speaker: 수간호사
lines.en: I already proposed it to the budget office, but they responded that approval isn't easy once night-shift allowances are factored in.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Looking at it long-term, we should also persuade them that lower turnover could actually save costs.

lines.speaker: 수간호사
lines.en: Good point. I'll rework the budget proposal to include the retraining costs caused by turnover as well.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: And if our input is reflected in advance when adjusting the rotation cycle, it would go much more smoothly.

lines.speaker: 수간호사
lines.en: Of course we should. Starting from the next meeting, I'll share the draft schedule in advance.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: If there's anything about the vaccination that worries you, please feel free to tell me.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I've seen a lot of side-effect reports online, so honestly I'm quite anxious.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: That anxiety is completely understandable. Would it be okay if we looked together at how well-verified those reports actually are?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Sure, but I don't fully trust it because I feel like medical staff downplay side effects.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: I don't think that distrust is baseless either. That's why our hospital publishes the side-effect statistics as they are, without alteration.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Then could you tell me specifically what the actual occurrence rate is?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Of course. Serious side effects occur in only a tiny fraction out of tens of thousands, and most reactions are mild, like soreness at the injection site.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: That does put me a bit more at ease. Still, I'd like to think it over for a few more days before deciding.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Of course you should. Please come back anytime if you have more questions.

lines.speaker: 연구자1
lines.en: Our paper didn't produce statistically significant results—I'm not sure whether we should even submit it to a journal.

lines.speaker: 연구자2
lines.en: That very attitude is what creates publication bias. Null results are just as important to the field as positive ones.

lines.speaker: 연구자1
lines.en: But since most journals prefer only positive results, it feels burdensome to spend time on a paper with low odds of publication.

lines.speaker: 연구자2
lines.en: That's why more journals have been adopting pre-registration systems that guarantee publication regardless of outcome.

lines.speaker: 연구자1
lines.en: I know such journals exist, but their impact factor is still low, so I worry it won't help my career.

lines.speaker: 연구자2
lines.en: Rather than immediate career concerns, isn't it a bigger problem in the long run if distorted evidence ends up shaping clinical guidelines?

lines.speaker: 연구자1
lines.en: Now that I hear it, I think my judgment was too skewed by personal interest.

lines.speaker: 연구자2
lines.en: I struggled with the same thing at first. But in the end, I'm glad I submitted mine.

hospital-c1z-firstresponder.title: The psychological toll on first responders

lines.speaker: 구급대원
lines.en: The scenes from when I couldn't save someone at an emergency scene don't easily fade from my mind.

lines.speaker: 상담사
lines.en: That kind of recurring intrusive memory is one of the typical symptoms of post-traumatic stress.

lines.speaker: 구급대원
lines.en: I felt like I couldn't show weakness in front of my colleagues, so I've just been enduring it alone.

lines.speaker: 상담사
lines.en: That organizational culture itself is what makes it harder to ask for help in the first place.

lines.speaker: 구급대원
lines.en: Exactly. I also worry that seeking counseling might put me at a disadvantage in field assignments.

lines.speaker: 상담사
lines.en: We need improvements toward strengthening anonymous counseling systems so that no such disadvantage occurs.

lines.speaker: 구급대원
lines.en: If such a system were actually put in place, I think I could ask for help with a much easier mind.

lines.speaker: 상담사
lines.en: Just by opening up like this today, you've already taken an important first step toward recovery.

hospital-c2z-insurancedenial.title: An insurer and doctor dispute a coverage denial

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: I received notice that this patient's targeted therapy has been excluded from coverage—could you explain the basis for that decision?

lines.speaker: 보험사 심사역
lines.en: Under clinical guidelines, there was no confirmed record of first-line standard treatment being tried, so it was withheld during review.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: That patient already showed severe adverse reactions to standard treatment, forcing a switch to an alternative therapy. It's documented in the medical record.

lines.speaker: 보험사 심사역
lines.en: That adverse-reaction record wasn't logged in our system's standard format, which is likely why it was automatically rejected.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: So you're saying the patient's treatment is being delayed over a formal paperwork gap—do you realize how unreasonable that is?

lines.speaker: 보험사 심사역
lines.en: I understand, but we don't have the authority to approve outside the rules on our own—you'd need to go through the formal appeals process.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: How long does an appeal typically take? Given the patient's condition, every day matters.

lines.speaker: 보험사 심사역
lines.en: It's usually about two weeks, but if you can demonstrate urgency, we can switch it to expedited review.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: I'll submit the urgency documentation right now. In return, I'd like at least an intake confirmation by the end of today.

lines.speaker: 보험사 심사역
lines.en: Yes, once you submit it, I'll personally verify it and get back to you by the end of the day.

hospital-c2z-triageAIethics.title: Debating who bears responsibility for AI triage errors

lines.speaker: 병원 행정가
lines.en: You've all seen the report on the incident where the AI triage system malfunctioned and misclassified a critical patient as low-risk, right?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Yes, fortunately the attending nurse manually double-checked and it didn't lead to a major incident, but it was a close call.

lines.speaker: 법무팀장
lines.en: If an actual incident had occurred, it would be ambiguous whether responsibility lies with the system developer, the hospital, or the medical staff who missed the final check.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: I was told AI was introduced only as an auxiliary tool, but in practice, everyone ends up trusting its judgment as-is.

lines.speaker: 병원 행정가
lines.en: That's exactly what's called 'automation bias'—treating what's meant to be just a tool as if it were the final decision-maker.

lines.speaker: 법무팀장
lines.en: The contract has wording that says 'for reference only,' which the developer used to leave room to avoid liability.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: So doesn't that mean all ultimate responsibility ends up shifted onto the medical staff? That seems deeply unfair.

lines.speaker: 병원 행정가
lines.en: That's why I believe we should use this incident as an opportunity to renegotiate the AI adoption contract to specify a shared-liability clause.

lines.speaker: 법무팀장
lines.en: I agree. But since the developer is unlikely to comply easily, we should map out a negotiation strategy in advance.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Separate from the negotiation, the immediate priority is making a mandatory double-check procedure to prevent similar incidents right away.

hospital-c2z-organallocation.title: A committee debates organ allocation criteria

lines.speaker: 이식외과의
lines.en: For this liver transplant candidate selection, there's an opinion that survival probability should take priority over waiting-list order.

lines.speaker: 윤리위원
lines.en: If we prioritize survival probability, wouldn't that create a structural unfairness where patients already in worse health keep getting pushed aside?

lines.speaker: 이식외과의
lines.en: Medically speaking, there's also a strong counterargument that allocating an organ to a patient with a low success probability is a waste of resources.

lines.speaker: 사회복지사
lines.en: The very phrase 'waste of resources' already gives the impression that a particular patient's life is being weighed on a scale.

lines.speaker: 윤리위원
lines.en: I agree with that point. First-come rotation may be inefficient, but at least it aligns with the principle of equity.

lines.speaker: 이식외과의
lines.en: Then how do you view a compromise model that combines waiting order and survival probability as weighted factors?

lines.speaker: 사회복지사
lines.en: The outcome would vary greatly depending on how the weights are set, so who decides those standards, and through what process, would be the key issue.

lines.speaker: 윤리위원
lines.en: At the very least, involving patient representatives and a citizen jury in that standard-setting process would help secure legitimacy.

lines.speaker: 이식외과의
lines.en: I think that's a reasonable proposal. I'll prepare a concrete weighting draft for the compromise model before the next meeting.

hospital-c2z-geneticdisclosure.title: Debating whether to disclose incidental genetic findings

lines.speaker: 유전상담사
lines.en: In this genetic test, an additional mutation unrelated to the original purpose was found, and I'm torn on whether to inform the patient.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: What kind of mutation is it? Whether it relates to a treatable condition seems like the key issue.

lines.speaker: 유전상담사
lines.en: It's a mutation linked to early-onset Alzheimer's, and there's currently no way to prevent or treat it.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Wouldn't disclosing information with no available treatment just place unnecessary psychological burden on the patient?

lines.speaker: 유전상담사
lines.en: But the patient has a right to know, and it could be important information for family planning or deciding the direction of their future life.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then shouldn't there be a prior consent process to check whether the patient is prepared to receive such information before disclosing it?

lines.speaker: 유전상담사
lines.en: Right. During pre-test counseling we should have explained the range of possible incidental findings and given the patient a choice, but that step was insufficient this time.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then it seems the right order now is to first re-explain that choice to the patient, even at this stage.

lines.speaker: 유전상담사
lines.en: Yes, I'll redo the process so the patient decides for themselves whether or not to be informed.

hospital-c2z-mentalhealthparity.title: Debating parity between mental and physical health coverage

lines.speaker: 정신과의사
lines.en: There's almost no limit on hospital stays for physical illnesses, so I don't understand why mental illness is uniquely subject to a strict cap on covered days.

lines.speaker: 보험 정책 담당자
lines.en: The system designers' position was that it's harder to objectively determine when treatment for mental illness has concluded.

lines.speaker: 정신과의사
lines.en: Isn't that just as true for chronic physical illness? Diabetes and hypertension don't have a concept of complete cure either.

lines.speaker: 보험 정책 담당자
lines.en: That's a fair point. Still, it's true that a more conservative approach has been taken with mental health coverage due to concerns about misuse.

lines.speaker: 정신과의사
lines.en: I suspect that very concern about misuse stems from the stigma surrounding mental illness in the first place.

lines.speaker: 보험 정책 담당자
lines.en: That's hard to deny. But if the cap is suddenly removed, financial projections could be significantly destabilized, so a phased approach is needed.

lines.speaker: 정신과의사
lines.en: Then shouldn't we at least start a pilot program that relaxes the cap first for the severe-illness group?

lines.speaker: 보험 정책 담당자
lines.en: If you submit a concrete pilot program proposal, I'll bring it up as an agenda item at the next policy meeting.

lines.speaker: 정신과의사
lines.en: Thank you. I hope this becomes an opportunity to properly address the parity issue.

hospital-c2z-clinicaltrialplacebo.title: Debating the ethics of a placebo-controlled trial

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: For this new drug trial, we're planning to design it as a double-blind study administering a placebo to the control group.

lines.speaker: 윤리위원
lines.en: Given that a standard treatment already exists for this condition, wouldn't using a placebo for the control group be ethically problematic?

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: It could be designed as a comparison with the standard treatment instead, but that makes it much harder to statistically demonstrate the drug's pure effect.

lines.speaker: 윤리위원
lines.en: Isn't sacrificing a patient's chance at treatment for the sake of statistical clarity putting things in the wrong order?

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: Instead, we plan to include an escape clause allowing control-group patients to switch to standard treatment immediately if their condition worsens.

lines.speaker: 윤리위원
lines.en: The key will be how quickly that escape clause actually functions in practice. It can't exist only on paper.

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: I agree. I'll have an independent safety monitoring committee check for signs of deterioration on a weekly basis.

lines.speaker: 윤리위원
lines.en: Then please be sure to include a procedure that transparently shares the committee's findings with the participants as well.

lines.speaker: 연구책임자
lines.en: Yes, I'll specify that sharing procedure in the participant consent form and resubmit the approval application.

hospital-c2z-nursingshortagepolicy.title: Debating whether to import foreign nursing labor

lines.speaker: 국회의원
lines.en: I'm preparing a bill to actively bring in foreign nursing labor to resolve the shortage of nursing staff.

lines.speaker: 간호협회 대표
lines.en: It would help ease the staffing crunch, but we shouldn't overlook the risk of medical errors arising from language and cultural differences.

lines.speaker: 국회의원
lines.en: That's why the bill includes a clause mandating a minimum one-year language and practical training course.

lines.speaker: 간호협회 대표
lines.en: Realistically, I think it's difficult to fully master the subtle nuances of clinical practice through a training course alone.

lines.speaker: 국회의원
lines.en: So you believe the fundamental solution is improving conditions for domestic nursing staff to prevent them from leaving in the first place.

lines.speaker: 간호협회 대표
lines.en: Exactly. Importing foreign labor is only a stopgap, and without improving working conditions, the same problem will keep repeating.

lines.speaker: 국회의원
lines.en: What about pursuing both in parallel—foreign labor in the short term, and improved conditions in the long term?

lines.speaker: 간호협회 대표
lines.en: I agree with that direction, but I'm concerned that without a concrete budget and timeline for improved conditions written into the bill, only the foreign-labor provision will end up surviving.

lines.speaker: 국회의원
lines.en: That's a valid concern. I'll consider revising the bill to also codify a concrete implementation plan for improved conditions.

lines.speaker: 데이터과학자
lines.en: If we train a disease-prediction model on the anonymized clinical data we've secured, we could significantly raise early-diagnosis rates.

lines.speaker: 개인정보보호책임자
lines.en: You said anonymized, but with rare-disease data, the risk of re-identifying an individual just from combining fields is quite high.

lines.speaker: 데이터과학자
lines.en: To lower that risk, we're applying differential privacy techniques to add noise to the data.

lines.speaker: 개인정보보호책임자
lines.en: If too much noise is added, doesn't model accuracy drop precisely for small-sample groups like rare-disease patients?

lines.speaker: 데이터과학자
lines.en: That's a fair point. Finding the right balance between privacy protection and model accuracy is our biggest challenge.

lines.speaker: 개인정보보호책임자
lines.en: Do you plan to incorporate the views of patient representatives or civic groups when determining that balance point?

lines.speaker: 데이터과학자
lines.en: Honestly, we haven't considered that step yet. We've truly only focused on technical optimization.

lines.speaker: 개인정보보호책임자
lines.en: Even if it's technically flawless, if it fails to earn social trust, the research itself could ultimately collapse.

lines.speaker: 데이터과학자
lines.en: I agree. As a next step, I'll form a patient advisory panel to gather input on privacy standards.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: What's bothering you?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I have a runny nose.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Since when?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Since this morning.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My throat hurts. Do you have any lozenges?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, try these.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How many a day should I take?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: About three a day.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I have a headache. Please give me some medicine.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Sure, here's some medicine.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Do I take it with water?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, take it with water.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Excuse me, where do I get a number?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Take one from that machine over there.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: ありがとうございます。

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, please have a seat and wait.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Where do I pay?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You can pay at that machine.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Can I use a card?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, cards work too.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I got a mosquito bite. Do you have any cream?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, here you go.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: It's very itchy — is that okay?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, put this on and it'll get better.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Please recommend a sunscreen.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: This one is popular.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Can I use it on my face?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, it's good for the face too.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I hurt my hand a little. Do you have band-aids?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, here you go.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How many should I put on?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: One is enough.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Excuse me, could I have some water?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Sure, here you go.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: ありがとうございます。

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Drink it slowly.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Where's the blood pressure machine?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's over there by the window.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Can I use it by myself?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, just sit and put your arm in.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Where's the restroom?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's at the end of the hallway.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Is it on the right?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, on the right.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Do you have masks?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, we have big and small ones.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: The small one, please.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: どうぞ。

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I have a cough. What's good for it?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: These drops are good.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How much is it?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: It's 3,000 won.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: What time are you open until today?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Until 6 p.m.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Are you open on Saturdays too?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, until the afternoon.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Could I borrow a thermometer?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Sure, here you go.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How do I use it?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Put it in your ear and press the button.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My nose has been running for a while, and I can't tell if it's a cold or an allergy.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Have you had a fever?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: No, no fever.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then it's likely an allergy. Did you clean recently?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Yes, I shook out my blanket yesterday.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: That's probably it. I'll give you allergy medicine.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: How did you get hurt?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I fell on the stairs and sprained my ankle.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: It's quite swollen. Can you walk?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I can walk slowly.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Let's take an X-ray first.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Okay — it's not broken, is it?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'm taking a boat next week — do you have motion-sickness pills?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, take it a few hours before.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How long before should I take it?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: An hour before is best.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Does it make you sleepy?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, it can make you a bit drowsy.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'd like a flu shot — do I need to make an appointment?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, today's slots are all full.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Then is tomorrow possible?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, tomorrow morning works.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Please book a time then.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll set it for 10 o'clock.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Let's check your blood pressure. Give me your arm.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Sure, it's felt a bit high lately.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: It came out at 140 over 90.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Is that high?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: A little high. Try cutting down on salty food.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My shoulder keeps hurting, so I'd like physical therapy.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: How many times a week can you come?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I can come about twice.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then I'll set it for Tuesdays and Thursdays.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Please make it in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, I've set it for 3 p.m.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My eyes get very dry when I wear contacts.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: About how many hours a day do you wear them?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Over ten hours.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then cut down the hours and use artificial tears.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How many times a day should I use the tears?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: You can use them whenever you need to.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Something red appeared on my arm. It's itchy.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Has anything changed recently?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I bought a new detergent.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: That could be the cause. I'll give you an ointment.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Should I stop using that detergent?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Yes, don't use it for a few days.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My back has been hurting lately.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Do you sit a lot at work?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Yes, I sit all day.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Get up and walk every hour.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Do I not need medicine?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Try stretching first.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My ear has hurt since I went swimming yesterday.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Do you think water got in?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Yes, it feels like the water hasn't drained.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Let me take a look. Turn your ear this way.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Is it very swollen?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I woke up and my neck won't turn.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Since when has it been like that?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Since this morning.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Isn't your pillow too high?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: It might be.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Apply a warm compress and try a lower pillow.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My stomach has hurt ever since I ate out yesterday.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: How many times did you go to the bathroom?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Five times just today.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: It could be food poisoning. Drink plenty of water.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Should I avoid spicy food?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Yes, eat bland food for a few days.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I feel dizzy every time I stand up.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Do you skip breakfast?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Yes, I've been too busy to eat lately.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: That could be the cause. Please make sure to eat.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Would drinking a lot of water help too?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Yes, it helps.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I've been getting nosebleeds often lately.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: About how many times a week?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: About three times.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: The dry air could be causing it.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Should I use a humidifier?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Yes, keeping one on should help.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: The spot I got bitten a few days ago has swollen more.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Where were you bitten?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My ankle. Now it even feels hot.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: It looks infected. I'll give you a stronger medicine.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How many days should I take it?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Take it for five days and come back.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My stomach hurts and then feels fine, on and off. It's not constant.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: When does it usually hurt? Is it related to meals?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: It seems to start about an hour after I eat.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Does it get worse when you eat spicy food?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Now that you mention it, maybe. I'm not sure, though.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: If you keep a food diary for about a week, it'll be easier to find the cause.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Do I really need to take this medicine with food?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes — on an empty stomach it can cause stomach irritation.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Then is it better before or after eating?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Right after a meal is best.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: If I forget a dose, can I take a double dose next time?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: No, absolutely not. Just take the normal amount at the next scheduled time.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'd like to move my appointment next Tuesday to another day.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Did something come up?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: A business trip came up suddenly.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then how about this Friday?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: That day, only the morning works for me.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll move it to 10 o'clock.

hospital-b1x-nodrowsy.title: Medicine that won't make you drowsy

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Does this medicine make you drowsy? I have to drive in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Yes, this ingredient can cause drowsiness.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Could you switch me to something that won't make me drowsy?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: It might be a bit less effective, but I'll switch it.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: That's fine — driving safely matters more to me.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then I'll prescribe this one instead.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Could I get a printout of my past vaccination records?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, could you tell me your name and date of birth?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'm studying abroad next month and need to submit it to my school.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then I'll print it in English as well.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Can I find out if I'm missing any vaccinations?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, the doctor will check the record and let you know.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'm traveling to Southeast Asia next month — what should I prepare?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Which country, and how long will you be there?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'll be in Vietnam for about ten days.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then it's good to bring anti-malarial medicine and something for diarrhea.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Do I also need any vaccinations beforehand?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: I recommend the hepatitis A vaccine. Get it at least two weeks before you leave.

hospital-b1x-recurringback.title: Booking therapy for a recurring back problem

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: The back I injured before has been hurting again lately.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Have you continued physical therapy since then?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: No, I stopped once it felt better.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: That area tends to relapse, so it's important to manage it consistently.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How long should I go this time?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Let's start with about two months, twice a week.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Could I get a doctor's note to submit to my company?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Sure, I'll note how many days you need to rest.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Would two days be enough? I need to be back at work starting Monday.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Given your symptoms, I think three days of rest would be better.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Then please make it three days.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Okay, you can pick it up at the front desk.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'm currently taking blood-pressure medicine — is it okay to take this cold medicine along with it?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Could you tell me the name of your blood-pressure medicine?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I don't know the exact name, but it's a white pill.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Could you show me the medicine packet, then?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Hold on, I have a photo of it saved.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: I checked — this cold medicine is fine to take together.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Did you finish the medicine I prescribed last week?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Yes, I finished it, but it hasn't really improved.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: How's the cough or fever?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: The cough has lessened, but my nose keeps running.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then it could be sinusitis, so let's take an image to check.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: It's taking longer than I expected.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Is there a cheaper version of this medicine?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, there's a generic with the same ingredients.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Does it work just the same?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: The ingredients and effect are identical — only the price is lower.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Then please switch me to that one.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Sure, I'll check with the doctor and switch it.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Since your stomach has kept hurting, I think we should do an ultrasound.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Is it possible today?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: You need to be fasting — have you eaten?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I ate this morning.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then come in tomorrow morning while fasting.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Can I not even drink water?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: A little water is fine, but don't drink too much.

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: You're all done with the injection. Please wait here for about twenty minutes.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Why do I need to wait?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: It's to check for any unexpected reaction.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Is it okay to exercise today?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Avoid intense exercise — just a light walk is fine.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Got it. What should I do if something feels off?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I want to go to the dermatology department at a bigger hospital — could I get a referral letter?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Which hospital are you planning to go to?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I haven't decided yet, but I'm thinking of a university hospital.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then I'll leave the hospital name blank and write it up.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: When can I get it?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: It'll be ready in about thirty minutes.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My child is five — how much of this medicine should I give?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: About how much does your child weigh?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'm not exactly sure, but roughly 18 kilograms.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Then half a spoon, three times a day, should be right.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Can it be given regardless of meals?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Yes, just keep the timing consistent.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How long do I have to wait? My pain is fairly severe.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: There are three people ahead of you right now.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Would it be possible to see me sooner?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Could I ask a bit more about your symptoms?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My side has suddenly started stabbing with pain.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: In that case, I'll move you up in the order.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I get migraines two or three times a month, and they seem to be getting worse over time.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: When the pain comes, do you also get sensitivity to light or nausea?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Yes, it worsens with light, so I have to lie down somewhere dark.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: In that case, we could try two things together — a daily preventive medicine and an acute medicine you only take when symptoms start.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'm a little worried about side effects from a daily medicine.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Drowsiness is the common side effect, but starting at a low dose and increasing gradually usually works out fine.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Then I'd like to try starting at a low dose.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'd like to know beforehand whether this test is covered by insurance before I decide.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If it's a general health checkup, most of it is uncovered and out-of-pocket costs are high.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Then what if I'm having it done because of actual symptoms?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: In that case, if there's a medical record, it can be processed as a covered item.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I actually saw a doctor for similar symptoms last month.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll check that record and let you know if it applies.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Please contact me once you have the result, then.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: It's been over a month since I started physical therapy — when should I expect to see results?

lines.speaker: 치료사
lines.en: Looking at your progress so far, the recovery has been on the slower side.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Am I doing something wrong?

lines.speaker: 치료사
lines.en: It's more about how consistently you're doing the stretches at home.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Honestly, there are stretches I skip for a few days sometimes.

lines.speaker: 치료사
lines.en: Then please make sure to do at least ten minutes, twice a day. That alone makes a big difference.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Understood. I'll really stick to it this time.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: For months now, no matter how much I sleep, the fatigue won't go away.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: About how many hours do you sleep?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I sleep about seven hours, but I never feel refreshed in the morning.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Do you snore, or ever feel like you're gasping for air while asleep?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My family has said I snore heavily.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then it'd be good to first check for sleep apnea, along with a blood test.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How does that test work?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: You stay overnight at the hospital while readings are taken.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: The last medicine worked well, but it really irritated my stomach.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then shall I switch you to one that's gentler on the stomach, even if it's a bit less effective?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How much of a difference is there?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: The pain relief is similar, but it takes a bit longer to kick in.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: That seems fine to me. The stomach pain has been harder to deal with.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Just be sure to take it after meals — never on an empty stomach.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Okay, I'll keep that in mind.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Is there any food I shouldn't eat while taking this medicine?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: You should avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice — the medicine's effect can become too strong.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: What about alcohol? I have a gathering next week.

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: It's best to avoid it if possible, and if you do drink, keep it to one or two glasses.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Is coffee okay?

lines.speaker: 약사
lines.en: Coffee's fine, but wait at least thirty minutes after taking the medicine.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Understood. I'll be careful about it.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I got hurt while working, and I need paperwork for a workers' compensation claim.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Could you tell me more details about how the accident happened?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I hit my knee while moving boxes in the warehouse.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then you'll need to bring a workers'-comp confirmation form from your company before we can issue the medical certificate.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Can I get that form from the person in charge at my company?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, you should be able to request it from HR.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Understood. I'll come back once I have it.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: In this test, your cholesterol level went up even more than last time.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I thought I'd been careful with my diet.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Could I ask specifically what you've been eating?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I cut back on greasy food, but I haven't really managed to stop eating late at night.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Late-night eating has a bigger impact than you'd think. And are you exercising?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Barely at all. I don't have the time.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Try starting with even fifteen minutes of walking a day. Let's check again at your next test.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Okay, I'll really try this time.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: For the past few weeks it's been really hard for me to fall asleep.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: What thoughts tend to come up when you lie down?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: The next day's tasks keep coming to mind, so my head never rests.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Has your workload increased recently, or is there something stressing you out?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Yes, my work increased a lot after I switched departments.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: I can help short-term with sleep medication, but fundamentally you'll need to adjust your workload.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: For now, I'd like to start with the medication.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Okay, I'll give you a two-week supply — let's see if things improve in that time.

hospital-b2x-travelvaccine.title: Vaccine side effects before international travel

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I leave the country next week — is it okay to get vaccinated now, or should I worry about side effects?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Usually there can be a mild fever or body aches for a day or two.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: What if it overlaps with my departure date?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: That's why we recommend getting it at least five days beforehand.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: If I get it today, that leaves exactly a week — would that be okay?

lines.speaker: 간호사
lines.en: Yes, that gives you plenty of margin.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Understood. I'll get it done today, then.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Ever since I started running, my knee makes a noise and hurts.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Did you suddenly increase your running distance or frequency?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Yes, I went from 5 kilometers to 15 within a month.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: That sudden increase is very likely the cause. You'll need to rest for about two weeks first.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Can I do other exercise while resting?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Low-impact exercise like swimming is fine.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How should I approach running again once I start back up?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: The rule of thumb is to increase distance gradually, never more than ten percent a week.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: This medicine needs to be taken three times a day, but I work night shifts, so timing is hard to manage.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: What are your working hours?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I work from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then it'd be better to take it every eight hours rather than matching it to mealtimes.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: So before my shift, during it, and after it ends?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Yes, that pattern should suit your schedule. Setting alarms will make it easier.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Understood. I'll try that.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I heard it's a simple procedure, but I'm still a bit nervous.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: I can tell you're quite tense. What part worries you the most?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I'm worried it'll hurt when the anesthesia goes in, and how much it'll hurt afterward.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: The anesthesia is just a small pinch, and afterward you'll only feel slight discomfort for a day or two.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Can I go about my normal life right away?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Light activity is fine from the same day — you'd just need to avoid strenuous activity for about two days.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Hearing that explanation puts my mind at ease a bit.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Which is more accurate — an MRI or a CT scan? I'm also curious about the cost difference.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: MRI is more accurate for soft tissue, but it's much more expensive.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Specifically, how much of a difference is there?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: It depends on insurance coverage, but it could differ by three or four times.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: For my symptoms, would a CT scan be enough?

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Since we suspect a bone issue, starting with a CT should be fine.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Then let's start with that first.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: My stomach has felt bloated for months, and I don't think I've eaten anything in particular that's wrong.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Is there a particular time of day or situation when it gets worse?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Now that I think about it, it seems especially bad on days I have meetings.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Then it could be stress-related rather than food-related. Do you drink coffee often?

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I do end up drinking more coffee when I'm tense.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: Caffeine can increase stomach acid and worsen the symptoms. Try cutting back on those days.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: Then I'll start by cutting back on coffee.

lines.speaker: 의사
lines.en: If it still doesn't improve, let's consider an endoscopy as well.

hospital-b2x-copayestimate.title: Estimating the cost of seeing a specialist

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: How much would it cost to see an orthopedic specialist? I'd like to know beforehand.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It depends on whether this would be a first visit or a follow-up.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: It'd be my first time. I do have a referral letter from my current clinic.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Having a referral letter reduces your out-of-pocket cost somewhat.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: So roughly how much should I expect?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Just the consultation is around 20,000 won, but it can be more if additional tests are needed.

lines.speaker: 환자
lines.en: I suppose I won't know what tests are needed until I actually go?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: That's right. The doctor will let you know after the examination.

lines.speaker: 총지배인
lines.en: The post that went up yesterday has already crossed a hundred thousand views?

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: Yes, it's a video pointing out a room hygiene issue, and the reaction is far more intense than expected.

lines.speaker: 총지배인
lines.en: We need to verify the facts first. Could you pull the cleaning log for that room?

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: I already checked, and it turns out the staff member did miss one item on the checklist by mistake.

lines.speaker: 총지배인
lines.en: Then rather than making excuses, we should acknowledge it and apologize, and announce prevention measures at the same time.

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: I'll contact the guest individually to offer a refund along with a sincere apology.

lines.speaker: 총지배인
lines.en: Please keep monitoring the comments too, and if needed, let's review the entire cleaning process.

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: Yes, I think this incident is a good opportunity to switch the checklist to a double-verification system.

lines.speaker: 총지배인
lines.en: Good idea. Turning a crisis into an opportunity for improvement is ultimately the shortcut to rebuilding trust.

lines.speaker: 수익관리팀장
lines.en: Raising rates in real time to match demand during peak season has long been the industry standard.

lines.speaker: 지배인
lines.en: I understand, but from a guest's perspective who sees the price double right after booking, they can't help but feel betrayed.

lines.speaker: 수익관리팀장
lines.en: That's a misunderstanding. It's not that the rate of an already confirmed booking changes; it only applies to the remaining rooms.

lines.speaker: 지배인
lines.en: Even so, it's hard for consumers to understand that structure precisely. It's understandable that criticism about lack of transparency arises.

lines.speaker: 수익관리팀장
lines.en: Then how about capping the range of the rate fluctuation and clearly stating a notice on the booking page?

lines.speaker: 지배인
lines.en: With that level of compromise, I think guests could accept it. Though we should make an exception for extreme cases like local festival periods.

lines.speaker: 수익관리팀장
