phone-b1x-hotel-late-checkin.title: Asking a hotel about a late check-in

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I have a reservation, but my flight is delayed so I'll arrive after midnight.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: That's fine, we have a 24-hour front desk.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's a relief. But the room stays reserved, right?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, just give me the name on the reservation and it'll be fine.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Lee Jihoon. I'll call again if it gets even later.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, take your time getting here.

phone-b1x-cafe-wallet-missing.title: Cafe can't find the wallet right away

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'd like to check again about a wallet I left there yesterday afternoon.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: One moment, I'll look. I'm sorry, but I don't see it here.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Really? I definitely sat by the window.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The cleaning staff might have set it aside separately. Let me look into it more.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, please do. I'll leave my number.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, I'll call you as soon as I find it.

phone-b1x-sick-workload.title: Calling in sick and handing off work

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Team lead, I'm sorry, but I need to see a doctor today so I don't think I can come in.

lines.speaker: 팀장
lines.en: That's fine, but who's preparing today's meeting materials?

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: I finished them yesterday and already sent them by email.

lines.speaker: 팀장
lines.en: Ah, I checked it. Then don't worry and get some rest.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Thank you. I think I'll be able to come in tomorrow.

lines.speaker: 팀장
lines.en: Okay, take care of yourself first.

phone-b1x-gym-freeze.title: Asking to pause a gym membership

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I was going to cancel my membership, but I'm wondering if I can just pause it.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, if there's a reason like a work trip or an injury, a pause is possible.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'm going on an overseas business trip next month. Can I pause it for a month?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, just send us proof of the trip and we'll process it.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Got it, then I won't cancel after all.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Great, please send the proof by text.

phone-b1x-landlord-noise-complaint.title: Reporting noisy neighbors to the landlord

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Hello, sorry to bother you, but I'm calling because the upstairs unit is very noisy every night.

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Ah, I see. Since when has this been happening?

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: About a week. I can hear footsteps until dawn.

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: I'll ask them to be quieter.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Thank you. If it continues, may I contact you again?

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Of course, feel free to reach out anytime.

phone-b1x-door-code-guest.title: Guiding a courier through a new building layout

lines.speaker: 기사님
lines.en: Hello, this building is split into two sections and I'm getting confused.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Ah, I'm in Building A. Come to the left from the main entrance.

lines.speaker: 기사님
lines.en: Left? I don't see a sign clearly from here.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: There should be a small door next to the convenience store — come in through there.

lines.speaker: 기사님
lines.en: Ah, found it. What's the door code?

phone-b1x-pharmacy-insurance.title: Asking the pharmacy about insurance coverage

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'm wondering if my prescribed medicine is covered by insurance.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It depends on the type of prescription — could you tell me which medicine it is?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'm not sure — the name was kind of long.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then could you send a photo of the prescription by text?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Sure, I'll send it right now.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: As soon as I get it, I'll check and call you back.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'd like to order a birthday cake — can you add a message on it?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's possible. What message would you like?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Please write 'Happy birthday, Jihoon'.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Got it. What size would you like, in inches?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's for six people — which size would be right?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then eight inches should be enough. When will you pick it up?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'll come at three tomorrow afternoon.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'd like to use your laundry pickup service — is today possible?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Today's already closed out, but tomorrow morning is available.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then would around nine tomorrow work?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's fine. Do you also have bedding or large laundry?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I have two comforters.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then the price might be a bit higher. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, that's fine. Please schedule it for nine.

phone-b2x-pizza-allergy.title: Asking about allergens before ordering pizza

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I have something I'd like to ask before I order.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, go ahead.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I have a nut allergy — does the dough contain any nuts?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The dough itself doesn't contain any, but since other menu items are made in the same kitchen, we can't guarantee complete separation.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I see. Could you at least use separate utensils?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that we can do. I'll add a note about the allergy to your order.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. Then I'll order one pepperoni pizza.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Hello, I'd like to come pick up the laptop I left last week.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, but we do have an identity verification process, so you'll need to bring ID.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Ah, could I just describe what's inside the laptop instead? I left my ID at home.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry, but based on our policy, that alone won't be enough.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Then I'll come again tomorrow with my ID instead of today.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that would be the safest option. We're open until eight in the evening.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Understood, see you tomorrow.

phone-b2x-table-dietary.title: Reserving a table with dietary requests

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'd like to book for this Saturday evening, and I have a request in advance.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, go ahead.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: One of my guests is vegetarian — does the course menu have a vegetarian option?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The standard course is mostly meat, but we can prepare a separate vegetarian course instead.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Oh, that's great. Is the price the same?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it's the same. I'll note down one vegetarian guest for the reservation.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. Then please book for four people at seven.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'm calling about the jacket you said you'd hold for me last week.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it's still safely kept.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Good to hear. But I saw it cheaper at another store — could you possibly match the price?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We don't have our own discount policy, but I can check with headquarters.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Please do. About when can I get an answer?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I should be able to let you know by tomorrow morning.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood. You'll keep holding the jacket until then, right?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I have some questions about my cat's neutering surgery.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, go ahead.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Can I feed her the day before surgery, or should she fast?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: From midnight on the day of surgery, both water and food are off-limits. Up until the evening before is fine.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood. I'm also curious how long the surgery takes.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Usually about thirty minutes, but including recovery you'll need to leave her for about half a day.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay, then I'll drop her off early in the morning.

phone-b2x-moving-insurance.title: Asking a moving company about damage insurance

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'd like to ask one more thing about the quote I got before.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, go ahead.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What happens if furniture gets damaged during the move?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Damage compensation insurance is included by default, but for high-value items you need to declare them separately to be covered.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: We have a piano at home — how do I declare that?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll add it as a line item on the quote — but the transport fee will be a bit higher.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's fine, safety comes first, so please add it.

phone-b2x-flight-standby.title: Requesting standby on an earlier flight

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'd like to ask if I can switch to a flight two hours earlier than mine.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: That time slot's flight is already fully booked.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then could you at least put me on the waitlist?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's possible. Just be aware that being on the waitlist doesn't guarantee a seat.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood. If it doesn't work out, I'll just take my original flight.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, I'll text you right away if it's confirmed.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. How many hours before departure will I know?

phone-b2x-hotel-early-checkin.title: Requesting an early check-in at a hotel

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'm staying next week, and I'd like to ask if I can move my check-in earlier.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: What time would you like?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I think I'll arrive around ten in the morning — could I get the room right then?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Official check-in is from 3 pm, so I can't guarantee it, but I'll call you as soon as the room is ready.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then can I at least drop off my luggage before that?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's possible anytime. Just leave it at the front desk.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood, I'll do that.

phone-b2x-cafe-wallet-dispute.title: Disputing what was left in a found wallet

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, thank you for finding my wallet, but it seems like some of the cash inside is missing.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We kept it exactly as it was when we found it — how much do you think is missing?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: About 10,000 won short, I think. Though I'm not totally sure.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If you're not certain, it's hard for us to verify, but I'll go ahead and check the CCTV.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I'd appreciate that.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll check and get back to you by tomorrow.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood, I'll wait.

phone-b2x-sick-deadline.title: Calling in sick while a deadline looms

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Team lead, I'm sorry, but I'm not feeling well — could I switch to working from home today?

lines.speaker: 팀장
lines.en: Sure, but what about the report that's due today?

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: I can finish it during the morning and send it by email.

lines.speaker: 팀장
lines.en: Are you sure you'll be okay? Don't push yourself too hard.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Yes, I think I can manage that much. I'll rest once it's done.

lines.speaker: 팀장
lines.en: Okay. After the deadline, turn off the computer and get proper rest.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: ありがとうございます。

phone-b2x-gym-refund-dispute.title: Pushing back on a gym's no-refund policy

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I requested a membership refund, but I was told it's not allowed under the terms, so I'm calling again.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Right, we explained that refunds are difficult after ten days from registration.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: But I was never informed of that clause when I signed up.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's stated at the bottom of the contract, but if the staff member didn't explain it, that's on us.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Right, nobody pointed that section out when I signed.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Understood — as an exception, I'll process a partial refund this time.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. How many days will processing take?

phone-b2x-landlord-repair-cost.title: Negotiating repair costs with the landlord

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Hello, I have something to ask about the repair cost from the leak last time.

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Yes, did you receive the bill?

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Yes, but it says the tenant is responsible for the cost — isn't this an issue from the building's age?

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Hmm, checking again, it does seem like the pipes themselves being old caused it.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Then I think the repair cost should be the landlord's responsibility.

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Alright, I'll cover this one. Please ignore the bill.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Thank you. I hope there won't be issues like this going forward.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I missed my appointment last week and I'm calling because a no-show fee was charged.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, checking here, we sent a text reminder the day before the appointment.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I didn't see that text — I was rushed to the hospital myself.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Ah, if that's the case, you should have told us. Do you have something like a doctor's note?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I have one. I can send it by text.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then after we confirm it, I'll cancel the fee.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you, I'll send it right now.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I arrived yesterday but my suitcase still hasn't shown up.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry — could you give me your baggage tag number?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, here it is. I'm worried because there are important documents inside.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I checked, and it was mistakenly loaded onto a different flight. It's expected to arrive tonight.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What about the things I need in the meantime? Is there compensation?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, if you keep the receipts for essential items, we'll cover part of the cost.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood, I'll be sure to keep the receipts.

phone-b2x-cafe-stale-pastry.title: Complaining about a stale pastry by phone

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, I'm calling because the croissant I bought this morning was quite stale.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Ah, I'm sorry. Do you have the receipt?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I do. But I already ate about half of it — is that still okay?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's fine. Just bring the receipt and we'll exchange it for a fresh one.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you. Is it okay if I come later today?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, anytime before we close is fine.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then I'll stop by in the evening.

phone-b2x-landlord-early-termination.title: Asking the landlord about ending the lease early

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Hello, I suddenly got transferred to another region, so I wanted to ask if I could end the lease early.

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: There are still six months left on the contract, so a penalty fee may apply.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: I understand that, but what if I find a new tenant myself?

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Oh, if you do that, I can waive the penalty fee.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: That's a relief. Then I'll ask someone I know first.

lines.speaker: 집주인
lines.en: Sure, but we'll still handle the screening.

lines.speaker: 나
lines.en: Understood, I'll contact you as soon as I find someone.

restaurant-c1y-menu-change.title: Defending a menu overhaul to a regular

lines.speaker: 단골
lines.en: The old menu felt so much more familiar — why change everything so suddenly?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Familiarity matters, but sourcing got unstable, so I had no choice but to make changes.

lines.speaker: 단골
lines.en: Still, it's a bit disappointing that the yukgaejang I've eaten for over ten years is gone.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: I completely understand that feeling. Instead, I've prepared a new spicy soup dish rooted in the same tradition — would you like to try it?

lines.speaker: 단골
lines.en: Hmm, it's unfamiliar but the aroma is similar.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: I'd like you to think of it not as abandoning familiarity, but as building something new on top of it.

lines.speaker: 단골
lines.en: That sounds reasonable in theory, but ultimately it'll come down to how customers react.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Exactly. That's why I'm running a month-long tasting period and plan to keep incorporating feedback.

lines.speaker: 단골
lines.en: With that much effort, I suppose it's worth trusting.

restaurant-c1y-tipping-culture.title: Debating whether to import tipping culture

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Lately the younger staff keep asking whether we should introduce American-style tipping.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: Honestly I'm skeptical. We already charge a service fee, so it'd essentially be double-charging.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That's true, but there's also a point to the argument that we need incentives to retain skilled staff.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: If it's about incentives, wouldn't restructuring a performance-pay system be better than tips? Tipping just shifts the burden onto customers.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That criticism about shifting the burden is fair, but lately foreign customers actually seem awkward about the absence of tipping.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: That's just a cultural difference — I don't think we need to accommodate it.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That makes sense. Let's start by fixing the performance-pay system and hold off on tipping a bit longer.

restaurant-c1y-sommelier-pairing.title: A sommelier explains a pairing philosophy

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Why are you recommending a red wine with this fish dish? That seems counterintuitive.

lines.speaker: 소믈리에
lines.en: It goes against conventional wisdom, but this dish has a soy-based sauce, so a soft-tannin red actually pairs well.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Doesn't tannin tend to amplify the fishy taste?

lines.speaker: 소믈리에
lines.en: That happens when tannin meets fat. But this fish is low in fat, and the sauce's umami is strong enough to balance it out.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Now that I hear it, it does sound logical, but part of me still wants to play it safe with white.

lines.speaker: 소믈리에
lines.en: White is certainly a safe choice too. I just wanted to offer you a bolder experience today.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: All right, let's take the adventure. But I'll be honest if it doesn't work.

lines.speaker: 소믈리에
lines.en: I welcome that. We believe that kind of feedback is what drives the menu forward.

restaurant-c1y-authenticity-debate.title: Two food writers argue over fusion authenticity

lines.speaker: 기자A
lines.en: This fusion kimchi taco — doesn't it feel ambiguously identity-less? Neither one thing nor the other.

lines.speaker: 기자B
lines.en: I disagree. I see it as two traditions meeting to create a new grammar altogether.

lines.speaker: 기자A
lines.en: But doesn't that 'new grammar' end up erasing the original context?

lines.speaker: 기자B
lines.en: I'd rather say it expands the context rather than erasing it. The fermentation principle of kimchi is still intact.

lines.speaker: 기자A
lines.en: Just because the fermentation principle survives doesn't guarantee authenticity. Consumers might end up misunderstanding the original.

lines.speaker: 기자B
lines.en: Isn't that leaving room for reinterpretation rather than misunderstanding? Every cuisine has ultimately been transformed somewhere along the way.

lines.speaker: 기자A
lines.en: That's fair, but if the pace of transformation is too fast, there's also a risk of losing one's roots.

lines.speaker: 기자B
lines.en: In the end we're both worried about the same thing — the balance between speed and respect.

restaurant-c1y-labor-costs.title: Discussing labor costs with a journalist

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: With the minimum wage rising, what practical burdens has that placed on running the restaurant?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: With labor costs exceeding thirty percent of revenue, it's become a structure where we can't survive without raising menu prices.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: But raising prices also risks losing customers, doesn't it?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Right. So instead of raising prices, we chose to simplify the menu and deploy kitchen staff more efficiently.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: From the employees' perspective, wouldn't that intensify their workload?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That concern is real, so instead we made work hours more flexible and introduced performance-based bonuses.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So in the end, the minimum wage increase became an occasion to change how the whole operation runs.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: You've put it exactly right. It was a burden, but in hindsight it was also a chance to improve our fundamentals.

restaurant-c1y-vip-complaint.title: Mentoring a new server on a VIP complaint

lines.speaker: 신입
lines.en: That customer just now got angry because we seated them twenty minutes past their reservation, and I don't know how to respond.

lines.speaker: 선배
lines.en: First, it's important not to start with excuses. Before explaining the reason, you have to clearly apologize for the inconvenience first.

lines.speaker: 신입
lines.en: Won't the customer get angrier if I just apologize? I feel like they'd want to know the reason.

lines.speaker: 선배
lines.en: The order matters — apologize, briefly explain the reason, then offer what you can do to make up for it. For example, offering a complimentary welcome dessert.

lines.speaker: 신입
lines.en: And if the customer still isn't satisfied even after that?

lines.speaker: 선배
lines.en: In that case, the right move is to call the manager and hand off the authority. New staff often make things worse by trying to handle it alone.

lines.speaker: 신입
lines.en: Got it — apologize, explain, offer, and call the manager if needed.

lines.speaker: 선배
lines.en: Exactly. Just following that order resolves most complaints smoothly.

restaurant-c1y-neighborhood-decline.title: The decline of a neighborhood's dining culture

lines.speaker: 주민A
lines.en: This alley used to be packed with people every evening, but these days more than half the shops have closed.

lines.speaker: 주민B
lines.en: Rent went up so much that the old shops couldn't hold on. Instead, only franchises moved in.

lines.speaker: 주민A
lines.en: I'm not saying franchises are bad, but it's a shame the alley's unique character is disappearing.

lines.speaker: 주민B
lines.en: I feel the same way. But the younger generation actually seems to find familiar, tidy franchises more comfortable.

lines.speaker: 주민A
lines.en: Comfort and warmth are different things — it seems hard to hold onto both.

lines.speaker: 주민B
lines.en: I heard the district office is running a support program for the alley's commercial district, but we'll have to see if it's actually effective.

lines.speaker: 주민A
lines.en: Subsidies alone probably won't be enough — ultimately we need to create reasons for people to come back.

lines.speaker: 담당자
lines.en: Our company plans to run team dinners via catering about three times a month — would a regular contract be possible?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That's possible. But for a regular contract, it's better to decide in advance how much menu variety to maintain.

lines.speaker: 담당자
lines.en: We'd like a different menu each time — would that raise the unit price significantly?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Rather than a completely different menu each time, I'd recommend keeping a base composition and rotating just two or three dishes — that also reduces price fluctuation.

lines.speaker: 담당자
lines.en: We have staff with allergies — can you accommodate that individually?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: If you just give us the list in advance, we'll mark those dishes separately. That kind of advance notice actually makes things easier for us too.

lines.speaker: 담당자
lines.en: Sounds good. Then how about running it on a trial basis for one month first and discussing the contract terms again after?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: I think that's a reasonable proposal. Let's proceed that way.

restaurant-c1y-inspector-reveal.title: A Michelin inspector's visit revealed after the fact

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: That person who quietly sat and ate through our whole tasting course last Tuesday — turns out they were a Michelin inspector.

lines.speaker: 부주방장
lines.en: Really? We didn't do anything particularly special that day — actually that's a relief.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Exactly. If we'd known in advance, we probably would've gotten nervous and made mistakes.

lines.speaker: 부주방장
lines.en: Still, doing it as usual ultimately means our fundamentals didn't waver.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Right. Evaluation is ultimately about looking at the everyday, not a special occasion.

lines.speaker: 부주방장
lines.en: So does that mean we might actually get a star this time?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: It hasn't been announced yet so I can't be sure, but at the very least it was a day we have nothing to be ashamed of.

restaurant-c2y-succession.title: A daughter debates taking over the family restaurant

lines.speaker: 딸
lines.en: Dad, I keep wondering lately whether taking over this restaurant is really right for me. It feels less like something I want and more like I'm being pushed into it.

lines.speaker: 아버지
lines.en: I didn't think I'd pushed you, but if that's how you felt, then I must have unknowingly put pressure on you.

lines.speaker: 딸
lines.en: It's less about pressure and more about the fear of what happens if I ruin what you've built over thirty-some years.

lines.speaker: 아버지
lines.en: That very fear might be evidence that you're taking this seriously. If you were indifferent, you wouldn't be afraid at all.

lines.speaker: 딸
lines.en: Hearing you say that is somewhat comforting, but the pressure to carry it on exactly the same way still lingers.

lines.speaker: 아버지
lines.en: Who said you have to carry it on exactly the same? I didn't follow my own father's methods exactly either — as times change, methods should change too.

lines.speaker: 딸
lines.en: Then would you not be hurt if I changed the menu somewhat or renovated the interior?

lines.speaker: 아버지
lines.en: Curiosity would come before any hurt feelings, I think — I'd be curious what shape the next thirty years you build will take.

lines.speaker: 딸
lines.en: Hearing that actually gives me courage. I'll seriously start preparing for it.

restaurant-c2y-review-fallout.title: The fallout from a scathing online review

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Did you see that review? I never expected the phrase 'overpriced with no real effort' to spread this far.

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: I was surprised too. But if you read the comments closely, it seems the real trigger was that reservations were unusually backed up that day, delaying our response.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Whatever the reason, from the customer's perspective it'll only sound like an excuse. Should we post a public apology first?

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: Rushing to post an apology first could actually fan the flames. I think reaching out to that customer personally first to understand the situation is the right order of operations.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That makes sense. But since screenshots have already spread, I'm worried silence might also be perceived negatively.

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: That's why we should leave at least a brief note saying we're looking into it and will respond soon, and issue the actual apology only after we've confirmed the facts.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Understood. Let's proceed step by step without reacting emotionally.

lines.speaker: 홍보팀장
lines.en: This incident should also be a chance to review our response manual for busy hours.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: True. This must be exactly the situation the saying 'a crisis is also a chance to review' was made for.

restaurant-c2y-critic-anonymity.title: A literary essay on the vanishing anonymous critic

lines.speaker: 작가A
lines.en: These days restaurant reviews seem entirely governed by follower counts and sponsorships, so the purity of the anonymous critic feels almost like a myth now.

lines.speaker: 작가B
lines.en: Rather than a myth, wouldn't it be more accurate to say that role has simply been redistributed in a different form? After all, anyone can hold a camera now.

lines.speaker: 작가A
lines.en: 'Redistributed' is fair, but accountability has blurred just as much. In the past, one person's byline guaranteed trust; now, within a wave of anonymity, no one is accountable.

lines.speaker: 작가B
lines.en: That's a painful point. Still, I'd say multiple voices might actually reduce distortion more than a single person's authority.

lines.speaker: 작가A
lines.en: The trap is that 'multiple voices' is ultimately just a multitude curated by an algorithm. It could be amplified bias rather than genuine diversity.

lines.speaker: 작가B
lines.en: Then what we're nostalgic for isn't anonymity itself, but the editorial system of trust that once sustained that anonymity.

lines.speaker: 작가A
lines.en: You've hit it exactly. In the end the question isn't anonymity or not, but who takes responsibility for that voice.

lines.speaker: 작가B
lines.en: Why don't we write this discussion up as a column? Maybe titled something like 'The Vanished Critic, Scattered Accountability.'

lines.speaker: 작가A
lines.en: I like that. But let's not end the conclusion on cynicism — let's leave it open to the possibility of a new system of trust.

restaurant-c2y-generational-palate.title: Debating whether younger palates are losing depth

lines.speaker: 노셰프
lines.en: It's a shame that young customers these days only seem to respond to intense flavors and don't really pick up on subtle umami or lingering aftertaste.

lines.speaker: 젊은셰프
lines.en: I see it a bit differently. Maybe it's not that they can't sense it, but that they simply haven't had many opportunities to encounter it.

lines.speaker: 노셰프
lines.en: If they haven't had the opportunity, that ultimately means our generation failed to properly pass down that sensibility.

lines.speaker: 젊은셰프
lines.en: It's less that it wasn't passed down and more that the method of transmission needed to change — letting it seep in through experience rather than long explanations.

lines.speaker: 노셰프
lines.en: That has a point, but taste is ultimately trained too — if people only get accustomed to intense flavors, wouldn't the ability to distinguish subtle flavors itself atrophy?

lines.speaker: 젊은셰프
lines.en: I'd rather call it a shift in taste rather than atrophy. Though as you say, we do need to make sure not to lose depth within that shift.

lines.speaker: 노셰프
lines.en: In the end, what we should do isn't judge but build a bridge — between intensity and subtlety.

lines.speaker: 젊은셰프
lines.en: Agreed. Let me build that bridge into today's course — starting bold and finishing on a lingering note.

lines.speaker: 노셰프
lines.en: That's something to look forward to. I'd like to have a plate of that composition myself.

restaurant-c2y-labor-dispute.title: A tense negotiation over service-charge distribution

lines.speaker: 노조대표
lines.en: Service charges amount to ten percent of revenue, and the fact that more than half of that goes to management strikes us as fundamentally inequitable.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Management also plays a coordinating role behind the scenes to maintain service quality, so completely excluding them is difficult.

lines.speaker: 노조대표
lines.en: We're not denying the value of coordination — but ultimately it's the floor staff and kitchen staff who directly interact with customers and generate the basis for that service charge.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That point is valid. But I'd ask you to also understand the concern that a sudden change in the distribution ratio could lead to management turnover.

lines.speaker: 노조대표
lines.en: If turnover is the concern, how about separating the pay structures entirely — the service charge goes fully to front-line staff, while management is compensated through a base-salary increase instead?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That's an interesting proposal. But that would increase the total labor cost, so we'd need to discuss how to absorb that.

lines.speaker: 노조대표
lines.en: We'd like to be part of that discussion too. We believe the real solution to this conflict is jointly designing the plan, not a one-sided announcement.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Agreed. Let's share the financial data next week and run the simulations together.

lines.speaker: 노조대표
lines.en: Thank you. The fact that we can sit down and discuss this face to face is itself already significant progress.

restaurant-c2y-closing-legacy.title: An owner reflects on closing a forty-year restaurant

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I heard you're closing the restaurant you've run for forty years this month — I imagine your feelings must be quite complex.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Honestly, relief washed over me before sadness did. That surprised even me.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Relief is unexpected. I would have thought attachment would make closing it even harder.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: It's not that I lack attachment — it's that carrying this attachment like a burden and forcing it to continue felt like an insult to the place itself.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: That word 'insult' is striking. Could you elaborate a bit more?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: This place gave me something beyond just a livelihood — and keeping the sign up while my stamina isn't what it used to be and my passion isn't as fiery felt like a betrayal of those years.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So what plans do you have after closing?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: I don't really have a plan for right now. But rather than erasing this place entirely, I'd like to leave a record of the final dinners with regular customers.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: That record will likely become this restaurant's legacy in some form down the line.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: If it can remain that way, I couldn't ask for anything more.

restaurant-c2y-food-media-ethics.title: A panel debates paid placements in food media

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Today's topic is the issue of paid-ad disclosure in restaurant content. First, I'd like to ask how you view this problem.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: Disclosure itself is now legally mandatory, but I think the bigger problem is that the sincerity of the evaluation is compromised regardless of whether it's labeled.

lines.speaker: 마케터
lines.en: I see it a bit differently. If it's clearly labeled as an ad, I believe consumers have the judgment to factor that in and filter accordingly.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: Theoretically, yes, but in practice the disclosure is usually made small and hard to notice, so it loses its practical effect.

lines.speaker: 마케터
lines.en: Isn't that a problem with how the disclosure is displayed, not with sponsored content itself? That seems like something stronger regulation could fix.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: Stronger regulation is needed too, but fundamentally I think a culture needs to take root where creators themselves treat trust as an asset.

lines.speaker: 마케터
lines.en: I agree with that. But the moment the demand to treat trust as an asset collides with making a living, it's realistically hard to uphold, and that's the truth.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Can we sum this up as saying that regulation, self-restraint, and livelihood all need to find balance, in the end?

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: I think that's an accurate summary.

lines.speaker: 마케터
lines.en: I agree as well. I hope today's discussion becomes a small clue toward finding that balance.

restaurant-c2y-ai-kiosk-depth.title: Two regulars debate whether kiosks erode dining as ritual

lines.speaker: 손님A
lines.en: This kiosk is convenient, but lately I keenly feel that ordering itself used to be a kind of ritual. It feels as if that's disappeared.

lines.speaker: 손님B
lines.en: Calling it a ritual sounds a bit grandiose to me — wasn't ordering ultimately just a means of conveying information? I see it as simply the means becoming more efficient.

lines.speaker: 손님A
lines.en: I agree it's a means, but the process within that means — exchanging glances, explaining preferences — was itself an element that built a relationship.

lines.speaker: 손님B
lines.en: But that 'relationship' was ultimately just a brief contact with a stranger — isn't lamenting its loss actually a romanticization?

lines.speaker: 손님A
lines.en: I won't deny that charge of romanticization. Still, I tend to believe that small contacts accumulate to eventually form the sense of community that makes a neighborhood.

lines.speaker: 손님B
lines.en: I respect that belief, but the data shows many places have actually seen higher repeat-visit rates after adopting kiosks. Efficiency doesn't necessarily mean coldness.

lines.speaker: 손님A
lines.en: A higher repeat-visit rate doesn't necessarily guarantee the quality of those visits, but hearing you, I do wonder if I've leaned too heavily into one-sided sentiment.

lines.speaker: 손님B
lines.en: I wouldn't say leaned so much as that we simply value different things. You find warmth in contact, and I find reassurance in efficiency.

lines.speaker: 손님A
lines.en: Framing it that way makes clear this debate isn't about winning or losing. Still, I think I'll occasionally go out of my way to chat with the staff anyway.

restaurant-c2y-critics-notebook.title: A veteran critic reflects on the ethics of a scathing verdict

lines.speaker: 후배 평론가
lines.en: Senior, that review of yours was really scathing. There are even rumors the restaurant might close this season — I imagine that must weigh on you.

lines.speaker: 선배 평론가
lines.en: How could it be easy? But I know for myself that the harshness didn't come from personal grudge — it came from respect for the cooking itself.

lines.speaker: 후배 평론가
lines.en: I understand what you mean about respect, but how do you carry the weight of knowing one sentence could determine a restaurant's survival?

lines.speaker: 선배 평론가
lines.en: I've never once taken that weight lightly. But you mustn't forget that silence is itself a form of judgment too. Turning a blind eye to bad cooking can be its own kind of violence to someone else.

lines.speaker: 후배 평론가
lines.en: Violence to someone else — could you explain that a bit more?

lines.speaker: 선배 평론가
lines.en: Silence about a poorly made dish just means the next customer repeats the same disappointment. An honest review might actually be the restaurant's last chance to reflect on itself.

lines.speaker: 후배 평론가
lines.en: Hearing that, harshness might actually be another face of care. Still, I don't yet have the confidence to write with that level of conviction.

lines.speaker: 선배 평론가
lines.en: Conviction doesn't form overnight. Just ask yourself before every sentence you write — is this honesty toward the cooking, or just a desire to show off cleverness?

lines.speaker: 후배 평론가
lines.en: I'll make that question my standard for writing from now on.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: This kimchi carbonara is an interesting attempt, but doesn't it feel like you just slapped two cultures together?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: It's not slapping together — I found fermentation as a common thread and connected them through that.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: Having a common thread doesn't automatically make it respectful.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Then I'm curious what conditions you'd consider necessary for it to count as respectful.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: At the very least, whether you learned from the people who created that cuisine and understood its context matters.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: I spent three years in Italy and learned from my mother at my Korean family home. Wouldn't that count as grounding?

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: That's personal experience, but customers don't know that background — they only see the plate.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: That's why I'm considering adding at least a brief note on the menu explaining that process.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: That level of effort would at least be a reasonable starting point.

restaurant-c1z-farm-to-table-skepticism.title: A chef explaining farm-to-table marketing skepticism

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: The menu says 'farm to table' — do you actually source directly from a farm?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Partly, but honestly I think that phrase has become more of a marketing cliche by now.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Then why do you keep using the expression?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: There's an element of using it out of necessity — if I don't, customers might assume the food isn't fresh.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So is there some other criterion that actually guarantees freshness?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: We operate on a principle of receiving produce within twenty-four hours of harvest, and we log that every day.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: A concrete standard like that is actually more convincing than the phrase itself.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Exactly. So going forward I'm thinking of replacing 'farm to table' with disclosing that record instead.

lines.speaker: 투자자
lines.en: We'd like to make an acquisition offer on the condition of expanding to ten locations.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Expansion itself is welcome, but I'm worried about whether the recipes and cooking methods can stay the same.

lines.speaker: 투자자
lines.en: Some standardization is unavoidable. Relying on a personal touch means quality would be inconsistent across locations.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: But that personal touch is the core of our brand — wouldn't standardizing it erase that?

lines.speaker: 투자자
lines.en: What about a compromise where the core sauce and pickling are supplied from the flagship, and only the rest of the cooking is manualized?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That level might let us keep our identity — but what would the equity structure look like?

lines.speaker: 투자자
lines.en: We would hold sixty percent and you would hold forty percent, with operational control remaining with you.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: If operational control is preserved, it's worth considering. I'll consult my lawyer and get back to you.

lines.speaker: 투자자
lines.en: Of course, no need to rush. It's better for us too if you decide carefully.

restaurant-c1z-lab-grown-meat.title: Food scientists debating lab-grown meat on the menu

lines.speaker: 연구원A
lines.en: Why do you think putting lab-grown meat on the regular menu is premature?

lines.speaker: 연구원B
lines.en: It's technically feasible, but the problem is that taste consistency drops during mass production.

lines.speaker: 연구원A
lines.en: Isn't consistency just an issue that will improve over time?

lines.speaker: 연구원B
lines.en: That's true, but once customers are disappointed once, they tend not to even try again.

lines.speaker: 연구원A
lines.en: Then instead of waiting for perfection from the start, how about starting as a small limited menu item?

lines.speaker: 연구원B
lines.en: That approach isn't bad, since even failure would have limited impact.

lines.speaker: 연구원A
lines.en: Plus, if we use the reduced environmental impact in marketing, the initial response probably won't be bad.

lines.speaker: 연구원B
lines.en: But we have to keep in mind that many customers feel resistance to the word 'lab-grown meat' itself.

lines.speaker: 연구원A
lines.en: In that case, the first order of business would be to reconsider the naming.

restaurant-c1z-no-show-fees.title: Debating whether reservations should carry no-show fees

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Our reservation no-show rate is over twenty percent, so I'm considering introducing a no-show fee.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: Charging a fee might reduce reservations altogether — customers might find it burdensome.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That's possible, but wouldn't it be better than losing money by leaving tables empty like now?

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: What about taking a deposit instead, and deducting it from the meal cost if they actually show up?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: That would have a no-show prevention effect while causing less resistance.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: Still, I think we should allow a grace period for canceling in case of sudden circumstances.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Let's set it so cancellation is free until the morning of, and after that the deposit is forfeited.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: That's reasonable. We should also put clear notice text on the reservation page.

restaurant-c1z-tip-pooling-law.title: A labor lawyer explaining tip pooling regulations

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: I want to split the servers' tips with the kitchen staff — is that legally okay?

lines.speaker: 변호사
lines.en: As long as management-level staff don't get a share, it's generally fine. But you need clear criteria.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: What kind of criteria are you referring to, for example?

lines.speaker: 변호사
lines.en: You need to document the distribution ratio in advance based on work hours or job weight, otherwise disputes can arise later.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: What happens if an employee later raises an objection that it's unfair?

lines.speaker: 변호사
lines.en: If there's a documented standard, you can defend based on that, but without one, you're likely to be at a disadvantage.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: Then I should get the distribution policy written down as a document within this week.

lines.speaker: 변호사
lines.en: Yes, and if you also get employee signatures on it, it'll be much safer down the line.

restaurant-c1z-authenticity-gatekeeping.title: An immigrant chef discussing authenticity gatekeeping

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: This dish seems a bit different from what you'd eat back in your hometown — why is that?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Since it's hard to get local ingredients, I use substitutes, which changed the taste a bit.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then is it right to call this 'authentic'?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: I ask myself that question all the time too. But I also wonder whether 'authentic' is even something fixed.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What do you mean?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: My mother's generation's cooking was already different from the generation before that. Cuisine has always been continuously changing.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then customers demanding 'authenticity' might itself be somewhat contradictory.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Not entirely contradictory, but I think 'whether it was made with sincerity' matters more than that word.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hearing that makes me see this plate differently.

restaurant-c1z-menu-psychology.title: Economists debating menu psychology and pricing tricks

lines.speaker: 경제학자A
lines.en: There's research showing sales rise just from dropping the currency unit after prices on a menu — should we apply that here too?

lines.speaker: 경제학자B
lines.en: It'd probably work, but I'm a bit reluctant since that kind of trick feels like deceiving customers.

lines.speaker: 경제학자A
lines.en: It's less about deceiving and more about lowering psychological resistance — the price itself is displayed the same.

lines.speaker: 경제학자B
lines.en: Then is putting an expensive item at the top, like a decoy, the same logic?

lines.speaker: 경제학자A
lines.en: Right, it's a technique that makes the item next to it look relatively reasonable.

lines.speaker: 경제학자B
lines.en: I think those techniques might boost sales in the short term but erode trust in the long run.

lines.speaker: 경제학자A
lines.en: That concern is valid, but as long as the whole industry uses it, not using it could actually be a disadvantage.

lines.speaker: 경제학자B
lines.en: Then let's compromise by at least removing blatant decoy items and only adjusting the display format.

restaurant-c1z-kitchen-staff-status.title: A documentary crew interviewing kitchen staff about status

lines.speaker: 감독
lines.en: For this documentary, I'd like to cover the real working conditions of kitchen staff — could you agree to an interview?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Could you blur my face? There are some sensitive issues around my status.

lines.speaker: 감독
lines.en: Of course. We'll alter both your face and voice so your identity isn't revealed.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Then I'll be honest with you. There are more people in situations like mine in this industry than you'd think.

lines.speaker: 감독
lines.en: What's the biggest difficulty specifically?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Even when treated unfairly, if I report it, I'm the one who ends up at risk, so I often just endure it.

lines.speaker: 감독
lines.en: Capturing that structural problem is exactly what our documentary aims to do.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: But I'm also worried that once this airs, employers might just become more guarded instead.

lines.speaker: 감독
lines.en: We're aware of that risk too. That's why we plan to cover industry insiders' reactions in a balanced way as well.

restaurant-c2z-critic-anonymity-social-m.title: A critic defending anonymity in the age of social media

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: These days even ordinary customers post photos online — I'm curious why you still insist on anonymity.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: Once anonymity disappears, the treatment I receive differs from that of ordinary customers, and that undermines the fairness of my assessment.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: But social media influencers also review with their real names and faces public. How is that different from you?

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: They're sharing the experience of a specific visit, whereas my role is to repeatedly verify a venue's overall standard. The purposes themselves are different.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Then couldn't anonymity itself start to look like a privilege — since no one can hold you accountable?

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: That's a fair point. That's why I address that concern by publishing my evaluation criteria and keeping transparent records of repeat visits.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Still, from a reader's perspective, the question of 'why should I trust writing by someone I don't know' seems to remain.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: That doubt is legitimate. But I believe consistent standards and accumulated trust are a more important asset than a name.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So in the end, it's less about the form of anonymity and more about the standards behind it, you're saying.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: Exactly. The form is just a means — the essence lies in trustworthy verification.

restaurant-c2z-immigration-status-scruti.title: A union organizer and owner debating verification duties

lines.speaker: 노조간사
lines.en: I heard several kitchen staff suddenly quit after the recent crackdown — did you know about that?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: I knew about it, but I wasn't sure it was right to dig into individual circumstances.

lines.speaker: 노조간사
lines.en: That sounds like you neglected your verification obligations, and that could lead to legal liability.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: I'm aware of that risk too, but I was cautious because excessively probing into documents might come across as discrimination.

lines.speaker: 노조간사
lines.en: Couldn't that caution have ended up pushing employees into an even more vulnerable position? No one protects them when trouble arises.

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: I admit that. So even at this point, I'm planning to sort out the process with a labor consultant.

lines.speaker: 노조간사
lines.en: Sorting out procedures matters, but what will you do about at least minimal compensation for the employees who already left?

lines.speaker: 사장
lines.en: I can't give a clear answer on that yet. But I can promise I won't turn a blind eye to it.

lines.speaker: 노조간사
lines.en: So that promise doesn't end up as just words, I'll come back next month to check on the situation again.

restaurant-c2z-menu-translation-loss.title: Debating what's lost when a menu is translated for export

lines.speaker: 번역가
lines.en: I keep getting stuck translating the phrase 'tastes like home cooking' into English — the nuance just doesn't survive.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Then instead of trying to translate the meaning literally, what about substituting a different sense entirely?

lines.speaker: 번역가
lines.en: Like what?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Something like 'the kind your grandmother would make' — a concrete image, which lands faster than an abstract sentiment.

lines.speaker: 번역가
lines.en: But wouldn't that image also only land with Western customers? The image of grandmother's cooking probably differs by culture.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: I don't think a perfect equivalence is possible to begin with. We have to accept some loss.

lines.speaker: 번역가
lines.en: Minimizing that loss is my job, so it's awkward when you keep telling me to just give up.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: I'm not saying give up — I'm saying what the customer feels after eating the dish matters more than a perfect translation.

lines.speaker: 번역가
lines.en: That has a point, but then it means the menu text is just a reference, doesn't it?

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Exactly. The real translation is ultimately done by the plate — the text is just a sign guiding them there.

restaurant-c2z-kitchen-hierarchy-abuse.title: Former line cooks debate the culture of kitchen hierarchy

lines.speaker: 전직A
lines.en: It's been five years since I left that kitchen, but I can still hear the sound of the chef throwing plates.

lines.speaker: 전직B
lines.en: Back then everyone said that was just the normal way of training — that you grow under pressure.

lines.speaker: 전직A
lines.en: Looking back, I think that wasn't training at all — it was just abuse. But why did nobody raise the issue back then?

lines.speaker: 전직B
lines.en: There was a fear that raising it would get you blacklisted from the industry — the network of chefs is so tight-knit.

lines.speaker: 전직A
lines.en: But these days young cooks can't stand that culture and just quit right away — isn't that actually the right response?

lines.speaker: 전직B
lines.en: It is the right response, but at the same time there's criticism that they give up too easily without patience.

lines.speaker: 전직A
lines.en: Patience and enduring abuse are different issues. The discussion goes off the rails because people keep conflating the two.

lines.speaker: 전직B
lines.en: Then do you actually think it's possible to develop skill without pressure at all?

lines.speaker: 전직A
lines.en: I'm not saying to eliminate pressure entirely — I'm saying we should separate personal degradation from pressure related to skill.

lines.speaker: 전직B
lines.en: Keeping that line in an actual working kitchen would be the real challenge.

restaurant-c2z-tasting-menu-ethics.title: Debating whether tasting menus should disclose sourcing failures

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Today's planned sea urchin course couldn't happen due to a catch shortage, so we swapped it — should we tell the customers?

lines.speaker: 홀매니저
lines.en: Of course we should. A tasting menu is itself a narrative — swapping it secretly breaks that narrative.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: But the substitute is matched in quality just the same — is there really a need to highlight the problem?

lines.speaker: 홀매니저
lines.en: It's not about quality — it's about transparency. Explaining why it changed could actually read as sincerity.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: I actually think that kind of explanation might make customers uneasy — like 'is something wrong here.'

lines.speaker: 홀매니저
lines.en: Rather than unease, since a catch shortage connects to climate issues these days, it could actually be an interesting talking point.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: I hadn't thought of it that way. Then should we add a short explanation card alongside it?

lines.speaker: 홀매니저
lines.en: Yes, but it's important to write it plainly so it doesn't sound like an excuse.

lines.speaker: 셰프
lines.en: Got it. This might be a good opportunity to standardize how we handle substitute-menu notices in general.

restaurant-c2z-dining-solo-stigma.title: A columnist and reader debate the stigma of dining alone

lines.speaker: 독자
lines.en: You wrote in your column that 'eating alone is no longer pitiable,' but I still feel self-conscious sitting at a solo table.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: That self-consciousness might actually be created by the restaurant's own layout — solo seats are mostly in corners or at the bar.

lines.speaker: 독자
lines.en: Right. All the good spots are two-or-more tables, and if you come alone you're automatically shown to a worse spot.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: So my point was that the problem lies in spatial design, not individual attitude.

lines.speaker: 독자
lines.en: But from the restaurant's perspective, groups are more profitable than solo diners — is there an incentive to change the structure?

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: Solo customers actually have an advantage in table turnover — they vacate seats faster.

lines.speaker: 독자
lines.en: I hadn't thought of that. Then why do most restaurants still treat solo seats as an afterthought?

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: It's inertia. Dining out has long been designed purely as a social act, so it takes time to break that mold.

lines.speaker: 독자
lines.en: Then I'd love it if your next column introduced restaurants that actually design good solo seating.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: Good suggestion. I happen to have a few places I've already researched, so I'll include them in the next issue.

restaurant-c2z-ghost-kitchen-identity.title: Two owners debate whether ghost kitchens dilute identity

lines.speaker: 사장A
lines.en: I'm considering opening another delivery-only ghost kitchen, but I'm hesitant because it might dilute my brand identity.

lines.speaker: 사장B
lines.en: Identity ultimately comes from the customer's experience facing the plate — without a physical space, doesn't that experience itself fail to hold?

lines.speaker: 사장A
lines.en: I share that concern, but looking at the revenue structure, the delivery share is a reality we can't ignore.

lines.speaker: 사장B
lines.en: I acknowledge that reality, but is expanding at the cost of abandoning identity really the right direction in the long run?

lines.speaker: 사장A
lines.en: I don't see it as abandonment — I see it as an attempt to carry over the identity by paying attention even to packaging and sauce composition.

lines.speaker: 사장B
lines.en: If that attempt succeeds, it would actually be a case of expanding the scope of the identity.

lines.speaker: 사장A
lines.en: Right. But the key would be managing it so the original store's quality doesn't get shaken in the process.

lines.speaker: 사장B
lines.en: Once you start sharing staff and ingredients, avoiding that instability will probably be harder than you think.

lines.speaker: 사장A
lines.en: That's why I plan to start with a completely separate staff and consider integration only once things stabilize.

restaurant-c2z-ai-review-authenticity.title: A panel debates AI-generated reviews and trust erosion

lines.speaker: 패널A
lines.en: I hear there are companies mass-producing plausible-sounding reviews with AI these days — what impact will this have on the industry?

lines.speaker: 패널B
lines.en: In the short term it'll help sales, but ultimately it'll lead to the collapse of trust in reviews as a whole.

lines.speaker: 패널A
lines.en: Then a paradox would arise where restaurants that honestly built up reviews actually end up losing out.

lines.speaker: 패널B
lines.en: Exactly. Once it becomes hard to distinguish fake from real, consumers will end up not trusting reviews at all.

lines.speaker: 패널A
lines.en: Wouldn't introducing detection technology on the platform side solve this?

lines.speaker: 패널B
lines.en: Detection technology is also in a constant cat-and-mouse relationship with generation technology, so I don't think it can be a complete solution.

lines.speaker: 패널A
lines.en: Then what do you see as the alternative?

lines.speaker: 패널B
lines.en: I think devices that prove an actual visit — like real-name or payment verification — will end up being the last bastion of trust in reviews.

lines.speaker: 패널A
lines.en: That approach won't fully avoid privacy invasion controversy either, though.

lines.speaker: 패널B
lines.en: Right. In the end, it's a problem where the whole industry will have to keep searching for a balance between trust and privacy.

restaurant-c2z-heritage-recipe-ownership.title: Siblings dispute ownership of a heritage recipe

lines.speaker: 형
lines.en: If you're going to open a new location with Dad's recipe, you should have at least discussed it with me beforehand.

lines.speaker: 동생
lines.en: That recipe isn't only yours. I stood by Dad's side in the kitchen for over ten years too.

lines.speaker: 형
lines.en: I acknowledge you stood by him, but legally the name is registered under me due to the inheritance issue.

lines.speaker: 동생
lines.en: Just because the legal name is under you doesn't mean you alone own the spirit of that recipe.

lines.speaker: 형
lines.en: What does 'spirit' concretely mean? In the end, a business runs on clear rights relationships.

lines.speaker: 동생
lines.en: I'm saying this because I wonder if Dad, if he were alive, would have wanted us to split apart like this.

lines.speaker: 형
lines.en: That sounds a bit unfair to me. Let's not appeal to emotion and instead talk about terms.

lines.speaker: 동생
lines.en: Fine, then give me thirty percent equity in the new location and recognize my right to be consulted on recipe use.

lines.speaker: 형
lines.en: Thirty percent is too much, but I can accept twenty percent plus the consultation right.

lines.speaker: 동생
lines.en: All right, I'll accept that much. But let's put Dad's name up equally at both locations.

lines.speaker: 형
lines.en: That's a given. I never intended to fight over that name in the first place.
