lines.en: Sure, I'll get those ready right away.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: There are two of us — could you recommend what to order?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We have a two-person set — the portion would be just right.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What's included in that set?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You get two types of meat, a stew, and rice.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That sounds good, we'll go with that.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Great, I'll get it started right away.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: This is my first time at a buffet — can I keep refilling the same plate?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, though it's best not to leave leftovers.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What happens if I do leave food?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: If you leave more than a certain amount, there's an extra charge.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Ah, then I'll just take small portions.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's a good approach.

restaurant-b1x-cooktime.title: How long does it take to cook

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How long does this braised short rib dish take to come out?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: About thirty minutes — it's cooked to order.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's a bit long — can we order something else first?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, shall I get you some pajeon while you wait?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Understood.

restaurant-b1x-meeting.title: A quiet corner for a meeting

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: This is a work meeting — could we get a quieter table, please?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, there's a private room available in the back.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then we'll take that, please. Is there an outlet too?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, there's one by the wall.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's perfect, thank you.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll show you the way.

restaurant-b1x-photo.title: Asking staff to take a photo

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Sorry to ask, but could you take one photo of us?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Of course. How would you like it taken?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Please get both the table and all of us in the shot.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, one, two, three.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you, it came out great.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Enjoy the rest of your meal.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I only eat halal food — do you have any menu items that work?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Many of our dishes have pork, so let me check.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The fish dishes and vegetable menu should work for you.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then I'll have the grilled fish, please.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, I'll also make sure it's handled separately in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you so much.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I like spicy food — could I get some extra gochujang?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, though this dish is already quite spicy.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Even so, I'd like it spicier.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Understood — a little or a lot?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: A lot, please.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, I'll bring it right away.

restaurant-b1x-festival.title: Asking about a food festival discount

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I heard there's a discount during this festival period — is that right?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's correct. There's a twenty percent discount on everything.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Do I need to sign up separately, or is it applied automatically?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's taken off automatically at checkout.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's great, thank you.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: You're welcome — enjoy your meal.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Could you swap the radish kimchi for regular kimchi?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, but this set comes with radish kimchi by default, so there's an extra charge.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: How much more do I have to pay?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: About five hundred won.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's fine — please make the swap.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, got it.

restaurant-b1x-splitcards.title: Splitting the bill on two cards

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Can we split the payment across two cards?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, that's possible. Shall I split it evenly?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: No — I'll pay thirty thousand won, and my friend will pay the rest.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Understood, please give me the cards in order.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: どうぞ。

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: The payment is complete.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: This Monday is a public holiday — are you open that day?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, we're open, but only until six in the evening.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's earlier than usual.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Right, the staff need some rest too.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then I'll come around five in the evening.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, we'll be expecting you.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: There will be eight of us — can we book a private room?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, we have one. The minimum is six people, so you'd fit perfectly.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Is there a separate fee for using the room?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: No, it's free as long as you order food.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's great, I'll book it.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, please give me your name and time.

restaurant-b1x-reheat.title: Asking for a dish to be reheated

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: We were talking and the soup got cold. Could you reheat it?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, I'll take the whole bowl and heat it up.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thanks — will it take long?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: No, it'll be quick.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Here's your soup, reheated.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's nice and warm, thank you.

restaurant-b2x-buffetmixup.title: Mixed up plates at the buffet counter

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Excuse me, the plate I left at the pickup counter is gone.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry — it looks like another guest took it by mistake.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: The steak I ordered was on that plate.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm truly sorry — I'll have a new one grilled right away.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: While I wait, could you bring me something else in the meantime?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Of course, I'll bring you a salad first at least.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That would be much appreciated.

restaurant-b2x-appissue.title: The reservation app didn't go through

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I made a reservation through the app yesterday, but I never got a confirmation text.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Could you tell me your name and the time?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's under Kim Seoyeon, for seven o'clock.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Looking it up, the reservation didn't actually go through.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's strange — I even saw a confirmation screen.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It might have been a system error on our end — let me get you a table right now.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you — next time I'll follow up with a phone call to be sure.

restaurant-b2x-latecall.title: Calling ahead about a late arrival

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Hello, we have a seven o'clock reservation, but traffic means we'll probably be about fifteen minutes late.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Thank you for letting us know. I'll hold the table for you.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: What happens if we end up more than fifteen minutes late?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Up to twenty minutes is fine, but past that you'd need to call us again.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Understood, we'll try to hurry as much as we can.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Okay, drive safely.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I noticed a separate service charge on the receipt — is that different from a tip?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, we automatically add a ten percent service charge.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: So I don't need to leave an additional tip on top of that?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: That's right, that covers it.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It would have been nice if that had been mentioned earlier.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry — it's noted in small print on the menu. We'll mention it upfront next time.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, please do that.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Of what we just ordered, could we cancel one of the fried dishes?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Let me check — the kitchen may have already started on it.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry, they say it's already frying.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Ah, then I guess there's no helping it. Can we take it to go instead?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, we can do that for you.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you, let's go with that then.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure — just note there's a small container fee added at checkout.

restaurant-b2x-togobox.title: A fee for the to-go container

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I see a container fee on the receipt — is that normally charged?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, our restaurant charges for containers separately — sorry about that.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's usually free elsewhere, so I was a bit surprised.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I know — guests mention that fairly often.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It would help if there were a sign about it in advance next time.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Thanks for the feedback, I'll pass that suggestion along.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, please do.

restaurant-b2x-recipehint.title: Asking for a hint about the recipe

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: This sauce is really delicious — could you tell me what ingredients go into it?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I don't actually know the exact recipe — only the owner does.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's a shame — could you give me a rough idea, at least?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I've heard it has soy sauce, garlic, and pear juice in it.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I see — I'll try making it at home sometime.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It won't be exactly the same, but it should come out close.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thanks, that sounds fun.

restaurant-b2x-noisecomplaint.title: Requesting a quieter table due to noise

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Sorry, but the table next to us is so loud we can't have a conversation.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry — let me check on that.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Would it be all right if we moved you to a different table?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, moving would be better if that's possible.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: There's a quiet table further in — this way, please.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: This is much better, thank you.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry for the inconvenience.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Could I possibly pay in dollars? I'm short on Korean won.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry, but we only accept won or card payment.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then I'll pay by card — can I also get a receipt in English?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, we can print an English receipt too.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's great, please do.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Please insert your card.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Here you go, thank you.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'm planning to propose to my girlfriend today — could you help me set something up?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Wow, congratulations! How can we help?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Could you set out a candle and some flower petals when the dessert comes out?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, we can do that. Have you also decided how you'll present the ring?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I think hiding it under the plate would be nice.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: That's a great idea — we'll set it up carefully for you.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you so much — I'm really nervous.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: My child is five years old — does that qualify for the kids-eat-free promotion?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, kids six and under get one free meal per adult entrée ordered.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: We ordered two adult entrées — so would both of our kids be free then?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it applies per adult entrée ordered, so both kids would be free.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's great — we'll order the kids' meals then.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Sure, which items would you like for them?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Two pork cutlets, please.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: This week's seasonal special is abalone risotto — would you like to try it?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I'm curious, but is it very different from the pasta I usually get?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: It's cream-based, so it's richer, and it has a generous amount of abalone in it.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: It's probably more expensive too, right?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, it's about five thousand won more than the pasta.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then I'll take a chance and try that this time.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I think you'll be pleased — I'll get it started right away.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: I have a fairly severe nut allergy — could I ask about how the dish is prepared too?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, of course. What are you concerned about?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Do you cook dishes with nuts in the same pan?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We do use separate pans, but they're not entirely isolated from each other.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: So you can't say it's completely safe, then?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Right, honestly we can't guarantee it's a hundred percent safe. Let me ask the chef separately.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, I'd really appreciate you checking on that.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Could you make it without MSG? It gives me headaches when I eat it.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Our broth does have a small amount of seasoning added.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: So it's difficult to leave it out entirely, then?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: We could prepare a separate broth, but it would take a bit longer.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: That's fine, I'll wait — my health matters more.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Understood, it should take about fifteen minutes.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, please go ahead.

restaurant-b2x-wifidown.title: Wifi problems during a work meeting

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Sorry, but the wifi keeps dropping and I can't get through this video call.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'm sorry — it's probably because we've had a lot of guests lately.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Would restarting the router help, maybe?

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Yes, let me restart the router right now.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Could you wait just a moment — it should take about two minutes.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Okay — I'm a bit worried since my meeting is about to start.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll hurry as much as I can — I'm really sorry about this.

restaurant-b2x-coldseat.title: A drafty seat near the door

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Our table is right next to the door, so a draft comes in every time someone goes in and out.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Ah, that must have been uncomfortable. Would you like to be seated somewhere else?

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Yes, if possible I'd like to move further inside.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Everything's full right now, but a table should open up in about ten minutes.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Then what should we do until then? It's really cold.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: I'll bring you a blanket for now, and let you know the moment a table opens.

lines.speaker: 손님
lines.en: Thank you, please do that.

shopping-c1y-fastfashion.title: Debating fast fashion with a friend

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: This brand drops new arrivals literally every week now. Honestly, isn't that a bit much?

lines.speaker: 민호
lines.en: Since the prices are so low, it's tempting to keep buying. But lately I haven't felt great about it either.

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: Apparently most of it barely survives a few wears before being thrown out. That all comes back as an environmental burden.

lines.speaker: 민호
lines.en: I don't think just refusing to buy anything is the answer either. What about checking the materials and production methods before buying?

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: But that still puts the burden on the consumer to dig for it. Shouldn't companies be the ones disclosing that information transparently?

lines.speaker: 민호
lines.en: True, labels only show origin and material, nothing about labor conditions or carbon emissions.

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: That's why I've been leaning toward brands with resale or repair services. If I can wear something for a long time, that seems like the best I can do.

lines.speaker: 민호
lines.en: Hearing that, I think I need to sort out my closet first. I should sell what I don't wear and only buy what I actually need.

lines.speaker: 수진
lines.en: That's the surest way. Changing one consumption habit ends up making the biggest difference in the end.

shopping-c1y-buyernegotiate.title: A department store buyer negotiates with a designer

lines.speaker: 바이어
lines.en: The response to this season's collection has been strong, so I'd like to formally propose bringing you into our store.

lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: I appreciate the offer, but we run small-batch production, so it might be hard to meet a department store's volume.

lines.speaker: 바이어
lines.en: You don't have to start with a large volume. We can begin with a small quantity per season and scale based on response.

lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: Then what would the commission structure look like? That's the part that weighs heaviest on a small brand like ours.

lines.speaker: 바이어
lines.en: If we run this under our emerging-designer program, we can lower the initial commission rate and give you priority placement as well.

lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: Placement really matters. No matter how good the clothes are, they won't get noticed if the rack is tucked in a corner.

lines.speaker: 바이어
lines.en: Exactly. In exchange, I'd like to propose a short six-month contract term, with renewal discussed based on performance.

lines.speaker: 디자이너
lines.en: That sounds reasonable. If you can just clarify the return conditions for unsold inventory, we could consider this positively on our end.

lines.speaker: 바이어
lines.en: Of course. We'll draft the contract and get back to you within the week.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: The flight I looked at yesterday went up in price when I checked again today. Isn't this the algorithm reading people's behavior patterns?

lines.speaker: 은영
lines.en: Right, apparently just repeated searches signal high demand, so the price gets raised. The revisit itself becomes a signal.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: So from a consumer's perspective, do I have to clear my search history or use incognito mode? That seems a bit unreasonable.

lines.speaker: 은영
lines.en: A lot of people actually do that. But the problem is this isn't a transparent, disclosed policy. Consumers don't even know why they're paying more.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: It's the same product, but different people see different prices. Isn't that just price discrimination?

lines.speaker: 은영
lines.en: Legally it's still a gray area. Airlines and e-commerce companies argue it's just normal demand-based pricing.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: Still, shouldn't they at least disclose what factors affect the price? Only then can consumers actually make an informed choice.

lines.speaker: 은영
lines.en: Agreed. In the end, the line blurs between whether the algorithm serves the consumer or just maximizes company profit.

shopping-c1y-classaction.title: A consumer rights advocate explains a class-action case

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Today we have a representative from a consumer rights group to discuss the recent class-action lawsuit over cosmetics. Could you give us a brief explanation?

lines.speaker: 관계자
lines.en: Yes, testing revealed that the company's products actually contained an ingredient that wasn't listed on the label.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: It's unusual for a labeling error to escalate into a lawsuit. How exactly was consumer harm confirmed?

lines.speaker: 관계자
lines.en: Hundreds of consumer complaints about skin irritation were filed, and some even included medical diagnoses as evidence.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So in this lawsuit, what form of compensation can consumers actually expect to receive?

lines.speaker: 관계자
lines.en: It covers a refund of the purchase price, and for those with medical treatment receipts, they can separately claim reimbursement for actual costs.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: It's practically difficult for an individual consumer to sue on their own. Where do you see the significance of a class action?

lines.speaker: 관계자
lines.en: By sharing the cost and time burden, it becomes far more effective at proving widespread harm all at once.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: If viewers wish to participate, what procedure should they follow?

lines.speaker: 관계자
lines.en: We've opened a case-submission channel on our organization's website, so please apply along with your purchase receipt.

lines.speaker: 재현
lines.en: I hear minimalist living is trendy these days, but honestly, buying things is my one joy in life, so I don't quite get it.

lines.speaker: 소라
lines.en: I felt the same at first. But the more stuff I had, the more scattered my mind felt. I couldn't even remember where I put things.

lines.speaker: 재현
lines.en: Still, you can't ignore the satisfaction you feel when shopping. It's also a way to relieve stress.

lines.speaker: 소라
lines.en: I think the question is how long that satisfaction lasts. For me, my interest just drops off a few days after buying something.

lines.speaker: 재현
lines.en: I'll grant you that. But doesn't minimalism become its own obsession when taken to an extreme? Feeling guilty every time you bring in one object seems odd too.

lines.speaker: 소라
lines.en: Right, I approached it that obsessively at first too and it just wore me out. Now I've relaxed it to simply asking 'do I really need this.'

lines.speaker: 재현
lines.en: That level sounds doable for me too. It's not about tossing everything out extremely, but about setting a standard for consumption.

lines.speaker: 소라
lines.en: Exactly. In the end, the reason behind why you buy seems to matter more than the object itself.

shopping-c1y-livecommerce.title: A live-commerce host and guest discuss influencer ethics

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Today's broadcast features an influencer marketing expert, and I hear there's a controversial issue in live commerce right now.

lines.speaker: 게스트
lines.en: Yes, there are many cases where sponsored products are introduced as if the host bought and used them personally, and that's become a problem.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: From the viewer's perspective, it must be hard to tell whether it's a genuine review or an advertisement.

lines.speaker: 게스트
lines.en: Exactly. Legally, the sponsorship must be clearly disclosed, but many hosts insert the caption in tiny text or flash it by in an instant.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So are there actually many cases of viewers being deceived into purchasing?

lines.speaker: 게스트
lines.en: Yes, in particular, repeating phrases like 'limited quantity' or 'real-time discount' to rush purchases has been pointed out as problematic.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Then are there any standards viewers can use to check for themselves while watching a broadcast?

lines.speaker: 게스트
lines.en: First, check whether there's a sponsorship disclosure caption, and if urgency-inducing remarks repeat excessively, it's worth being a bit suspicious.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: In the end, platform-level regulation would be necessary too.

lines.speaker: 게스트
lines.en: That's right. Self-regulation alone has its limits, so I believe a system enforcing minimum disclosure standards needs to be established.

lines.speaker: 담당자
lines.en: On our end, we'd like to secure exclusive domestic distribution rights for this brand. Shall we discuss the terms in more detail?

lines.speaker: 본사
lines.en: To grant exclusivity, we'd first need to agree on a minimum order quantity and annual sales target. It carries some risk on our side.

lines.speaker: 담당자
lines.en: I understand. However, if the initial volume is set too high, it would place a heavy financial burden on us, which could make it hard to even get started.

lines.speaker: 본사
lines.en: Then how about lowering the target for the first year, but including a clause where exclusivity automatically terminates if the target isn't met?

lines.speaker: 담당자
lines.en: That sounds fair. In return, I'd like a clause where marketing costs are shared jointly.

lines.speaker: 본사
lines.en: What ratio are you thinking of for splitting the marketing costs?

lines.speaker: 담당자
lines.en: Since we manage the sales channels directly, around a 6-to-4 split with us covering more, in exchange for requesting data access rights.

lines.speaker: 본사
lines.en: Data sharing is something we need too, so that's no problem. Let's finalize a three-year contract term with a renewal clause.

lines.speaker: 담당자
lines.en: Sounds good. We'll have the detailed clauses reviewed by legal and send the final contract next week.

shopping-c1y-deescalate.title: A manager trains staff on de-escalating a demanding customer

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: Today I want to go over some response techniques based on the complaint situation we had last week.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: That customer raised their voice from the very start, so I was flustered about how to respond.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: In that case, the priority is to not interrupt and let them finish speaking. You need to first acknowledge the reason for their anger before the conversation can move forward.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: But when the customer's request can't be granted under policy, how should I phrase that?

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: Rather than saying 'that's not possible' outright, it's far more effective to explain the policy and offer an alternative at the same time.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: But there are cases with no good alternative. What do we do then?

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: In that case, it's better to inform them in advance that you'll escalate to a supervisor. Situations often worsen when staff try to handle everything alone to the end.

lines.speaker: 직원
lines.en: Not responding emotionally seems to be the hardest part. I catch myself speaking defensively without meaning to.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: That improves with practice. If we do a few more role-plays like today, it'll get much easier in real situations.

shopping-c1y-counterfeit.title: A casual chat about counterfeit goods and IP law

lines.speaker: 태윤
lines.en: My friend came back from a trip abroad with a fake bag. She knew it was fake when she bought it, but is bringing that into the country even okay?

lines.speaker: 혜린
lines.en: Customs usually lets it slide when it's a small amount for personal use, but if it's meant for resale, that's a completely different story.

lines.speaker: 태윤
lines.en: What happens if it's for resale?

lines.speaker: 혜린
lines.en: It can become subject to criminal punishment for trademark infringement. Fines, of course, and it could even go to trial.

lines.speaker: 태윤
lines.en: That's more serious than I thought. But nowadays fakes are so sophisticated that they're almost impossible to tell apart by eye.

lines.speaker: 혜린
lines.en: Right, that's why brands are introducing things like authentication apps or serial number lookups.

lines.speaker: 태윤
lines.en: Still, from a consumer's perspective, isn't the temptation there because you can get something similar for cheap?

lines.speaker: 혜린
lines.en: I get that impulse, but ultimately that kind of consumption eats away at the original brand's design investment and quality control, so isn't it a loss in the long run?

shopping-c2y-brickmortar.title: An op-ed-style talk on the decline of brick-and-mortar retail

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Today we'll be discussing an article on the continually rising vacancy rates in downtown commercial districts with two experts.

lines.speaker: 평론가A
lines.en: The convenience of online shopping is undeniable, but I find it hard to agree with the view that the decline of physical stores is simply a result of technological progress.

lines.speaker: 평론가B
lines.en: I see it a bit differently. As delivery infrastructure and payment systems have advanced, the very advantage of immediacy that physical stores offered has largely become meaningless.

lines.speaker: 평론가A
lines.en: But shouldn't we also examine local governments' stances on rent policy and district management? There's even the paradoxical phenomenon of rents rising as vacancies increase.

lines.speaker: 평론가B
lines.en: I agree with that point too. But fundamentally, I think the bigger issue is that stores haven't managed to redefine the experiential value consumers get from visiting.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: When you say experiential value, what specifically do you mean?

lines.speaker: 평론가B
lines.en: It means the space needs to shift from simply displaying and selling goods to letting customers experience the brand's worldview firsthand.

lines.speaker: 평론가A
lines.en: That has some merit, but ultimately such experiential stores are only possible with large corporate capital, aren't they? How are small merchants supposed to survive?

lines.speaker: 평론가B
lines.en: That part would need to be backed by cooperation at the district level or public support policy. I don't think it's a problem individual merchants can bear alone.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So the survival of brick-and-mortar districts requires not just adapting to technology, but policy and spatial planning working in tandem as well.

shopping-c2y-luxuryresale.title: A journalistic segment on the luxury resale market

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: The luxury resale market has been posting double-digit growth every year. How do you diagnose this phenomenon?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: The long-standing formula of the luxury industry that scarcity equals value has, ironically, created the very structure that fuels the resale market.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: From the brand's perspective, they probably aren't entirely thrilled that their own products are being resold at a markup.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Right. That's why brands have recently pivoted toward directly partnering with resale platforms or launching their own authentication services.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Could we call this a strategy of pulling an otherwise uncontrollable market into the formal system?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: That's a precise observation. At the same time, there's also the benefit of gaining consumer data through resale transactions that would be hard to capture through new-product sales alone.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: From the consumer side, the rise in resale purchasing doesn't seem to be purely about price. What's your view?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: The collector's desire to own discontinued limited editions or rare colorways accounts for a considerable share as well. There's also a growing tendency to approach it as an investment asset.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: The phrase 'investment asset' is interesting. Do you think that kind of return is actually sustainable?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: I think it's only sustainable in a limited sense. Except for a tiny number of rare items, there's a significant risk that value will crash sharply according to trend cycles.

shopping-c2y-greenwashing.title: Debate on greenwashing in retail marketing

lines.speaker: 사회자
lines.en: We've reached an era where the label 'eco-friendly' appears on nearly every product's packaging. Does this reflect real change, or is it just marketing?

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: Frankly, a substantial portion leans toward the latter. There are plenty of cases where a product is branded an 'eco-friendly line' with recycled content barely over five percent.

lines.speaker: 업계관계자
lines.en: I think that's generalizing from a somewhat extreme case. It's just confusion arising from an early-stage market where standards haven't yet been clearly established.

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: Using the absence of standards as an excuse seems inadequate when there have already been repeated claims that consumers are being misled. Isn't it already too late to leave this to self-regulation?

lines.speaker: 업계관계자
lines.en: Our industry is also making efforts to build trust on its own, such as introducing certification marks. Blanket regulation would be difficult given how much variation there is across industries.

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: Isn't the very fact that variation is large across industries the reason a unified legal standard is needed? Self-regulation offers no way to stop free-riding companies.

lines.speaker: 사회자
lines.en: So from the consumer's standpoint, what should they use as a basis for judgment right now?

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: First, check whether there's a mark from a third-party certification body, and it's safer to be suspicious of products with vague wording but no actual figures.

lines.speaker: 업계관계자
lines.en: I agree with that advice too. Ultimately, providing trustworthy information is also tied to the long-term interest of the entire industry.

shopping-c2y-personaldata.title: A panel on personal data use in personalized retail

lines.speaker: 사회자
lines.en: There's a sharp divide between the claim that personalized recommendation services enhance consumer convenience, and the criticism that they amount to surveillance.

lines.speaker: 패널A
lines.en: I don't think we need to reject personalization technology itself. The problem lies in how the consent process becomes a mere formality during data collection.

lines.speaker: 패널B
lines.en: I'd like to raise a more fundamental issue. Isn't the structure such that consent itself can't function as a genuine choice? If you refuse, you're blocked from using the service at all.

lines.speaker: 패널A
lines.en: That point is valid too, but if we ban personalized services outright, we can't ignore the side effect of significantly reducing consumer benefit.

lines.speaker: 패널B
lines.en: Isn't the very framework of weighing benefit against privacy already skewed toward corporate logic? Services can function perfectly well with minimal information.

lines.speaker: 패널A
lines.en: In theory, yes, but there's data showing that when recommendation accuracy drops, consumer complaints rise as well. Finding the balance point is what matters.

lines.speaker: 사회자
lines.en: Then what do you see as the most urgent action regulators should take?

lines.speaker: 패널B
lines.en: First, consent screens should be broken down so users can choose item by item, and it should be mandated that core services remain usable even when a user declines.

lines.speaker: 패널A
lines.en: I agree with that direction too. However, we should also consider a grace period so companies aren't left to shoulder the transition cost unilaterally.

shopping-c2y-labormarket.title: A commentary on retail automation and labor displacement

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: As unmanned stores rapidly spread, concerns are growing that retail workers' jobs are disappearing.

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: Historically, automation has always replaced certain job categories. What's different this time is the unprecedented speed at which it's happening.

lines.speaker: 노동단체대표
lines.en: It's not just about speed. The core issue is that displaced workers aren't even given time to retrain and move into new jobs.

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: I agree with that point too. But shouldn't we also consider that, from the company's perspective, automation is an unavoidable survival strategy amid rising labor cost pressures?

lines.speaker: 노동단체대표
lines.en: The phrase 'survival strategy' can't justify shifting the cost onto workers. It's a structure where the company reaps the benefit and the worker bears the burden.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Then is there a middle ground both of you could agree on?

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: I think it's realistic to consider mandating that a portion of the cost savings from automation be allocated to a retraining fund.

lines.speaker: 노동단체대표
lines.en: That alone falls short, but it could be a starting point. At the very least, workers shouldn't be completely excluded from the transition process.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So the point is that the pace of technology adoption and the pace of building a social safety net need to be discussed together.

shopping-c2y-thirdplace.title: Analyzing retail spaces as a cultural 'third place'

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: Recently there's a clear trend of stores investing more effort in the spatial experience itself than in selling products. You could call it a 'third place' strategy.

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: I agree. But when you consider that the concept originally referred to spaces for communal interaction, it seems somewhat paradoxical to graft it onto commercial spaces.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: It is paradoxical, but given that consumers actually feel that emotional bond and return, it seems strategically effective.

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: The problem is that the bond isn't genuine community feeling but an emotion designed by the brand. Ultimately, consumers can only belong to that space through consumption.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: That's a fair point. Even so, given the reality that traditional third places like libraries or parks are shrinking, isn't a commercial alternative like this still necessary?

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: It can serve as an alternative, but I don't think it can be a replacement. In the end, that space isn't open to people without purchasing power.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: That's a fair point. From the angle of accessibility inequality, the limits of the commercial third place become clear.

lines.speaker: 건축가
lines.en: That's why I believe, at the urban planning level, public and commercial spaces need to be designed in a way that complements each other.

lines.speaker: 평론가
lines.en: So the task going forward is to acknowledge the role of commercial space while balancing it so that public value isn't excluded.

shopping-c2y-subscription.title: A critique of subscription-based retail models

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: The subscription consumption model has spread into nearly every category, but whether it's truly beneficial for consumers deserves scrutiny.

lines.speaker: 업계전문가
lines.en: In terms of convenience, there are clear benefits. It reduces the cognitive burden of making a purchase decision every time.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: But doesn't that convenience end up letting unnecessary spending slide? Given the nature of automatic billing, quite a lot of consumers miss the point at which they should cancel.

lines.speaker: 업계전문가
lines.en: It's true that some services design a deliberately complicated cancellation process. But I'd be cautious about generalizing that across the whole industry.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: Then would you agree with legally mandating that the cancellation process be made as simple as the sign-up process?

lines.speaker: 업계전문가
lines.en: There's no reason to oppose that direction itself. In fact, I think increasing transparency would help industry credibility in the long run too.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: From the consumer's side, what habits are needed to use subscription services wisely?

lines.speaker: 업계전문가
lines.en: Regularly reviewing your usage history and decisively cutting subscriptions with low actual use frequency is the most basic habit.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: So the conclusion is that consumers themselves need to find the balance between convenience and ongoing management.

shopping-c2y-secondhandstigma.title: Cultural commentary on the changing perception of secondhand goods

lines.speaker: 사회학자
lines.en: Just a decade ago, secondhand trading was viewed almost as a symbol of poverty, but now it's accepted as discerning consumption instead.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: What factors do you see behind that shift in perception?

lines.speaker: 사회학자
lines.en: For one, awareness of environmental issues has clearly risen across the generation as a whole, and at the same time, owning rare vintage items has itself become a form of taste expression.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: That phrase 'taste expression' is interesting. In the past, owning something new was itself proof of taste.

lines.speaker: 사회학자
lines.en: Exactly. But in an era of mass production, new products became something anyone could have, whereas rare or discontinued secondhand items became the means of differentiation instead.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Even so, there must still be a substantial group of consumers who feel resistance around hygiene or quality.

lines.speaker: 사회학자
lines.en: Of course. But it's also true that as platforms with professional cleaning and inspection services have grown, that psychological barrier has been considerably lowered as well.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So could we say that the growth of the secondhand market goes beyond simple frugality and is reshaping consumer culture itself?

lines.speaker: 사회학자
lines.en: That's right. I think it's a representative example showing the shift in the meaning of ownership from 'something new' to 'something with a story.'

shopping-c2y-hyperconsumerism.title: A literary-style monologue reflecting on hyperconsumerism

lines.speaker: 화자
lines.en: Do you know that standing under a shopping mall's lighting, your very sense of time disappears? A space designed without a single window turns out not to be an accident.

lines.speaker: 청자
lines.en: I've never thought about it quite that way, but hearing you put it like that, it does feel like something deliberately engineered.

lines.speaker: 화자
lines.en: I used to work at a department store, and on slow sales days, the first thing we'd change was the scent and the music. Tuning the customer's senses was where the sales strategy began.

lines.speaker: 청자
lines.en: Consumers believe they're choosing things of their own free will, but in reality they might just be moving within an already engineered path.

lines.speaker: 화자
lines.en: That's exactly it. Even the layout forcing you to switch escalators floor by floor is, in the end, designed to make you circle the store one more time.

lines.speaker: 청자
lines.en: Knowing all that, I'd think it would make you cynical about consumption itself. Do you still buy things now?

lines.speaker: 화자
lines.en: Of course. But I don't reach for things impulsively the way I used to. Every time I buy something, I ask myself whether it's really my own choice, or an illusion created by that lighting and music.

lines.speaker: 청자
lines.en: It sounds like that single question alone could change consumption habits quite a lot.

lines.speaker: 화자
lines.en: At the very least, my regrets have dropped considerably. In the end, consumption seems to come down to how closely you examine yourself.

shopping-c1z-warehouse.title: A labor journalist investigates warehouse conditions

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Among the night-shift warehouse workers, has anyone here gotten a warning for not hitting the quota?

lines.speaker: 노동자
lines.en: Me. We have to process a few hundred orders a day, and we're so pressed for time we can barely go to the bathroom freely.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Who sets that quota? Does it come down unilaterally from headquarters?

lines.speaker: 노동자
lines.en: I heard an algorithm sets it. It doesn't account for human condition at all — it just keeps raising the average.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Has the union ever demanded improvements from the company over this?

lines.speaker: 노동자
lines.en: A few times, but we've been turned down repeatedly, with the company citing delivery delay concerns.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Consumers probably don't realize next-day delivery is maintained at this kind of cost.

lines.speaker: 노동자
lines.en: Right, from where we stand, it feels like a structure where people get ground down behind the convenience of a single click.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Would it be okay if I ran this anonymously in the article? I'll handle it carefully.

lines.speaker: 노동자
lines.en: Yes, please do. I hope our voices get out there, even a little.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: This washing machine is exactly three years old and the motor's already gone. Repair costs half of a new one.

lines.speaker: 은비
lines.en: Have you heard that some are designed that way on purpose? Parts engineered to fail after a certain point.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: I used to think it couldn't be that deliberate, but after going through this myself, it really does seem suspicious.

lines.speaker: 은비
lines.en: There was even a case that went to lawsuit where a printer maker had a chip stop working after a set number of prints.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: So what can a consumer even do? It ends up being buy new again, doesn't it.

lines.speaker: 은비
lines.en: Apparently more countries are passing right-to-repair laws. They force companies to make parts and manuals available to consumers.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: With that, someone like me could've gotten it fixed much cheaper at a local repair shop.

lines.speaker: 은비
lines.en: Right. And if replacing parts gets easier, the amount of discarded appliances would drop sharply too.

lines.speaker: 지훈
lines.en: For now I'll get this repaired, and next time I'll look for brands with a transparent repair track record.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: The urge to shop when stressed — is there actual evidence behind that psychologically?

lines.speaker: 심리학자
lines.en: Yes, from a brain-science perspective, the moment of choosing and paying for something releases dopamine, giving a temporary sense of satisfaction.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So shopping actually does help relieve stress, then?

lines.speaker: 심리학자
lines.en: In the short term, yes. The problem is that the effect fades quickly, leading people to repeat the purchase to refill it.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So if it becomes a habit, it leads to impulse buying.

lines.speaker: 심리학자
lines.en: Right. There's even research showing self-control drops sharply in front of the payment button, especially when emotions are unstable.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So how can someone break out of this pattern?

lines.speaker: 심리학자
lines.en: Just leaving it in the cart and revisiting it 24 hours later is said to reduce impulsive spending quite a bit.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So in the end, it's about practicing to separate emotion from spending.

lines.speaker: 심리학자
lines.en: Exactly. There's no need to demonize spending itself, but it's important not to use it as a substitute for emotion.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: On our actor's side, we'd like to limit the contract term to one year.

lines.speaker: 브랜드담당자
lines.en: We think we need at least two years, considering the shoot and campaign preparation time.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: Then I think we'd need to revise the penalty clause. As it stands, only our side is disadvantaged in early termination.

lines.speaker: 브랜드담당자
lines.en: That's a fair point. We'll look into adjusting it so both sides have the same terms.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: Also, the competitor-exclusion clause is far too broad. Blocking the entire cosmetics category makes almost any other work impossible.

lines.speaker: 브랜드담당자
lines.en: We could narrow it to color cosmetics. We can leave skincare open.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: Good. I'd also like to confirm the scope of image rights — will you keep using the images after the contract ends?

lines.speaker: 브랜드담당자
lines.en: We'll specify that online posts stay up only for six months after the contract ends, and everything comes down after that.

lines.speaker: 매니저
lines.en: That should be something we can agree to. We'll review the revised draft and get back to you.

shopping-c1z-childads.title: Debating targeted ads aimed at children

lines.speaker: 학부모
lines.en: I was startled when toy ads kept popping up while my kid was watching YouTube. It's like it knew exactly what she'd like.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: It's targeted advertising based on analyzing kids' viewing patterns, but the problem is children often can't tell it's an ad.

lines.speaker: 학부모
lines.en: My child can't distinguish content from ads either, and just begs for everything.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: That's why some countries have made laws banning targeted advertising on children's content entirely.

lines.speaker: 학부모
lines.en: Then platforms would push back hard since it cuts into their revenue.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Right, the industry sometimes argues that targeted ads actually provide more relevant information than random ones.

lines.speaker: 학부모
lines.en: Still, isn't collecting children's data to drive consumption a different issue altogether?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Exactly. Where to draw the line between protection and commercial interest will likely keep being debated.

shopping-c1z-graymarket.title: A customs official explains a gray-market crackdown

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: I heard you've stepped up crackdowns on parallel imports recently. Was there a specific trigger?

lines.speaker: 관세공무원
lines.en: There's been a sharp rise in counterfeit goods getting mixed in among products entering through unofficial channels.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Parallel importing itself isn't illegal, though. How should consumers tell that apart from counterfeits?

lines.speaker: 관세공무원
lines.en: Correct, it's legal as long as it goes through proper procedures. The problem is smuggled volume that bypasses those procedures.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So if the price is unusually cheap compared to the market, that's worth being suspicious of.

lines.speaker: 관세공무원
lines.en: Yes, if the seller dodges a request for an authenticity certificate or import declaration, chances are it's a problematic item.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: How does this kind of crackdown affect authentic brand sales?

lines.speaker: 관세공무원
lines.en: In the short term, prices may rise as parallel-import volume drops, but in the long term it helps restore consumer trust.

lines.speaker: 설계사
lines.en: This mall's vacancy rate has passed 40%. A simple remodel doesn't seem like it'll be enough.

lines.speaker: 시청담당자
lines.en: So you're suggesting converting it to a completely different use?

lines.speaker: 설계사
lines.en: Yes, keeping the lower floors commercial and converting the upper floors to residential or office space — that's the current trend in mixed-use redevelopment.

lines.speaker: 시청담당자
lines.en: Residents might push back against losing the mall — it also served as a kind of community space for the area.

lines.speaker: 설계사
lines.en: That's why I'd like to propose keeping the central plaza or community center as is, and arranging residential space around it.

lines.speaker: 시청담당자
lines.en: What happens to the existing merchants then? Can they be given a chance to move back in?

lines.speaker: 설계사
lines.en: We can provide temporary storefronts during construction and include priority re-entry rights in the contract for after completion.

lines.speaker: 시청담당자
lines.en: What about funding? A project of this scale probably can't rely on private investment alone.

lines.speaker: 설계사
lines.en: A public-private joint development approach would let us share the initial burden. I'll bring a draft funding structure to the next meeting.

lines.speaker: 찬성측
lines.en: Right now, even swapping a single battery requires going to the manufacturer's service center, and it's absurdly expensive.

lines.speaker: 반대측
lines.en: But if a non-expert tries to open it up carelessly and an accident happens, who's responsible for that?

lines.speaker: 찬성측
lines.en: That can be managed sufficiently through safety guidelines and a certified-repair-shop system.

lines.speaker: 반대측
lines.en: From the manufacturer's standpoint, there's also a risk of design technology leaking out — that's their competitive edge.

lines.speaker: 찬성측
lines.en: By that logic, consumers are forever locked into dependence on manufacturers. That's the current reality of the appliance market.

lines.speaker: 반대측
lines.en: There's also the warranty issue. If a defect arises in a product repaired externally, whose responsibility does that become?

lines.speaker: 찬성측
lines.en: That's resolved by requiring genuine parts, as in the European model. Several countries already do this.

lines.speaker: 반대측
lines.en: In the end, the core question is where to strike the balance between consumer benefit and corporate intellectual property rights.

shopping-c1z-trendhistory.title: A fashion historian traces a trend's cultural roots

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Those wide-leg pants trending again — I hear they're not actually new, is that right?

lines.speaker: 역사학자
lines.en: Right, the silhouette started with 1970s working-class workwear. It was cut generously for ease of movement.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: How did it end up crossing over into high fashion?

lines.speaker: 역사학자
lines.en: It began in the 80s when designers took that shape and elevated it purely through fabric, putting it on the runway.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So is the current trend a straight revival of that, or a completely different context?

lines.speaker: 역사학자
lines.en: The shape is the same, but the context differs. Now it's being revived within a trend that values comfort and sustainability.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: Interesting. So trends keep cycling, but they get summoned back for different reasons each time.

lines.speaker: 역사학자
lines.en: Exactly. Tracing the trend of a single garment lets you read what people in that era valued alongside it.

shopping-c2z-tariffs.title: An economist explains how tariffs affect prices

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: The government just raised tariffs on imported appliances — what changes from the consumer's perspective?

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: On the surface, importers pay the tariff, but that cost ultimately gets passed through several stages into the consumer price.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: But wouldn't domestic manufacturers actually benefit, since the competing products get more expensive?

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: In the short term, yes. But with reduced competition, domestic firms also lose the incentive to keep prices low.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So you're saying domestic product prices could quietly creep up too.

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: Right. There have actually been several observed cases where domestic and foreign product prices rose together after tariffs were imposed.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So who is this tariff policy ultimately meant to protect?

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: Nominally it's to protect domestic industry, but structurally a significant portion of that cost ends up falling on consumers.

lines.speaker: 진행자
lines.en: So as a consumer, what should we watch for when these policy changes happen?

lines.speaker: 경제학자
lines.en: Some companies stock up on inventory right before a tariff takes effect, so it helps to watch the gap between the announcement and the actual price increase.

shopping-c2z-influencerlaw.title: A lawyer explains disclosure law for sponsored content

lines.speaker: 인플루언서
lines.en: Do I really have to disclose it's a sponsored product? It seems like I could just say it's my personal taste.

lines.speaker: 변호사
lines.en: No, if you're being compensated to feature it, you must clearly indicate it's an ad. Otherwise you could be subject to legal sanctions.

lines.speaker: 인플루언서
lines.en: Is a small note tucked into a comment not enough?

lines.speaker: 변호사
lines.en: It's not enough. It needs to be stated on screen or in captions so viewers can recognize it the moment they watch, for it to count.

lines.speaker: 인플루언서
lines.en: If I don't comply with this, what kind of trouble could I actually run into?

lines.speaker: 변호사
lines.en: You could face a fine, and if it's repeated, it could even lead to sanctions against the channel itself.

lines.speaker: 인플루언서
lines.en: Then there's no issue at all with introducing a product I bought myself and genuinely like, as opposed to a sponsorship?

lines.speaker: 변호사
lines.en: Right, that's purely a personal opinion, so there's no disclosure obligation. But if it later comes out that it was sponsored, the trust issue becomes even bigger.

lines.speaker: 인플루언서
lines.en: Understood. Going forward, I'll make sure to put a clear disclosure on screen for every sponsored item.

shopping-c2z-loyaltydata.title: マイルプログラムの改悪

lines.speaker: 회의자A
lines.en: Membership app sign-ups have grown, but it seems consumers don't really know what we're doing with that data.

lines.speaker: 회의자B
lines.en: We collect it with consent, so there's no procedural problem. It's all stated in the terms.

lines.speaker: 회의자A
lines.en: Formally, sure. But most people just tap agree without reading that long document. Can we really call that meaningful consent?

lines.speaker: 회의자B
lines.en: So you're suggesting we present a summary version up front, then?

lines.speaker: 회의자A
lines.en: Yes, I think we should at least show, right on the first screen, what data is used for what, in essence.

lines.speaker: 회의자B
lines.en: But being that transparent could actually lower sign-up rates. A significant portion of our current revenue comes from these data-driven recommendations.

lines.speaker: 회의자A
lines.en: If we're eroding trust for short-term revenue, we could take an even bigger hit later when regulations get tighter.

lines.speaker: 회의자B
lines.en: That's a fair point. Should we pilot the summary disclosure with new sign-ups first, then?

lines.speaker: 회의자A
lines.en: Yes, watching the response and then rolling it out gradually to existing members would reduce risk and be better overall.

shopping-c2z-scentbranding.title: A retail consultant explains scent marketing

lines.speaker: 대표
lines.en: Does subtly scenting the store really change sales? I wonder if that's a bit exaggerated.

lines.speaker: 컨설턴트
lines.en: There are actual experimental results showing that stores playing a specific scent see meaningfully higher dwell time and purchase conversion.

lines.speaker: 대표
lines.en: Then it's not just any scent — we'd need to pick one that fits the brand.

lines.speaker: 컨설턴트
lines.en: Right. Many places use a signature scent developed to match the brand tone. Scent also plays a role in imprinting brand memory.

lines.speaker: 대표
lines.en: But couldn't consumers feel subtly manipulated by this kind of scent marketing?

lines.speaker: 컨설턴트
lines.en: That criticism keeps coming up in the debate. But many also view it as just one more element shaping store atmosphere, like lighting or music.

lines.speaker: 대표
lines.en: Still, I think we need to consider customers who are sensitive to scent or have allergies.

lines.speaker: 컨설턴트
lines.en: Exactly. That's why more stores are now setting up separate scent-free zones or keeping the concentration very low.

lines.speaker: 대표
lines.en: For now, I'll pilot a scent that fits our store's tone at one location and see how customers respond.

shopping-c2z-flagshipexperience.title: Critics debate flagship stores as brand theater

lines.speaker: 비평가A
lines.en: Flagship stores these days feel less like places to sell things and more like experiential exhibition halls. Barely anyone even buys there anymore.

lines.speaker: 비평가B
lines.en: That's the point, though. In an era where everyone already buys online, offline stores have shifted from selling to being a stage for imprinting brand impressions.

lines.speaker: 비평가A
lines.en: But pouring in that much rent and interior investment ultimately just gets you an emotional image. How do you even measure the return on that?

lines.speaker: 비평가B
lines.en: It looks like a loss if you only count direct sales, but a fair assessment has to include the exposure effect from photos taken there spreading on social media.

lines.speaker: 비평가A
lines.en: Still, what real benefit does that give the consumer? Isn't it ultimately just good for the brand?

lines.speaker: 비평가B
lines.en: From the consumer's side, even without buying anything, they're consuming the space itself as a product — an experience. People these days count that as value too.

lines.speaker: 비평가A
lines.en: Hearing that, it sounds like the very concept of consumption has shifted from goods to experience.

lines.speaker: 비평가B
lines.en: Exactly. And the flagship store is the stage that shows off that shift first, and most spectacularly.

lines.speaker: 비평가A
lines.en: Then maybe stores should now be evaluated not by sales figures, but by how memorable an experience they delivered.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: Across the retail industry these days, a flood of reissued products invoking 90s nostalgia is pouring out.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: It looks like a simple retro trend, but underneath it lies a sophisticated consumer psychology strategy.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: Nostalgia links a person to the sense of security from that era. That's why even a single familiar logo or package can loosen someone's wallet.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: It's especially interesting that even younger generations who never lived through that era are joining this trend.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: For them it isn't nostalgia at all, but curiosity about their parents' generation's culture and an aesthetic reinterpretation spread online.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: For companies, it's also attractive that they can recycle already-proven brand recognition without the risk of developing something new.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: However, concerns are also emerging that if this strategy repeats too often, genuine innovation gets pushed to the back burner.

lines.speaker: 해설자
lines.en: In the end, the industry itself needs to consider whether an industry built on selling the past is eating into its own capacity to prepare for the future.

shopping-c2z-authenticationmarket.title: Debating third-party authentication services for resale

lines.speaker: 판매자
lines.en: Going through an authentication service adds a fee, but without it, the transaction just doesn't happen at all anymore.

lines.speaker: 구매자
lines.en: That's because there have been so many counterfeit cases. Listings without an authentication certificate just aren't trustworthy from the start.

lines.speaker: 판매자
lines.en: But it's also a problem that authentication standards differ between companies. Something certified authentic at one place sometimes gets flagged for re-review at another.

lines.speaker: 구매자
lines.en: So in the end, consumers also have to newly judge which authentication company to trust.

lines.speaker: 판매자
lines.en: Right. Since there's no industry-wide standard, the authentication service itself ends up creating a new layer of uncertainty.

lines.speaker: 구매자
lines.en: Still, isn't it better than having none at all? It at least serves as a minimum safeguard.

lines.speaker: 판매자
lines.en: Of course. But I think as this market grows, there also needs to be a parallel push to standardize authentication criteria.

lines.speaker: 구매자
lines.en: What about brands themselves participating directly in authentication? Wouldn't that make the standards clearer?

lines.speaker: 판매자
lines.en: That would be ideal, but for brands it effectively means officially endorsing the resale market itself, so many are reluctant.

shopping-c2z-childlabor.title: An NGO researcher discusses supply-chain audits

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: In the report you just released, you mentioned indications of child labor at subcontracted factories for several major brands.

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: Yes, the paperwork made it look like adult verification had been done, but on-site investigation confirmed a number of workers who clearly appeared much younger.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Hasn't the brand claimed it conducts regular inspections through a third-party auditing body?

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: Right, but the audit itself was scheduled with advance notice, giving the factory plenty of time to prepare.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So you're saying audits under the current method are essentially just a formality.

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: I can't say it's true across the board, but cases like this show clear limits to advance-notice audits.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: So what changes would be needed to make audits actually effective?

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: Unannounced spot checks need to be the standard, and there absolutely must be a procedure allowing anonymous, direct interviews with workers.

lines.speaker: 기자
lines.en: Is there anything consumers can actually do about this issue?

lines.speaker: 연구원
lines.en: Rather than stopping purchases outright, it's more realistic to demand that brands disclose their audit methods and to prioritize products carrying an independent certification mark.

shopping-c2z-airportretail.title: Analyzing why airport duty-free pricing feels irrational

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: People don't seem to realize that duty-free prices are sometimes higher than in-city stores.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: That's right. Only the tariff is removed — airport rent and logistics costs are so high that they get reflected directly into the price.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: So why do consumers assume it's automatically cheap just because it's labeled duty-free?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: The travel situation itself clouds judgment somewhat. People are in a heightened mood and tend not to compare prices carefully.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: On top of that, being pressed for boarding time makes people buy even more impulsively.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Exactly. That's why the store layout is deliberately designed to place perfume and liquor counters right along the path to the gate.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: So are there specific items where consumers actually do come out ahead?

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: For high-tariff items, especially things like alcohol or tobacco where the tariff makes up a large share of the cost, the difference is definitely real.

lines.speaker: 칼럼니스트
lines.en: So it comes down to checking item by item rather than assuming everything is cheap.

lines.speaker: 전문가
lines.en: Yes, just searching the price of items you're interested in before departure can significantly cut down on losses.
